docs.title: nicefigs
docs.text:
Publication-grade, modular matplotlib plotting for geoscience.

nicefigs is a thin, composable layer on top of matplotlib. It gives you a single consistent house style (sans-serif, journal-like), physical figure sizing that keeps fonts consistent across every panel, and a toolbox of geoscience-ready plots: global/regional maps, ternary maps & scatters, image grids, tight colorbars, KDE agreement plots, model-comparison violins, timeseries, and map animations.

docs.title: Design philosophy
docs.text:
One consistent house style. A small, explicit Theme dataclass bundles font sizes, line widths, and colours. Call nicefigs.set_theme("paper") once and every helper — maps, scatter plots, heatmaps, timeseries — renders with matching fonts, tick sizes, and spine weights.

Physical figure sizing. You almost never want to think in inches. You want "a single-column figure" or "half the text width". Because font sizes live in points and figure sizes live in inches, nicefigs.figure / nicefigs.subplots solve the figure size from a named physical target (width="single", width="half", ...) and an aspect ratio. The rendered figure lands at exactly the requested physical size, with fonts at exactly the theme's point sizes — so a multi-panel paper figure looks consistent whether one panel is a map and another is a scatter plot.

Modular, composable helpers. Every plotting function accepts an existing ax (or fig) where it makes sense, so you can drop nicefigs pieces into your own matplotlib layouts — a GridSpec, a plt.subplots grid, an inset axes — rather than being handed a fixed figure you have to fight with. The composite figure example shows a map, a timeseries, and an agreement plot composed into one GridSpec, all sharing one theme and one physical width.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install nicefigs

# with cartopy-backed map projections
pip install "nicefigs[maps]"

# with xarray input helpers
pip install "nicefigs[xarray]"

# both
pip install "nicefigs[all]"

docs.title: A first example
docs.text:
The figure above is built from three independently composable pieces — a map, a timeseries, and an agreement plot — arranged in a GridSpec, all at one consistent physical width. See it fully worked through in the Gallery and Quickstart.

import nicefigs as nf
from nicefigs import data

nf.set_theme("paper")

lon, lat, temp = data.global_points(field="temperature")
fig, ax, m = nf.map(
    lon, lat, temp,
    cmap="RdYlBu_r",
    colorbar_label="air temperature [°C]",
    title="Mean annual air temperature",
)
nf.save(fig, "figures/global_map", formats=("pdf", "png"))

Continue to the Quickstart or browse the full Gallery for every plot family, or jump straight to the API Reference.

docs.title: style
docs.text:
Themes: frozen bundles of font sizes (pt), line widths (pt) and colours.

Because font sizes and figure sizes are both physical units, a figure rendered at a requested physical size (see :mod:nicefigs.figure) keeps its fonts at exactly the theme's sizes.

Example::

import nicefigs as nf

nf.set_theme("paper")            # globally

with nf.style("talk"):           # or temporarily
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()

@classmethod
def from_base(cls, base: float, **overrides: Any) -> Theme:
    """Build a theme whose font sizes scale from one ``base`` size.

    Args:
        base: Body font size (pt).
        **overrides: Field values that replace the derived ones.

    Returns:
        The new theme.
    """
    sizes = dict(
        base=base,
        fs_body=base,
        fs_panel_label=round(base * 1.2, 2),
        fs_title=round(base * 1.08, 2),
        fs_panel_title=round(base * 1.1, 2),
        fs_axis_label=round(base * 1.00, 2),
        fs_tick=round(base * 0.85, 2),
        fs_legend=round(base * 0.92, 2),
        fs_annot=round(base * 0.85, 2),
    )
    sizes.update(overrides)
    return cls(**sizes)

def scaled(self, factor: float) -> Theme:
    """Return a copy with every font size multiplied by ``factor``."""
    return replace(
        self,
        base=self.base * factor,
        fs_body=self.fs_body * factor,
        fs_panel_label=self.fs_panel_label * factor,
        fs_title=self.fs_title * factor,
        fs_panel_title=self.fs_panel_title * factor,
        fs_axis_label=self.fs_axis_label * factor,
        fs_tick=self.fs_tick * factor,
        fs_legend=self.fs_legend * factor,
        fs_annot=self.fs_annot * factor,
    )

def get_theme(theme: str | Theme | None = None) -> Theme:
    """Resolve a theme name, a :class:`Theme`, or ``None`` (the active theme).

    Raises:
        KeyError: ``theme`` is not a key of :data:`THEMES`.
    """
    if theme is None:
        return _active_theme
    if isinstance(theme, Theme):
        return theme
    try:
        return THEMES[theme]
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise KeyError(f"Unknown theme {theme!r}. Available: {sorted(THEMES)}") from exc

def set_theme(theme: str | Theme = "paper") -> Theme:
    """Set the active theme globally and apply its rcParams.

    Args:
        theme: Preset name (a key of :data:`THEMES`) or a :class:`Theme`.

    Returns:
        The resolved theme.
    """
    global _active_theme
    _active_theme = get_theme(theme)
    plt.rcParams.update(_active_theme.rc())
    return _active_theme

@contextlib.contextmanager
def style(theme: str | Theme | None = None, **rc_overrides: Any) -> Iterator[Theme]:
    """Apply a theme within a ``with`` block, restoring the previous one on exit.

    The theme is also the active one (:func:`get_theme`) inside the block.

    Args:
        theme: Preset name, a :class:`Theme`, or ``None`` for the active theme.
        **rc_overrides: Extra ``rcParams``, e.g.
            ``nf.style("paper", **{"axes.grid": True})``.

    Yields:
        The resolved theme.
    """
    global _active_theme
    resolved = get_theme(theme)
    prev = _active_theme
    rc = resolved.rc()
    rc.update(rc_overrides)
    _active_theme = resolved
    try:
        with plt.rc_context(rc):
            yield resolved
    finally:
        _active_theme = prev

fig, axs = nf.subplots(2, 3, width="full", panel_aspect=1.0)

def figure_size(
    width: float | str | None = None,
    height: float | None = None,
    aspect: float | None = None,
    *,
    nrows: int = 1,
    ncols: int = 1,
    panel_aspect: float | None = None,
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Solve a ``(width, height)`` in inches from a flexible spec.

    Args:
        width: Inches, or a name from :data:`WIDTHS` / :data:`CANVASES`.
        height: Inches. Give *either* ``width`` or ``height`` (or both).
        aspect: Whole-figure ``height / width``. Ignored if both dims are given.
        nrows: Panel rows; only used with ``panel_aspect``.
        ncols: Panel columns; only used with ``panel_aspect``.
        panel_aspect: Per-panel ``height / width``. If set, the figure aspect is
            derived so each panel has this shape (``nrows/ncols * panel_aspect``).
            Takes precedence over ``aspect``.

    Returns:
        ``(width, height)`` in inches. With nothing given, a ``"half"``
        wide panel at :data:`DEFAULT_ASPECT`.

    Raises:
        KeyError: ``width`` is an unknown preset name.
    """
    if isinstance(width, str):
        if width in CANVASES and height is None and aspect is None and panel_aspect is None:
            return CANVASES[width]
        if width in CANVASES:
            width = CANVASES[width][0]
        elif width in WIDTHS:
            width = WIDTHS[width]
        else:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown width preset {width!r}. Known: {sorted(WIDTHS) + sorted(CANVASES)}")

    if panel_aspect is not None:
        aspect = (nrows / ncols) * panel_aspect

    if width is not None and height is not None:
        return float(width), float(height)
    if width is not None:
        return float(width), float(width) * (aspect if aspect is not None else DEFAULT_ASPECT)
    if height is not None:
        asp = aspect if aspect is not None else DEFAULT_ASPECT
        return float(height) / asp, float(height)
    return WIDTHS["half"], WIDTHS["half"] * DEFAULT_ASPECT

def figure(
    width: float | str | None = None,
    height: float | None = None,
    aspect: float | None = None,
    *,
    theme: str | Theme | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> Figure:
    """Create an empty figure at a physical size.

    Args:
        width: Inches, or a preset name; see :func:`figure_size`.
        height: Inches.
        aspect: Figure ``height / width``.
        theme: Theme applied while the figure is created; ``None`` uses the
            active theme. Use :func:`nicefigs.set_theme` to keep it afterwards.
        **kwargs: Forwarded to :func:`matplotlib.pyplot.figure`.

    Returns:
        The new figure.
    """
    size = figure_size(width, height, aspect)
    th = get_theme(theme)
    with style(th):
        fig = plt.figure(figsize=size, dpi=th.dpi, **kwargs)
    return fig

def subplots(
    nrows: int = 1,
    ncols: int = 1,
    *,
    width: float | str | None = None,
    height: float | None = None,
    aspect: float | None = None,
    panel_aspect: float | None = None,
    theme: str | Theme | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> tuple[Figure, Any]:
    """:func:`matplotlib.pyplot.subplots` at a physical size, with a theme applied.

    Args:
        nrows: Panel rows.
        ncols: Panel columns.
        width: Inches, or a preset name; see :func:`figure_size`.
        height: Inches.
        aspect: Whole-figure ``height / width``.
        panel_aspect: Per-panel ``height / width``; overrides ``aspect``.
        theme: Theme applied while the figure is created; ``None`` uses the
            active theme.
        **kwargs: Forwarded to :func:`matplotlib.pyplot.subplots`;
            ``wspace``, ``hspace``, ``width_ratios`` and ``height_ratios`` are
            routed into ``gridspec_kw``.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, axes)`` as returned by :func:`matplotlib.pyplot.subplots`: one
        Axes, or an array of them.
    """
    size = figure_size(width, height, aspect, nrows=nrows, ncols=ncols, panel_aspect=panel_aspect)
    gridspec_kw = dict(kwargs.pop("gridspec_kw", None) or {})
    for k in ("wspace", "hspace", "width_ratios", "height_ratios"):
        if k in kwargs:
            gridspec_kw[k] = kwargs.pop(k)
    if gridspec_kw:
        kwargs["gridspec_kw"] = gridspec_kw
    th = get_theme(theme)
    with style(th):
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=size, dpi=th.dpi, **kwargs)
    return fig, axes

def save(
    fig: Figure,
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    formats: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
    dpi: int | None = None,
    transparent: bool = False,
    close: bool = False,
) -> list[Path]:
    """Save ``fig`` with a tight bounding box, creating parent directories.

    Args:
        fig: The figure.
        path: Output file. With ``formats``, its suffix is replaced by each format.
        formats: Extensions to write, e.g. ``("pdf", "png")``.
        dpi: Raster resolution; defaults to the active theme's ``savedpi``.
        transparent: Transparent background.
        close: Close the figure after saving.

    Returns:
        The written paths, one per format, in the order of ``formats``.

    Example::

        nf.save(fig, "figures/fig01", formats=("pdf", "png"))
    """
    p = Path(path)
    th = get_theme()
    dpi = dpi or th.savedpi
    paths = []
    if formats is None:
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        fig.savefig(p, dpi=dpi, bbox_inches="tight", pad_inches=0.02, transparent=transparent)
        paths.append(p)
    else:
        stem = p.with_suffix("")
        stem.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for ext in formats:
            out = stem.with_suffix(f".{ext.lstrip('.')}")
            fig.savefig(out, dpi=dpi, bbox_inches="tight", pad_inches=0.02, transparent=transparent)
            paths.append(out)
    if close:
        plt.close(fig)
    return paths

def check_text_overlaps(
    fig: Figure,
    *,
    ignore_ticks: bool = False,
    clipped: bool = True,
    tolerance: float = 1.0,
) -> list[TextIssue]:
    """Find text that overlaps other text or runs off the figure, as the renderer draws it.

    Every visible, non-empty text artist is measured by its rendered bounding box (titles, axis and
    tick labels, colorbar labels, legend entries, annotations). Boxes are axis-aligned, so rotated
    labels count by their enclosing rectangle.

    Args:
        fig: The figure; it is drawn once to lay out its text.
        ignore_ticks: Leave tick labels out entirely.
        clipped: Also report text whose box leaves the figure canvas. Saving with
            ``bbox_inches="tight"`` (as :func:`save` does) grows the canvas instead of cutting.
        tolerance: Pixels a box may cross the figure edge or another box before it counts.

    Returns:
        One :class:`TextIssue` per overlapping pair and per clipped text; empty when the layout is
        clean.
    """
    fig.canvas.draw()
    renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
    ticks, hidden = _tick_labels(fig)
    skip = ticks if ignore_ticks else hidden
    boxes = []
    for t in fig.findobj(Text):
        if id(t) in skip or not t.get_visible() or not t.get_text().strip():
            continue
        boxes.append((t.get_text(), t.get_window_extent(renderer).padded(-tolerance / 2)))
    issues = []
    for i, (s1, b1) in enumerate(boxes):
        for s2, b2 in boxes[i + 1 :]:
            if b1.overlaps(b2):
                issues.append(TextIssue("overlap", (s1, s2)))
    if clipped:
        fb = fig.bbox
        for s, b in boxes:
            if (
                b.x0 < fb.x0 - tolerance
                or b.y0 < fb.y0 - tolerance
                or b.x1 > fb.x1 + tolerance
                or b.y1 > fb.y1 + tolerance
            ):
                issues.append(TextIssue("clipped", (s,)))
    return issues

def panel_label(
    ax: Axes,
    label: str,
    title: str = "",
    *,
    x: float = 0.0,
    y: float = 1.0,
    pad: float | None = None,
    weight: str = "bold",
    parens: bool = False,
    use_ax_title: bool = False,
    dedupe: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Draw a panel label (``a``) and an optional short title above ``ax``.

    The label is bold lowercase without parentheses, set at the theme's
    ``fs_panel_label`` (1.2 times the axis-label size). Its left edge is flush
    with the axes' left edge and its baseline sits ``pad`` points above the top
    edge. The title follows on the same baseline in normal weight at
    ``fs_panel_title``, half a label-height after the label. On cartopy map
    axes both are anchored to the axes' grid cell, so labels line up down the
    figure.

    Note:
        The title is drawn as passed: label ``"a"`` with title
        ``"a priori flux"`` renders ``a  a priori flux``. Pass ``dedupe=True``
        to strip a title prefix equal to the label.

    Args:
        ax: Target axes.
        label: Label text, e.g. ``"a"``.
        title: Short title drawn after the label.
        x: Anchor x-position in axes fraction (of the grid cell for map axes).
        y: Anchor y-position, same coordinates as ``x``.
        pad: Height of the baseline above the anchor (pt); defaults to half the
            label size.
        weight: Font weight of the label; the title is always normal weight.
        parens: Wrap the label in parentheses, e.g. ``"(a)"``.
        use_ax_title: When ``title`` is empty, use the axes' own left, centre
            or right title instead and clear it, so it is not drawn twice.
        dedupe: Strip a leading copy of the label (and whitespace) from ``title``.
    """
    from matplotlib.transforms import offset_copy

    th = get_theme()
    text = f"({label})" if parens else label
    if not title and use_ax_title:
        for loc in ("left", "center", "right"):
            title = ax.get_title(loc=loc)
            if title:
                ax.set_title("", loc=loc)
                break
    if title and dedupe:
        title = _dedupe_title(text, label, title)
    pad = 0.5 * th.fs_panel_label if pad is None else pad
    fig = ax.figure
    if _is_geoaxes(ax):
        # The original (pre-aspect) position is the grid cell, not the pillar-boxed map.
        fig.canvas.draw()
        pos = ax.get_position(original=True)
        base, target = fig.transFigure, fig
        tx, ty = pos.x0 + x * pos.width, pos.y1 + (y - 1.0) * pos.height
    else:
        base, target = ax.transAxes, ax
        tx, ty = x, y
    at_label = offset_copy(base, fig=fig, x=0.0, y=pad, units="points")
    mark = target.text(
        tx,
        ty,
        text,
        transform=at_label,
        fontsize=th.fs_panel_label,
        fontweight=weight,
        va="baseline",
        ha="left",
    )
    if title:
        width_pt = mark.get_window_extent(fig.canvas.get_renderer()).width * 72.0 / fig.dpi
        gap_pt = width_pt + 0.5 * th.fs_panel_label
        at_title = offset_copy(base, fig=fig, x=gap_pt, y=pad, units="points")
        target.text(tx, ty, title, transform=at_title, fontsize=th.fs_panel_title, va="baseline", ha="left")

def label_panels(
    axes: Iterable[Axes | None],
    titles: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    *,
    start: int = 0,
    upper: bool = False,
    parens: bool = False,
    x: float = 0.0,
    y: float = 1.0,
    pad: float | None = None,
    skip_none: bool = True,
    use_ax_title: bool = False,
    dedupe: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Label axes ``a, b, c, …`` in reading order with :func:`panel_label`.

    Args:
        axes: Axes, or an array of them (flattened row-major).
        titles: Per-panel short titles, aligned with the flattened ``axes``.
        start: Offset into the alphabet (``0`` is ``a``).
        upper: Use ``A, B, C``.
        parens: Wrap the letter in parentheses.
        x: Anchor x-position in axes fraction.
        y: Anchor y-position in axes fraction.
        pad: Height of the label baseline above the anchor (pt); see :func:`panel_label`.
        skip_none: Skip ``None`` entries (empty grid cells) without using a letter.
        use_ax_title: For panels with no entry in ``titles``, fall back to
            each axes' own ``ax.get_title()`` and clear it — see
            :func:`panel_label`.
        dedupe: Drop a leading duplicate of the letter from the title — see
            :func:`panel_label`.
    """
    flat = (
        list(np.asarray(list(axes), dtype=object).ravel())
        if not isinstance(axes, np.ndarray)
        else list(axes.ravel())
    )
    i = 0
    for k, ax in enumerate(flat):
        if ax is None and skip_none:
            continue
        letter = chr(ord("A" if upper else "a") + start + i)
        title = titles[k] if titles is not None and k < len(titles) else ""
        panel_label(
            ax,
            letter,
            title or "",
            x=x,
            y=y,
            pad=pad,
            parens=parens,
            use_ax_title=use_ax_title,
            dedupe=dedupe,
        )
        i += 1

def row_labels(
    axes: Any,
    labels: Sequence[str],
    *,
    x: float = -0.22,
    rotation: float = 90.0,
    fontsize: float | None = None,
    weight: str = "normal",
    pad: float = 0.0,
) -> None:
    """Label the rows of a panel grid with rotated headers down the left margin.

    Args:
        axes: A ``(nrows, ncols)`` grid (its first column is used), or one axes per row.
        labels: One header per row; empty strings are skipped.
        x: Header x-position in axes fraction.
        rotation: Text rotation (degrees).
        fontsize: Font size (pt); defaults to the theme's ``fs_panel_title``.
        weight: Font weight.
        pad: Vertical shift of the header from the row centre, in axes fraction.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    fs = fontsize if fontsize is not None else th.fs_panel_title
    targets = _cell_axes(axes, "row")
    for ax, lab in zip(targets, labels):
        if ax is None or not lab:
            continue
        if _is_geoaxes(ax):
            fig = ax.figure
            fig.canvas.draw()
            pos = ax.get_position(original=True)
            fig.text(
                pos.x0 + x * pos.width,
                pos.y0 + 0.5 * pos.height,
                lab,
                rotation=rotation,
                ha="center",
                va="center",
                fontsize=fs,
                fontweight=weight,
            )
        else:
            ax.text(
                x,
                0.5 + pad,
                lab,
                transform=ax.transAxes,
                rotation=rotation,
                ha="center",
                va="center",
                fontsize=fs,
                fontweight=weight,
            )

def grid(
    nrows: int,
    ncols: int,
    *,
    width: float | str | None = None,
    height: float | None = None,
    aspect: float | None = None,
    panel_aspect: float | None = None,
    theme: str | Theme | None = None,
    hspace: float = 0.28,
    wspace: float = 0.22,
    width_ratios: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    height_ratios: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    projection: Any = None,
    with_legend_row: bool = False,
    legend_row_height: float = 0.12,
) -> tuple[Figure, np.ndarray] | tuple[Figure, np.ndarray, Axes]:
    """Create a GridSpec panel grid at a physical size.

    Args:
        nrows: Panel rows.
        ncols: Panel columns.
        width: Inches or a preset name; see :func:`nicefigs.figure_size`.
        height: Inches.
        aspect: Whole-figure ``height / width``.
        panel_aspect: Per-panel ``height / width``; overrides ``aspect``.
        theme: Theme applied while the figure is created; ``None`` uses the active theme.
        hspace: Vertical gap between panels (fraction of mean panel height).
        wspace: Horizontal gap between panels (fraction of mean panel width).
        width_ratios: Relative column widths.
        height_ratios: Relative row heights.
        projection: Projection for every panel, e.g. a cartopy CRS.
        with_legend_row: Add a hidden, full-width bottom row for a shared legend.
        legend_row_height: Height ratio of the legend row relative to a panel row.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, axes)`` with ``axes`` a ``(nrows, ncols)`` object array, or
        ``(fig, axes, ax_legend)`` when ``with_legend_row`` is set.
    """
    from matplotlib.gridspec import GridSpec

    size = figure_size(width, height, aspect, nrows=nrows, ncols=ncols, panel_aspect=panel_aspect)
    th = get_theme(theme)

    total_rows = nrows + (1 if with_legend_row else 0)
    hr = list(height_ratios) if height_ratios is not None else [1.0] * nrows
    if with_legend_row:
        hr = hr + [legend_row_height]
    with style(th):
        fig = plt.figure(figsize=size, dpi=th.dpi)
        gs = GridSpec(
            total_rows,
            ncols,
            figure=fig,
            hspace=hspace,
            wspace=wspace,
            width_ratios=width_ratios,
            height_ratios=hr,
        )
        axes = np.empty((nrows, ncols), dtype=object)
        for i in range(nrows):
            for j in range(ncols):
                axes[i, j] = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, j], projection=projection)
        if with_legend_row:
            ax_legend = fig.add_subplot(gs[nrows, :])
            ax_legend.axis("off")
            return fig, axes, ax_legend
    return fig, axes

def reference_line(
    ax: Axes,
    value: float,
    *,
    axis: str = "y",
    label: str = "",
    color: str | None = None,
    linestyle: str = "--",
    linewidth: float = 0.7,
    alpha: float = 0.7,
    fmt: str = "{label}",
    zorder: float = 1,
) -> None:
    """Draw a horizontal (``axis="y"``) or vertical (``axis="x"``) reference line with an optional label.

    Args:
        ax: Target axes.
        value: Position of the line in data coordinates.
        axis: ``"y"`` for a horizontal line at ``y=value``, ``"x"`` for a vertical one.
        label: Text drawn at the line's far end; empty draws none.
        color: Line and label colour; defaults to grey.
        linestyle: Line style.
        linewidth: Line width (pt).
        alpha: Line opacity.
        fmt: Label format with ``{label}`` and ``{value}`` fields, e.g. ``"{label} ({value:.2g})"``.
        zorder: Line drawing order.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    color = color or "#888888"
    (ax.axhline if axis == "y" else ax.axvline)(
        value, color=color, linestyle=linestyle, linewidth=linewidth, alpha=alpha, zorder=zorder
    )
    if label:
        text = fmt.format(label=label, value=value)
        if axis == "y":
            ax.text(
                0.995,
                value,
                f" {text}",
                transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(),
                ha="right",
                va="bottom",
                fontsize=th.fs_annot,
                color=color,
            )
        else:
            ax.text(
                value,
                0.995,
                f" {text}",
                transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform(),
                ha="left",
                va="top",
                rotation=90,
                fontsize=th.fs_annot,
                color=color,
            )

def facet(
    items: Iterable[Any],
    draw: Callable[[Axes, Any, int], object],
    *,
    ncols: int = 3,
    width: float | str = "full",
    panel_aspect: float = 0.8,
    theme: str | Theme | None = None,
    sharex: bool | str = False,
    sharey: bool | str = False,
    hide_unused: bool = True,
    labels: bool = False,
    titles: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    hspace: float = 0.35,
    wspace: float = 0.22,
) -> tuple[Figure, np.ndarray]:
    """Draw small multiples: one panel per item, filled by ``draw(ax, item, i)``.

    Args:
        items: One entry per panel, passed to ``draw``.
        draw: Callback drawing ``item`` (the ``i``-th) into ``ax``.
        ncols: Maximum panel columns; rows follow from ``len(items)``.
        width: Figure width, inches or a preset name.
        panel_aspect: Per-panel ``height / width``.
        theme: Theme applied while the figure is created; ``None`` uses the active theme.
        sharex: Forwarded to :func:`matplotlib.pyplot.subplots`.
        sharey: Forwarded to :func:`matplotlib.pyplot.subplots`.
        hide_unused: Hide the trailing cells without an item.
        labels: Add ``a, b, c`` panel labels.
        titles: Per-panel titles set with :func:`clean_title`.
        hspace: Vertical gap between panels.
        wspace: Horizontal gap between panels.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, axes)`` with ``axes`` the flat array of all cells, unused ones included.
    """
    items = list(items)
    n = len(items)
    ncols = min(ncols, n) if n else ncols
    nrows = int(np.ceil(n / ncols)) if n else 1

    size = figure_size(width, panel_aspect=panel_aspect, nrows=nrows, ncols=ncols)
    th = get_theme(theme)
    with style(th):
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(
            nrows,
            ncols,
            figsize=size,
            dpi=th.dpi,
            squeeze=False,
            sharex=sharex,
            sharey=sharey,
            gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=hspace, wspace=wspace),
        )
    axes_flat = axes.ravel()
    for i, (ax, item) in enumerate(zip(axes_flat, items)):
        draw(ax, item, i)
        if titles is not None and i < len(titles):
            clean_title(ax, titles[i])
    if hide_unused:
        for ax in axes_flat[n:]:
            ax.axis("off")
    if labels:
        label_panels(axes_flat[:n])
    return fig, axes_flat

def cmap_norm(self) -> tuple[mcolors.ListedColormap, mcolors.BoundaryNorm]:
    """``(cmap, norm)`` mapping each class code to its colour, for ``ax.imshow(codes, cmap=cmap, norm=norm)``."""
    codes = self.codes
    cols = [self.colors[c] for c in codes]
    cm = mcolors.ListedColormap(cols)
    bounds = [codes[0] - 0.5] + [0.5 * (a + b) for a, b in zip(codes[:-1], codes[1:])] + [codes[-1] + 0.5]
    norm = mcolors.BoundaryNorm(bounds, cm.N)
    return cm, norm

def to_rgb(self, arr: ArrayLike, *, default: str = "#dddddd") -> np.ndarray:
    """Convert class codes of shape ``(H, W)`` to a float32 RGB image ``(H, W, 3)``.

    Args:
        arr: Class codes.
        default: Colour of codes not in the palette.
    """
    arr = np.asarray(arr)
    out = np.tile(np.asarray(mcolors.to_rgb(default), dtype=np.float32), (*arr.shape, 1))
    for code, hexcol in self.colors.items():
        m = arr == code
        if m.any():
            out[m] = mcolors.to_rgb(hexcol)
    return out

def legend_handles(self, codes: list[int] | None = None) -> list[Patch]:
    """Legend patches, one per code in ``codes`` (default: all) that the palette defines."""
    codes = codes if codes is not None else self.codes
    return [
        Patch(facecolor=self.colors[c], edgecolor="none", label=self.names.get(c, str(c)))
        for c in codes
        if c in self.colors
    ]

def cmap(name: str | mcolors.Colormap, n: int | None = None) -> mcolors.Colormap:
    """Resolve a colormap by name.

    Args:
        name: A :data:`CUSTOM_CMAPS` or :data:`DEFAULTS` key, a matplotlib
            colormap name, or a ``Colormap`` (returned as is).
        n: Resample to ``n`` discrete levels.

    Raises:
        KeyError: Unknown name.
    """
    if isinstance(name, mcolors.Colormap):
        cm = name
    else:
        key = str(name)
        if key in CUSTOM_CMAPS:
            cm = CUSTOM_CMAPS[key]
        else:
            key = _ALIASES.get(key.lower(), key)
            if key in DEFAULTS:
                key = DEFAULTS[key]
                key = _ALIASES.get(key.lower(), key)
            cm = CUSTOM_CMAPS.get(key) or mpl.colormaps[key]
    if n is not None:
        cm = cm.resampled(n)
    return cm

def role_style(
    role: str, kind: str = "marker", *, filled: bool | None = None, **overrides: Any
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Keyword arguments that draw ``role`` with ``ax.plot``, ``ax.errorbar`` or ``ax.fill_between``.

    Line widths scale with the active theme's ``lw_line``; marker size is left
    to the caller.

    Args:
        role: A key of :data:`ROLES`.
        kind: ``"marker"`` (markers, no line), ``"line"`` (line, no markers),
            ``"both"``, or ``"band"`` (fill keywords for ``fill_between`` or
            ``axhspan``, drawn behind the role's markers).
        filled: Override the role's marker fill. ``False`` gives the open
            variant, e.g. for a sensitivity run of the same method.
        **overrides: Matplotlib keywords that replace the role's defaults.

    Returns:
        A new dict of matplotlib keyword arguments.

    Raises:
        KeyError: ``role`` is not in :data:`ROLES`.
        ValueError: Unknown ``kind``, or ``kind="band"`` for a role without a band.

    Example::

        ax.plot(x, y, **nf.role_style("primary", "both"))
        ax.fill_between(x, lo, hi, **nf.role_style("null", "band"))
    """
    if kind not in _ROLE_KINDS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown kind {kind!r}. Expected one of {_ROLE_KINDS}.")
    r = _role(role)
    if kind == "band":
        band = {"color": role_color(role, band=True), "linewidth": 0, "zorder": r.zorder - 0.5}
        return {**band, **overrides}
    kw: dict[str, Any] = {"color": r.color, "zorder": r.zorder}
    if kind == "marker":
        kw["linestyle"] = "none"
    else:
        kw["linestyle"] = r.linestyle
        kw["linewidth"] = r.linewidth_scale * get_theme().lw_line
    if kind == "line":
        kw["marker"] = "none"
    else:
        fill = r.filled if filled is None else filled
        kw.update(marker=r.marker, markeredgecolor=r.color, markerfacecolor=r.color if fill else "none")
    return {**kw, **overrides}

def diverging_norm(vmin: float, vmax: float, center: float = 0.0) -> mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm:
    """A ``TwoSlopeNorm`` mapping ``center`` to the colormap's midpoint, for anomaly maps.

    ``vmin`` and ``vmax`` are widened if needed so that ``vmin < center < vmax``.
    """
    vmin = min(vmin, center - 1e-9)
    vmax = max(vmax, center + 1e-9)
    return mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=vmin, vcenter=center, vmax=vmax)

def symmetric_limits(values: ArrayLike, *, percentile: float = 98.0) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Colour limits ``(-m, m)`` with ``m`` the ``percentile`` of ``|values|``.

    Non-finite values are ignored; no finite values give ``(-1, 1)``.
    """
    a = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    a = a[np.isfinite(a)]
    if a.size == 0:
        return -1.0, 1.0
    m = float(np.percentile(np.abs(a), percentile))
    m = max(m, 1e-12)
    return -m, m

def robust_limits(values: ArrayLike, *, low: float = 2.0, high: float = 98.0) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Colour limits at the ``low`` and ``high`` percentiles of ``values``.

    Non-finite values are ignored; no finite values give ``(0, 1)``.
    """
    a = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    a = a[np.isfinite(a)]
    if a.size == 0:
        return 0.0, 1.0
    lo, hi = np.percentile(a, [low, high])
    if hi <= lo:
        hi = lo + 1e-12
    return float(lo), float(hi)

def elevation_cmap(
    *,
    sea_level: float = 0.0,
    vmin: float = -8000.0,
    vmax: float = 6000.0,
    name: str = "nicefigs_elevation",
) -> tuple[mcolors.LinearSegmentedColormap, mcolors.Normalize]:
    """Hypsometric elevation colormap and its norm.

    Blues from deep to shallow below ``sea_level``; green, tan, brown and white
    above.

    Args:
        sea_level: Elevation of the land/sea colour break (m).
        vmin: Lowest elevation (m).
        vmax: Highest elevation (m).
        name: Name of the colormap.

    Returns:
        ``(cmap, norm)``; use both together so the break lands at ``sea_level``.
    """
    ocean = [
        (0.00, "#08306b"),
        (0.60, "#4292c6"),
        (1.00, "#c6dbef"),
    ]
    land = [
        (0.00, "#1a7a3c"),
        (0.18, "#8cc665"),
        (0.40, "#e8d98a"),
        (0.62, "#c9a24b"),
        (0.80, "#8f6b3f"),
        (0.92, "#c9c0b8"),
        (1.00, "#ffffff"),
    ]
    span = vmax - vmin
    break_frac = (sea_level - vmin) / span
    stops = []
    for pos, col in ocean:
        stops.append((pos * break_frac, col))
    for pos, col in land:
        stops.append((break_frac + pos * (1 - break_frac), col))
    # Ocean and land stops meet at break_frac; keep one stop per position.
    seen = {}
    for pos, col in stops:
        seen[round(pos, 6)] = col
    stops = sorted(seen.items())
    cm = mcolors.LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(name, stops)
    norm = mcolors.Normalize(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
    return cm, norm

scorecard_diverging_cmap(boundaries: list[float] | None = None) -> tuple[mcolors.ListedColormap, mcolors.BoundaryNorm]

Discrete, quasi-logarithmic diverging (cmap, norm) for skill scorecards.

This is not "the WeatherBench colormap": WeatherBench2's released weatherbench2/visualization.py colours scorecards with continuous RdBu_r at vmin=-100, vmax=100 — no discrete bands, no BoundaryNorm, no extend triangles. The bands and colours here were instead sampled pixel-wise from WeatherBench2's published website figure, which underwent a separate design pass never released as code. The sampled colours are confirmed not to be RdBu_r under any sampling: the worst per-channel error is 61/255 at equal band centres and 93/255 at 11 equal steps. So this is a discrete quasi-logarithmic diverging scale, WeatherBench2-inspired — not a reproduction of WeatherBench2's own code.

The quasi-log spacing (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 per side) resolves the +/-1-5% range where real forecast-skill differences cluster, while still reaching +/-50%; a continuous linear +/-100% scale (as WB2's code uses) flattens that whole cluster to near-uniform pale colour. The centre band is light grey (#F2F2F2), not white, and the under/over extend colours (#26549A / #9C2520) are deliberately distinct from the outermost band colours — the extend triangles read as their own colour, not a repeat of the band next to them.

def scorecard_diverging_cmap(
    boundaries: list[float] | None = None,
) -> tuple[mcolors.ListedColormap, mcolors.BoundaryNorm]:
    """Discrete, quasi-logarithmic diverging ``(cmap, norm)`` for skill scorecards.

    This is **not** "the WeatherBench colormap": WeatherBench2's released
    ``weatherbench2/visualization.py`` colours scorecards with continuous
    ``RdBu_r`` at ``vmin=-100, vmax=100`` — no discrete bands, no
    ``BoundaryNorm``, no extend triangles. The bands and colours here were
    instead sampled pixel-wise from WeatherBench2's *published website figure*,
    which underwent a separate design pass never released as code. The sampled
    colours are confirmed not to be ``RdBu_r`` under any sampling: the worst
    per-channel error is 61/255 at equal band centres and 93/255 at 11 equal
    steps. So this is a discrete quasi-logarithmic diverging scale,
    WeatherBench2-*inspired* — not a reproduction of WeatherBench2's own code.

    The quasi-log spacing (``1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50`` per side) resolves the
    +/-1-5% range where real forecast-skill differences cluster, while still
    reaching +/-50%; a continuous linear +/-100% scale (as WB2's code uses)
    flattens that whole cluster to near-uniform pale colour. The centre band is
    light grey (``#F2F2F2``), not white, and the under/over extend colours
    (``#26549A`` / ``#9C2520``) are deliberately distinct from the outermost
    band colours — the extend triangles read as their own colour, not a repeat
    of the band next to them.

    Args:
        boundaries: 12 band edges (11 bands). Defaults to
            :data:`SCORECARD_DIVERGING_BOUNDARIES`.

    Returns:
        ``(cmap, norm)``: a ``ListedColormap`` with ``set_under``/``set_over``
        applied, and a matching ``BoundaryNorm`` — ready for
        ``imshow``/``pcolormesh``/``colorbar`` with ``extend="both"``.
    """
    boundaries = list(boundaries) if boundaries is not None else list(SCORECARD_DIVERGING_BOUNDARIES)
    if len(boundaries) != len(_SCORECARD_DIVERGING_COLORS) + 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"boundaries must have {len(_SCORECARD_DIVERGING_COLORS) + 1} edges "
            f"for {len(_SCORECARD_DIVERGING_COLORS)} bands, got {len(boundaries)}"
        )
    base = mcolors.ListedColormap(_SCORECARD_DIVERGING_COLORS, name="scorecard_diverging")
    cm = base.with_extremes(under=_SCORECARD_DIVERGING_UNDER, over=_SCORECARD_DIVERGING_OVER)
    cm.name = "scorecard_diverging"
    norm = mcolors.BoundaryNorm(boundaries, cm.N)
    return cm, norm

def qualitative(n: int, palette: str = "nice") -> list[str]:
    """``n`` qualitative colours from a named palette.

    Args:
        n: Number of colours; the palette repeats if ``n`` exceeds its length.
        palette: ``"bright"``, ``"muted"`` or ``"high_contrast"`` (colour-blind
            safe), or a key of :data:`nicefigs.ARTIST_PALETTES` such as
            ``"nice"`` or ``"hockney"``.

    Returns:
        Hex colour strings.

    Raises:
        KeyError: ``palette`` is not a known palette name.
    """
    pals = {"bright": PALETTE_BRIGHT, "muted": PALETTE_MUTED, "high_contrast": PALETTE_HIGH_CONTRAST}
    pals.update(ARTIST_PALETTES)
    try:
        base = pals[palette]
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise KeyError(f"Unknown palette {palette!r}. Available: {sorted(pals)}") from exc
    if n <= len(base):
        return list(base[:n])
    return [base[i % len(base)] for i in range(n)]

def colorbar(
    mappable: ScalarMappable,
    ax: Axes | Sequence[Axes],
    *,
    label: str = "",
    location: str = "right",
    pad: float = 0.012,
    thickness: float = 0.012,
    shrink: float = 1.0,
    extend: str = "neither",
    ticks: ArrayLike | None = None,
) -> Colorbar:
    """Draw a slim colorbar flush to one axes, or spanning several.

    Args:
        mappable: E.g. the return of ``imshow``, ``scatter`` or ``pcolormesh``,
            or one from :func:`make_mappable`.
        ax: One axes, or a sequence of axes the bar should span.
        label: Colorbar label.
        location: ``"right"``, ``"left"``, ``"bottom"`` or ``"top"``.
        pad: Gap between plot and bar, in figure fraction.
        thickness: Bar thickness, in figure fraction.
        shrink: Fraction of the spanned length the bar occupies (centred).
        extend: ``"neither"``, ``"both"``, ``"min"`` or ``"max"``.
        ticks: Explicit tick locations.

    Returns:
        The colorbar.
    """
    axes = list(ax) if isinstance(ax, (list, tuple, np.ndarray)) else [ax]
    fig = axes[0].figure
    th = get_theme()
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = _bbox_union(axes)

    if location in ("right", "left"):
        length = (y1 - y0) * shrink
        cy = 0.5 * (y0 + y1) - length / 2
        if location == "right":
            cax = fig.add_axes([x1 + pad, cy, thickness, length])
        else:
            cax = fig.add_axes([x0 - pad - thickness, cy, thickness, length])
        orientation = "vertical"
    else:
        length = (x1 - x0) * shrink
        cx = 0.5 * (x0 + x1) - length / 2
        if location == "bottom":
            cax = fig.add_axes([cx, y0 - pad - thickness, length, thickness])
        else:
            cax = fig.add_axes([cx, y1 + pad, length, thickness])
        orientation = "horizontal"

    cb = fig.colorbar(mappable, cax=cax, orientation=orientation, extend=extend, ticks=ticks)
    cb.outline.set_linewidth(0.4)
    cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=th.fs_tick, length=1.6, width=0.35, pad=1.2)
    if location == "left":
        cax.yaxis.set_ticks_position("left")
        cax.yaxis.set_label_position("left")
    if location == "top":
        cax.xaxis.set_ticks_position("top")
        cax.xaxis.set_label_position("top")
    if label:
        cb.set_label(label, fontsize=th.fs_annot, labelpad=2.0)
    return cb

    values: ArrayLike | None = None,
    *,
    cmap: str | Colormap = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
) -> ScalarMappable:
    """Build a ``ScalarMappable`` for a colorbar without a plotted artist.

    Args:
        values: Data whose finite min and max fill in missing ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        cmap: Colormap or name, resolved by :func:`nicefigs.cmap`.
        vmin: Lower colour limit.
        vmax: Upper colour limit.
        norm: Normalisation; overrides ``vmin``, ``vmax`` and ``values``.
    """
    if norm is None:
        if (vmin is None or vmax is None) and values is not None:
            a = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
            a = a[np.isfinite(a)]
            vmin = float(np.min(a)) if vmin is None else vmin
            vmax = float(np.max(a)) if vmax is None else vmax
        norm = Normalize(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
    sm = ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=_resolve_cmap(cmap))
    sm.set_array([])
    return sm

def inset_histogram_colorbar(
    ax: Axes,
    values: ArrayLike,
    *,
    cmap: str | Colormap = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    bounds: tuple[float, float, float, float] = (0.045, 0.08, 0.24, 0.17),
    n_bins: int = 24,
    label: str | None = None,
    frame_alpha: float = 0.0,
    log: bool = False,
) -> Axes | None:
    """Draw an inset histogram of ``values`` with bars coloured by ``cmap``.

    The inset acts as a colorbar that also shows the data distribution.

    Args:
        ax: Host axes.
        values: Mapped data; non-finite values are ignored.
        cmap: Colormap or name, resolved by :func:`nicefigs.cmap`.
        vmin: Histogram and colour lower limit; defaults to the 2nd percentile.
        vmax: Histogram and colour upper limit; defaults to the 98th percentile.
        norm: Colour normalisation used instead of the linear ``vmin``/``vmax`` one.
        bounds: Inset ``(x, y, width, height)`` in axes fraction; the default
            sits in the lower left, the empty South Pacific of a world map.
        n_bins: Number of bins.
        label: X-axis label of the inset.
        frame_alpha: Opacity of the inset's white background.
        log: Show ``log1p`` counts.

    Returns:
        The inset axes, or ``None`` when ``values`` has no finite entries.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    vals = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    vals = vals[np.isfinite(vals)]
    if vals.size == 0:
        return None
    if vmin is None or vmax is None:
        lo, hi = np.percentile(vals, [2.0, 98.0])
        vmin = float(lo) if vmin is None else vmin
        vmax = float(hi) if vmax is None else vmax
    if vmax - vmin < 1e-12:
        vmax = vmin + 1e-12

    inset = ax.inset_axes(bounds)
    counts, edges = np.histogram(vals, bins=n_bins, range=(vmin, vmax))
    centers = 0.5 * (edges[:-1] + edges[1:])
    cm = _resolve_cmap(cmap)
    if norm is not None:
        colors = [cm(float(np.clip(norm(c), 0, 1))) for c in centers]
    else:
        colors = [cm(float((c - vmin) / (vmax - vmin))) for c in centers]
    if log:
        counts = np.log1p(counts)
    inset.bar(centers, counts, width=(edges[1] - edges[0]) * 0.95, color=colors, edgecolor="none")
    inset.set_xlim(vmin, vmax)
    inset.set_yticks([])
    inset.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(3))
    inset.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=th.fs_annot - 0.5, length=1.6, pad=0.8)
    for side in ("top", "right", "left"):
        inset.spines[side].set_visible(False)
    inset.spines["bottom"].set_linewidth(0.4)
    inset.set_facecolor("#ffffff")
    inset.patch.set_alpha(frame_alpha)
    if label is not None:
        # Left-aligned so a long label stays inside a curved map frame.
        inset.set_xlabel(label, fontsize=th.fs_annot - 0.5, labelpad=0.8, ha="left", x=0.0)
    return inset

def prettify_unit(unit: str | None, *, superscript: bool = True) -> str:
    """Prettify a plain-text unit string.

    ``"m2"`` becomes ``"m²"``, ``"kg m-2 s-1"`` becomes ``"kg m⁻² s⁻¹"`` and
    ``"degC"`` becomes ``"°C"``.

    Args:
        unit: Plain-text unit; ``None`` gives ``""``.
        superscript: Render exponents as Unicode superscripts; otherwise as ``^n``.

    Returns:
        The prettified unit.
    """
    if unit is None:
        return ""
    u = unit.strip()
    if u in _UNIT_FIX:
        return _UNIT_FIX[u]
    for k, v in _UNIT_FIX.items():
        u = re.sub(rf"\b{k}\b", v, u)

    def _exp(m: re.Match) -> str:
        base, exp = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        if superscript:
            return base + exp.translate(_SUP)
        return f"{base}^{exp}"

    u = re.sub(r"([A-Za-zµ°%])(-?\d+)", _exp, u)
    u = re.sub(r"([A-Za-zµ°%])\^(-?\d+)", _exp, u)
    return u

    brackets: str = "[]",

    label = quantity

        label = f"{quantity} {lo}{prettify_unit(units, superscript=superscript)}{hi}"
    arrow = _arrow(direction)
    return f"{label} {arrow}".rstrip() if arrow else label

def metric_label(
    key: str,
    units: str | None = None,
    *,
    direction: str | bool | None = None,
    registry: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Axis label for a metric key, e.g. ``"rmse"`` gives ``"RMSE"``.

    Args:
        key: Metric key, looked up case-insensitively; unknown keys are title-cased.
        units: Plain-text unit.
        direction: ``True`` looks the arrow up in :data:`METRIC_DIRECTION`; a
            string sets it as in :func:`axis_label`; ``None`` or ``False`` omits it.
        registry: Key-to-name mapping used instead of :data:`METRIC_NAMES`.

    Returns:
        The label.
    """
    reg = registry or METRIC_NAMES
    name = reg.get(key.lower(), key.replace("_", " ").title())
    if direction is True:
        direction = METRIC_DIRECTION.get(key.lower())
    elif direction is False:
        direction = None
    return axis_label(name, units, direction=direction)

def fmt_val(v: float, *, sig: int = 3) -> str:
    """Format a number with ``sig`` significant digits.

    Magnitudes outside ``[1e-3, 1e4)`` use ``m×10ⁿ`` notation; zero gives ``"0"``
    and non-finite values give ``"–"``.
    """
    if v == 0 or not np.isfinite(v):
        return "0" if v == 0 else "–"
    a = abs(v)
    if 1e-3 <= a < 1e4:
        s = f"{v:.{sig}g}"
        return s
    exp = int(np.floor(np.log10(a)))
    mant = v / 10**exp
    return f"{mant:.{max(sig - 1, 0)}f}×10{str(exp).translate(_SUP)}"

def fmt_pval(p: float) -> str:
    """Format a p-value as ``"p < 0.001"``, ``"p = 0.004"`` or ``"p = 0.12"``."""
    if p < 1e-3:
        return "p < 0.001"
    if p < 1e-2:
        return f"p = {p:.3f}"
    return f"p = {p:.2f}"

The default map is a Robinson projection with Antarctica cropped, a light land backdrop, coastlines and an inset histogram that doubles as the colorbar. :func:map picks a drawing method from the data layout; the per-layout helpers (:func:scatter_map, :func:binned_map, :func:raster_map, :func:tri_map, :func:categorical_map) draw onto an existing axes. Without cartopy, maps fall back to plain equirectangular axes.

def make_map_axes(
    fig: Figure,
    subplot_spec: int | tuple[int, int, int] | SubplotSpec = 111,
    *,
    projection: str = "robinson",
    central_longitude: float = 0.0,
    **proj_kwargs: Any,
) -> tuple[Axes, ModuleType | None]:
    """Add a map axes to ``fig``, projected when cartopy is installed.

    Args:
        fig: Figure to add the axes to.
        subplot_spec: An int such as ``111``, a ``(nrows, ncols, index)`` tuple,
            or a :class:`~matplotlib.gridspec.SubplotSpec`.
        projection: ``"robinson"``, ``"platecarree"``, ``"mollweide"``,
            ``"equalearth"``, ``"orthographic"`` or ``"nearside"``.
        central_longitude: Central meridian in degrees east, where the
            projection supports it.
        **proj_kwargs: Forwarded to the cartopy projection class.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, ccrs)``: the axes and the ``cartopy.crs`` module, or a plain axes
        and ``None`` without cartopy.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``projection`` is not one of the names above.
    """
    key = projection.lower()
    if key not in _PROJECTIONS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown projection {projection!r}. Known: {sorted(_PROJECTIONS)}")
    ccrs = _try_cartopy()
    proj = None
    if ccrs is not None:
        cls = getattr(ccrs, _PROJECTIONS[key])
        try:
            proj = cls(central_longitude=central_longitude, **proj_kwargs)
        except TypeError:
            proj = cls(**proj_kwargs)
    if isinstance(subplot_spec, tuple):
        ax = fig.add_subplot(*subplot_spec, projection=proj)
    else:
        ax = fig.add_subplot(subplot_spec, projection=proj)
    return ax, ccrs

def draw_background(
    ax: Axes,
    ccrs: ModuleType | None,
    *,
    land: bool = True,
    ocean: bool = False,
    coastline: bool = True,
    borders: bool = False,
    land_color: str = COLORS["land"],
    ocean_color: str = COLORS["ocean"],
    coast_color: str = COLORS["coast"],
    coast_lw: float = 0.3,
    resolution: str = "110m",
) -> None:
    """Draw a land, ocean, coastline and border backdrop on a projected map axes.

    The features are rasterized so vector output (SVG, PDF) stays small while text
    and frame remain vectors. Does nothing when ``ccrs`` is ``None``.

    Args:
        ax: Cartopy ``GeoAxes``, e.g. from :func:`make_map_axes`.
        ccrs: The ``cartopy.crs`` module, or ``None`` for a plain axes.
        land: Fill land with ``land_color``.
        ocean: Fill ocean with ``ocean_color``.
        coastline: Draw coastlines.
        borders: Draw country borders.
        land_color: Land fill colour.
        ocean_color: Ocean fill colour.
        coast_color: Coastline and border colour.
        coast_lw: Coastline width in points; borders are 0.7 times this.
        resolution: Natural Earth coastline resolution: ``"110m"``, ``"50m"`` or ``"10m"``.
    """
    if ccrs is None:
        return
    import cartopy.feature as cfeature

    def _rasterize(artist: Any) -> None:
        if artist is not None and hasattr(artist, "set_rasterized"):
            artist.set_rasterized(True)

    if ocean:
        _rasterize(ax.add_feature(cfeature.OCEAN, facecolor=ocean_color, edgecolor="none", zorder=0))
    if land:
        _rasterize(ax.add_feature(cfeature.LAND, facecolor=land_color, edgecolor="none", zorder=0))
    if coastline:
        try:
            _rasterize(
                ax.coastlines(resolution=resolution, linewidth=coast_lw, color=coast_color, zorder=2.5)
            )
        except OSError:  # Natural Earth data unavailable (e.g. offline): skip coastlines.
            pass
    if borders:
        _rasterize(
            ax.add_feature(cfeature.BORDERS, linewidth=coast_lw * 0.7, edgecolor=coast_color, zorder=2.5)
        )
    try:
        ax.spines["geo"].set_edgecolor("#333333")
        ax.spines["geo"].set_linewidth(0.7)
    except (KeyError, AttributeError):
        pass

def hatch_region(
    ax: Axes,
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike,
    mask: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ccrs: ModuleType | None = None,
    hatch: str = "////",
    edgecolor: str = "#333333",
    linewidth: float = 0.5,
    bin_deg: float = 2.0,
    threshold: float = 0.5,
) -> QuadContourSet:
    """Hatch the region where a per-point mask is set, leaving the colours beneath visible.

    The mask is bin-averaged onto a ``bin_deg`` grid and cells at or above
    ``threshold`` are hatched without fill.

    Args:
        ax: Map axes.
        lon: Point longitudes in degrees east.
        lat: Point latitudes in degrees north.
        mask: Per-point boolean or fraction, same shape as ``lon``.
        ccrs: The ``cartopy.crs`` module when ``ax`` is projected, else ``None``.
        hatch: Matplotlib hatch pattern.
        edgecolor: Hatch colour.
        linewidth: Hatch line width in points.
        bin_deg: Grid cell size in degrees.
        threshold: Minimum cell-mean mask value that is hatched.

    Returns:
        The contour set drawing the hatch.
    """
    lon = np.asarray(lon, dtype=float)
    lat = np.asarray(lat, dtype=float)
    m = np.asarray(mask, dtype=float)
    lon_e, lat_e, grid = _bin_values(lon, lat, m, bin_deg, 0, False, "110m")
    lon_c = 0.5 * (lon_e[:-1] + lon_e[1:])
    lat_c = 0.5 * (lat_e[:-1] + lat_e[1:])
    filled = np.ma.filled(grid, 0.0)
    kw = {}
    if ccrs is not None:
        kw["transform"] = ccrs.PlateCarree()
    cs = ax.contourf(lon_c, lat_c, filled, levels=[threshold, 1e9], colors="none", hatches=[hatch], **kw)
    # matplotlib < 3.8 exposes per-level ``.collections``; later the ContourSet is the collection.
    targets = getattr(cs, "collections", None) or [cs]
    for coll in targets:
        coll.set_edgecolor(edgecolor)
        coll.set_linewidth(linewidth)
    return cs

def scatter_map(
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike,
    values: ArrayLike | None = None,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    ccrs: ModuleType | None = None,
    cmap: str | Colormap = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    size: float = 6.0,
    alpha: float = 0.9,
    sort_by_value: bool = True,
    **scatter_kw: Any,
) -> tuple[Axes, PathCollection]:
    """Scatter points on a map, coloured by ``values`` if given.

    Points with non-finite values are dropped.

    Args:
        ax: Map axes; a Robinson map figure is created if ``None``.
        lon: Longitudes in degrees east, shape ``(N,)``.
        lat: Latitudes in degrees north, shape ``(N,)``.
        values: Per-point values; ``None`` draws plain locations.
        ccrs: The ``cartopy.crs`` module; detected from ``ax`` if ``None``.
        cmap: Colormap name or object.
        vmin: Lower colour limit.
        vmax: Upper colour limit.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        size: Marker area in points².
        alpha: Marker opacity.
        sort_by_value: Draw low values first so high values sit on top.
        **scatter_kw: Forwarded to :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.scatter`.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, mappable)``: the axes and the scatter collection (a mappable when ``values`` is given).
    """
    ax, ccrs = _layer_axes(ax, ccrs)
    lon = np.asarray(lon, dtype=float)
    lat = np.asarray(lat, dtype=float)
    kw = dict(s=size, linewidths=0, alpha=alpha, rasterized=True)
    if ccrs is not None:
        kw["transform"] = ccrs.PlateCarree()
    if values is None:
        return ax, ax.scatter(lon, lat, **kw, **scatter_kw)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    valid = np.isfinite(values)
    lon, lat, values = lon[valid], lat[valid], values[valid]
    if sort_by_value:
        order = np.argsort(values)
        lon, lat, values = lon[order], lat[order], values[order]
    kw.update(c=values, cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
    if norm is not None:
        kw["norm"] = norm
        kw.pop("vmin")
        kw.pop("vmax")
    return ax, ax.scatter(lon, lat, **kw, **scatter_kw)

def binned_map(
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike,
    values: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    ccrs: ModuleType | None = None,
    cmap: str | Colormap = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    bin_deg: float = 2.0,
    fill_bins: int = 0,
    clip_ocean: bool = False,
    land_resolution: str = "110m",
    **mesh_kw: Any,
) -> tuple[Axes, QuadMesh]:
    """Average point values onto a regular lon/lat grid and draw it as a mesh.

    Args:
        ax: Map axes; a Robinson map figure is created if ``None``.
        lon: Point longitudes in degrees east, shape ``(N,)``.
        lat: Point latitudes in degrees north, shape ``(N,)``.
        values: Point values, shape ``(N,)``; non-finite values are ignored.
        ccrs: The ``cartopy.crs`` module; detected from ``ax`` if ``None``.
        cmap: Colormap name or object.
        vmin: Lower colour limit.
        vmax: Upper colour limit.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        bin_deg: Grid cell size in degrees.
        fill_bins: Fill empty cells within this many cells of data by linear
            interpolation (requires scipy); 0 disables filling.
        clip_ocean: Mask cells whose centre lies at sea (requires cartopy and
            shapely); the grid then spans the globe.
        land_resolution: Natural Earth resolution of the land mask.
        **mesh_kw: Forwarded to :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.pcolormesh`.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, mappable)``: the axes and the ``QuadMesh`` mappable.
    """
    ax, ccrs = _layer_axes(ax, ccrs)
    lon = np.asarray(lon, dtype=float)
    lat = np.asarray(lat, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    lon_e, lat_e, grid = _bin_values(lon, lat, values, bin_deg, fill_bins, clip_ocean, land_resolution)
    kw = dict(cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), shading="flat", rasterized=True)
    if norm is not None:
        kw["norm"] = norm
    else:
        kw["vmin"], kw["vmax"] = vmin, vmax
    if ccrs is not None:
        kw["transform"] = ccrs.PlateCarree()
    return ax, ax.pcolormesh(lon_e, lat_e, grid, **kw, **mesh_kw)

def categorical_map(
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike,
    codes: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    categories: Mapping[Any, str] | Sequence[str],
    ccrs: ModuleType | None = None,
    colors: Mapping[Any, str] | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    kind: Literal["auto", "binned", "scatter"] = "auto",
    bin_deg: float = 2.0,
    legend: bool = True,
    legend_kw: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    **kw: Any,
) -> tuple[Axes, QuadMesh | PathCollection]:
    """Map per-point class labels as discrete colours with a matching legend.

    Class codes cannot be averaged, so dense clouds are reduced to a ``bin_deg``
    grid by **majority vote** (ties go to the earlier category) rather than by
    the mean :func:`binned_map` takes; sparse clouds are drawn as a scatter.
    Points whose code is not in ``categories``, and points with a non-finite
    coordinate, are dropped.

    Args:
        ax: Map axes; a Robinson map figure is created if ``None``.
        lon: Point longitudes in degrees east.
        lat: Point latitudes in degrees north.
        codes: Per-point class label (integer or string), same shape as ``lon``.
        categories: Ordered class names — a ``{code: name}`` mapping for
            arbitrary codes, or a sequence of names read as codes ``0..n-1``
            (or, for string labels, as the codes themselves).
        ccrs: The ``cartopy.crs`` module; detected from ``ax`` if ``None``.
        colors: One colour per category, as a sequence in category order or a
            mapping keyed by category name or code. Defaults to
            :func:`nicefigs.qualitative`.
        kind: ``"auto"`` (binned above 5000 valid points, else scatter),
            ``"binned"``, or ``"scatter"``.
        bin_deg: Grid cell size in degrees for the binned path.
        legend: Draw a discrete patch legend, one entry per category present.
        legend_kw: Overrides forwarded to :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.legend`.
        **kw: Forwarded to :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.pcolormesh` or :func:`scatter_map`.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, mappable)``: the axes and the mappable (a ``QuadMesh`` or ``PathCollection``). The legend, when
        drawn, is reachable as ``ax.get_legend()``.

    Example:
        >>> categorical_map(lon, lat, codes, categories=["in", "out"], ax=ax)  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    ax, ccrs = _layer_axes(ax, ccrs)
    import matplotlib.colors as mcolors

    cat_codes, cat_names = _resolve_categories(categories, codes)
    cat_colors = _resolve_category_colors(colors, cat_codes, cat_names)
    n = len(cat_codes)
    cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap(cat_colors)
    norm = mcolors.BoundaryNorm(np.arange(-0.5, n + 0.5, 1.0), n)

    lon = np.asarray(lon, dtype=float).ravel()
    lat = np.asarray(lat, dtype=float).ravel()
    index = _category_indices(codes, cat_codes).ravel()
    valid = (index >= 0) & np.isfinite(lon) & np.isfinite(lat)
    lon, lat, index = lon[valid], lat[valid], index[valid]

    binned = kind == "binned" or (kind == "auto" and index.size > AUTO_BIN_MIN_POINTS)
    if binned and index.size:
        lon_e, lat_e, grid = _bin_majority(lon, lat, index, n, bin_deg)
        mesh_kw = dict(cmap=cmap, norm=norm, shading="flat", rasterized=True)
        if ccrs is not None:
            mesh_kw["transform"] = ccrs.PlateCarree()
        mappable = ax.pcolormesh(lon_e, lat_e, grid, **mesh_kw, **kw)
        present = np.unique(np.ma.compressed(grid))
    else:
        _, mappable = scatter_map(
            lon,
            lat,
            index.astype(float),
            ccrs=ccrs,
            cmap=cmap,
            norm=norm,
            sort_by_value=False,
            **kw,
            ax=ax,
        )
        present = np.unique(index)

    if legend and present.size:
        from matplotlib.patches import Patch

        th = get_theme()
        handles = [
            Patch(facecolor=cat_colors[i], edgecolor="none", label=cat_names[i]) for i in present.astype(int)
        ]
        # A class map fills its frame, so the legend sits on a translucent
        # backing rather than over bare colour.
        lkw = dict(
            loc="lower left",
            fontsize=th.fs_legend,
            frameon=True,
            framealpha=0.85,
            facecolor="white",
            edgecolor="none",
            handlelength=1.0,
            handletextpad=0.5,
            borderpad=0.4,
            labelspacing=0.35,
        )
        lkw.update(legend_kw or {})
        ax.legend(handles=handles, **lkw)
    return ax, mappable

def raster_map(
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike,
    field: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    ccrs: ModuleType | None = None,
    cmap: str | Colormap = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    method: Literal["pcolormesh", "imshow"] = "pcolormesh",
    shading: str = "auto",
    **kw: Any,
) -> tuple[Axes, ScalarMappable]:
    """Draw an already-gridded 2-D field on a map.

    Args:
        ax: Map axes; a Robinson map figure is created if ``None``.
        lon: Cell-centre longitudes in degrees east: 1-D ``(nx,)`` for a regular
            grid, or 2-D ``(ny, nx)`` for a curvilinear one.
        lat: Cell-centre latitudes in degrees north: 1-D ``(ny,)`` or 2-D ``(ny, nx)``.
        field: Values of shape ``(ny, nx)``; NaNs render transparent.
        ccrs: The ``cartopy.crs`` module; detected from ``ax`` if ``None``.
        cmap: Colormap name or object.
        vmin: Lower colour limit.
        vmax: Upper colour limit.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        method: ``"pcolormesh"`` handles irregular and curvilinear grids;
            ``"imshow"`` is faster but needs a regular grid with 1-D coordinates.
        shading: ``pcolormesh`` shading mode.
        **kw: Forwarded to :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.pcolormesh` or
            :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.imshow`.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, mappable)``: the axes and the ``QuadMesh`` or ``AxesImage`` mappable.
    """
    ax, ccrs = _layer_axes(ax, ccrs)
    field = np.ma.masked_invalid(np.asarray(field, dtype=float))
    kw = dict(kw, cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), rasterized=True)
    if norm is not None:
        kw["norm"] = norm
    else:
        kw["vmin"], kw["vmax"] = vmin, vmax
    if ccrs is not None:
        kw["transform"] = ccrs.PlateCarree()
    if method == "imshow":
        lon = np.asarray(lon)
        lat = np.asarray(lat)
        extent = (float(lon.min()), float(lon.max()), float(lat.min()), float(lat.max()))
        origin = "upper" if lat[0] > lat[-1] else "lower"
        return ax, ax.imshow(field, extent=extent, origin=origin, aspect="auto", **kw)
    return ax, ax.pcolormesh(np.asarray(lon), np.asarray(lat), field, shading=shading, **kw)

def tri_map(
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike,
    values: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    ccrs: ModuleType | None = None,
    cmap: str | Colormap = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    method: Literal["tricontourf", "tripcolor"] = "tricontourf",
    levels: int | Sequence[float] = 14,
    max_edge_frac: float = 0.12,
    **kw: Any,
) -> tuple[Axes, ScalarMappable]:
    """Draw unstructured data (e.g. an icosahedral mesh) by triangulating its points.

    The triangulation is built in projected coordinates, and triangles whose
    longest edge exceeds ``max_edge_frac`` of the map width are masked, so no
    triangle smears across the antimeridian or the poles.

    Args:
        ax: Map axes; a Robinson map figure is created if ``None``.
        lon: Node longitudes in degrees east, shape ``(N,)``.
        lat: Node latitudes in degrees north, shape ``(N,)``.
        values: Node values, shape ``(N,)``; non-finite nodes are dropped.
        ccrs: The ``cartopy.crs`` module; detected from ``ax`` if ``None``.
        cmap: Colormap name or object.
        vmin: Lower colour limit.
        vmax: Upper colour limit.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        method: ``"tricontourf"`` for smooth filled contours, ``"tripcolor"`` for
            Gouraud-shaded triangles.
        levels: Contour levels (count or boundaries) for ``tricontourf``.
        max_edge_frac: Mask triangles with an edge longer than this fraction of
            the projected map width.
        **kw: Forwarded to :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.tricontourf` or
            :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.tripcolor`.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, mappable)``: the axes and the contour set or ``PolyCollection`` mappable.
    """
    ax, ccrs = _layer_axes(ax, ccrs)
    from matplotlib.tri import Triangulation

    lon = np.asarray(lon, dtype=float)
    lat = np.asarray(lat, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    finite = np.isfinite(values) & np.isfinite(lon) & np.isfinite(lat)
    lon, lat, values = lon[finite], lat[finite], values[finite]

    # Points are projected here, so the plot call needs no ``transform``.
    if ccrs is not None:
        pts = ax.projection.transform_points(ccrs.PlateCarree(), lon, lat)
        x, y = pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1]
        ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
        x, y, values = x[ok], y[ok], values[ok]
    else:
        x, y = lon, lat

    tri = Triangulation(x, y)
    xt, yt = x[tri.triangles], y[tri.triangles]
    edges = np.sqrt((xt - np.roll(xt, 1, 1)) ** 2 + (yt - np.roll(yt, 1, 1)) ** 2).max(1)
    width = np.nanmax(x) - np.nanmin(x)
    tri.set_mask(edges > max_edge_frac * width)

    kw = dict(kw, cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap))
    if norm is not None:
        kw["norm"] = norm
    else:
        kw["vmin"], kw["vmax"] = vmin, vmax
    if method == "tripcolor":
        return ax, ax.tripcolor(tri, values, shading="gouraud", rasterized=True, **kw)
    return ax, ax.tricontourf(tri, values, levels=levels, **kw)

def from_xarray(da: Any) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Extract ``(lon, lat, field)`` numpy arrays from an xarray ``DataArray``.

    Longitude and latitude coordinates are found by common names (``lon``,
    ``longitude``, ``x``, ``nav_lon``, ...; case-insensitive) after squeezing
    singleton dimensions. Works for regular grids and for unstructured data with
    one cell dimension.

    Args:
        da: An ``xarray.DataArray``.

    Returns:
        ``(lon, lat, field)`` as numpy arrays.

    Raises:
        KeyError: No longitude or latitude coordinate is found.
    """
    da = da.squeeze()
    coords = {str(k).lower(): k for k in da.coords}
    lon_key = next((coords[n] for n in _LON_NAMES if n in coords), None)
    lat_key = next((coords[n] for n in _LAT_NAMES if n in coords), None)
    if lon_key is None or lat_key is None:
        raise KeyError(
            f"Could not find lon/lat coords in {list(da.coords)}. "
            "Pass lon/lat explicitly, or rename coords to lon/lat."
        )
    return np.asarray(da[lon_key].values), np.asarray(da[lat_key].values), np.asarray(da.values)

def map(
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike | None = None,
    values: ArrayLike | None = None,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    fig: Figure | None = None,
    subplot_spec: int | tuple[int, int, int] | SubplotSpec = 111,
    kind: str = "auto",
    projection: str = "robinson",
    central_longitude: float = 0.0,
    extent: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    antarctica_cutoff: bool = True,
    cmap: str | Colormap | None = None,
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    robust: bool = True,
    diverging: bool = False,
    center: float = 0.0,
    bin_deg: float = 2.0,
    fill_bins: int = 0,
    clip_ocean: bool | None = None,
    land: bool = True,
    ocean: bool = False,
    coastline: bool = True,
    borders: bool = False,
    inset_hist: bool = True,
    colorbar_label: str = "",
    cbar: bool = False,
    cbar_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    hist_bounds: tuple[float, float, float, float] = (0.07, 0.22, 0.18, 0.11),
    width: str | float = "full",
    aspect: float = 0.52,
    title: str = "",
    **plot_kw: Any,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes, ScalarMappable | None]:
    """Draw a global or regional map, choosing the drawing method from the data layout.

    Four layouts are supported:

    * **points**: 1-D ``lon``, ``lat``, ``values``, scattered, or bin-averaged for
      dense clouds;
    * **gridded**: 1-D or 2-D ``lon``/``lat`` with a 2-D ``values`` field, or an
      xarray ``DataArray`` as the only argument (``map(da)``);
    * **unstructured**: 1-D ``lon``/``lat``/``values`` with ``kind="tri"``;
    * **classes**: class labels with ``kind="categorical"`` and ``categories=...``,
      decoded by a patch legend instead of a colorbar.

    Args:
        lon: Longitudes in degrees east, or an xarray ``DataArray`` passed alone.
        lat: Latitudes in degrees north.
        values: Per-point values (1-D) or a gridded field (2-D); ``None`` draws
            just the locations.
        ax: Existing map axes to draw into; created if ``None``.
        fig: Figure to add the axes to when ``ax`` is ``None``.
        subplot_spec: Position of the new axes, as in :func:`make_map_axes`.
        kind: ``"auto"`` (raster for 2-D fields, binned above
            :data:`AUTO_BIN_MIN_POINTS` points, else scatter), ``"scatter"``,
            ``"binned"``, ``"raster"``, ``"imshow"``, ``"tri"``, ``"tripcolor"``
            or ``"categorical"`` (see :func:`categorical_map`).
        projection: Projection name, as in :func:`make_map_axes`.
        central_longitude: Central meridian in degrees east.
        extent: ``(west, east, south, north)`` in degrees for a regional map;
            overrides ``antarctica_cutoff``.
        antarctica_cutoff: Crop the global view to latitudes -60 to 84.
        cmap: Colormap name or object; defaults to ``"RdBu_r"`` when
            ``diverging``, else ``"inferno"``.
        vmin: Lower colour limit.
        vmax: Upper colour limit.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides the limits.
        robust: Use 2nd/98th-percentile limits when ``vmin``/``vmax`` are unset.
        diverging: Use limits symmetric about ``center`` and a diverging colormap.
        center: Centre value of the diverging normalisation.
        bin_deg: Grid cell size in degrees for binned and categorical maps.
        fill_bins: Gap filling for binned maps, as in :func:`binned_map`.
        clip_ocean: For binned maps, mask cells whose centre is at sea. ``None``
            clips global maps that draw land; pass ``False`` for data measured
            over the ocean.
        land: Draw the land background.
        ocean: Fill the ocean.
        coastline: Draw coastlines.
        borders: Draw country borders.
        inset_hist: Draw the inset histogram that doubles as the colorbar.
        colorbar_label: Label of the histogram and/or colorbar.
        cbar: Also draw a conventional colorbar.
        cbar_kwargs: Keywords for :func:`nicefigs.colorbar`.
        hist_bounds: Inset histogram ``(x0, y0, width, height)`` in axes fractions.
        width: Width of a new figure, a named width or inches.
        aspect: Height / width of a new figure.
        title: Left-aligned panel title.
        **plot_kw: Forwarded to the layout helper (:func:`scatter_map`,
            :func:`binned_map`, :func:`raster_map`, :func:`tri_map` or
            :func:`categorical_map`).

    Returns:
        ``(fig, ax, mappable)``; ``mappable`` is ``None`` when ``values`` is ``None``.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    # An xarray DataArray may be passed as the sole positional argument.
    if _is_dataarray(lon) and lat is None:
        lon, lat, values = from_xarray(lon)
        if kind == "auto":
            kind = "raster"

    if ax is None:
        if fig is None:
            from .figure import figure_size

            fig = plt.figure(figsize=figure_size(width, aspect=aspect), dpi=th.dpi)
        ax, ccrs = make_map_axes(
            fig, subplot_spec, projection=projection, central_longitude=central_longitude
        )
    else:
        fig = ax.figure
        ccrs = _try_cartopy() if hasattr(ax, "projection") else None

    if cmap is None:
        cmap = "RdBu_r" if diverging else "inferno"

    # limits (meaningless for class labels, which carry their own discrete norm)
    if values is not None and norm is None and kind != "categorical":
        if diverging:
            from .palettes import diverging_norm, symmetric_limits

            lo, hi = symmetric_limits(values) if (vmin is None or vmax is None) else (vmin, vmax)
            vmin = lo if vmin is None else vmin
            vmax = hi if vmax is None else vmax
            norm = diverging_norm(vmin, vmax, center)
        elif robust and (vmin is None or vmax is None):
            lo, hi = robust_limits(values)
            vmin = lo if vmin is None else vmin
            vmax = hi if vmax is None else vmax

    draw_background(ax, ccrs, land=land, ocean=ocean, coastline=coastline, borders=borders)
    _apply_extent(ax, ccrs, extent, antarctica_cutoff and extent is None)

    mappable = None
    if values is not None:
        eff = kind
        if kind == "auto":
            eff = (
                "raster"
                if np.ndim(values) == 2
                else ("binned" if np.size(values) > AUTO_BIN_MIN_POINTS else "scatter")
            )

        if eff in ("raster", "imshow", "pcolormesh"):
            _, mappable = raster_map(
                lon,
                lat,
                values,
                ccrs=ccrs,
                cmap=cmap,
                vmin=vmin,
                vmax=vmax,
                norm=norm,
                method="imshow" if eff == "imshow" else "pcolormesh",
                **plot_kw,
                ax=ax,
            )
        elif eff in ("tri", "tricontourf", "tripcolor"):
            _, mappable = tri_map(
                lon,
                lat,
                values,
                ccrs=ccrs,
                cmap=cmap,
                vmin=vmin,
                vmax=vmax,
                norm=norm,
                method="tripcolor" if eff == "tripcolor" else "tricontourf",
                **plot_kw,
                ax=ax,
            )
        elif eff == "categorical":
            _, mappable = categorical_map(lon, lat, values, ccrs=ccrs, bin_deg=bin_deg, **plot_kw, ax=ax)
        elif eff == "binned":
            # Ocean-clip only for global maps: over a fine regional grid the
            # point-in-polygon land mask is prohibitively slow and rarely wanted.
            clip = (land and extent is None) if clip_ocean is None else bool(clip_ocean)
            _, mappable = binned_map(
                lon,
                lat,
                values,
                ccrs=ccrs,
                cmap=cmap,
                vmin=vmin,
                vmax=vmax,
                norm=norm,
                bin_deg=bin_deg,
                fill_bins=fill_bins,
                clip_ocean=clip,
                **plot_kw,
                ax=ax,
            )
        else:
            _, mappable = scatter_map(
                lon,
                lat,
                values,
                ccrs=ccrs,
                cmap=cmap,
                vmin=vmin,
                vmax=vmax,
                norm=norm,
                **plot_kw,
                ax=ax,
            )
    else:
        scatter_map(lon, lat, ccrs=ccrs, color=COLORS["primary"], **plot_kw, ax=ax)

    if title:
        from .panels import clean_title

        clean_title(ax, title)

    # A categorical map decodes itself through its legend, never a colorbar.
    if mappable is not None and kind != "categorical":
        if inset_hist:
            inset_histogram_colorbar(
                ax,
                values,
                cmap=cmap,
                vmin=vmin,
                vmax=vmax,
                norm=norm,
                bounds=hist_bounds,
                label=colorbar_label or None,
            )
        if cbar:
            cbar_kwargs = dict(cbar_kwargs or {})
            cbar_kwargs.setdefault("label", colorbar_label)
