def image(
    data: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    cmap: str = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    robust: bool = False,
    rgb: bool = False,
    stretch: bool = False,
    title: str = "",
    interpolation: str = "nearest",
    origin: Literal["upper", "lower"] = "upper",
    overlay_contour: ArrayLike | None = None,
    contour_color: str = "white",
    contour_linewidth: float = 0.8,
    frame: bool = False,
    **imshow_kw: Any,
) -> tuple[Axes, AxesImage | None]:
    """Show an intensity or RGB array on ``ax`` without ticks.

    Args:
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        data: Intensity array ``(H, W)``, or colour image ``(H, W, 3|4)`` in
            ``[0, 1]`` or ``[0, 255]``. A 3-D array with 3 or 4 channels is always
            shown as RGB.
        cmap: Colormap name for intensity data.
        vmin: Lower colour limit for intensity data.
        vmax: Upper colour limit for intensity data.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        robust: Use the 2nd/98th percentiles when no limits or ``norm`` are given.
        rgb: Treat ``data`` as a colour image.
        stretch: Contrast-stretch each RGB channel to its 2nd/98th percentiles.
        title: Axes title.
        interpolation: Passed to :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.imshow`.
        origin: Passed to :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.imshow`.
        overlay_contour: Mask of shape ``(H, W)``; its 0.5 contour is drawn on top.
        contour_color: Colour of the overlay contour.
        contour_linewidth: Line width of the overlay contour in points.
        frame: Draw a thin box on all four sides; otherwise no spines.
        **imshow_kw: Forwarded to :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.imshow`.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, image)``: the axes and the :class:`~matplotlib.image.AxesImage` of
        intensity data (for a colorbar), or ``None`` for RGB data.
    """
    if ax is None:
        _, ax = subplots()
    th = get_theme()
    if rgb or (np.ndim(data) == 3 and np.asarray(data).shape[-1] in (3, 4)):
        img = (
            _stretch_rgb(data)
            if stretch
            else np.clip(np.asarray(data, float) / (255.0 if np.nanmax(data) > 1.5 else 1.0), 0, 1)
        )
        ax.imshow(img, interpolation=interpolation, origin=origin, aspect="equal", **imshow_kw)
        mappable = None
    else:
        if robust and vmin is None and vmax is None and norm is None:
            vmin, vmax = robust_limits(data)
        kw = dict(cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), interpolation=interpolation, origin=origin, aspect="equal")
        if norm is not None:
            kw["norm"] = norm
        else:
            kw["vmin"], kw["vmax"] = vmin, vmax
        mappable = ax.imshow(data, **kw, **imshow_kw)
    if overlay_contour is not None:
        ax.contour(
            np.asarray(overlay_contour, dtype=float),
            levels=[0.5],
            colors=contour_color,
            linewidths=contour_linewidth,
        )
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    # Symmetric spines: a thin box on all four sides, or none at all — never the
    # theme's asymmetric top/right-off look, which reads oddly around an image.
    for sp in ax.spines.values():
        sp.set_visible(frame)
        if frame:
            sp.set_linewidth(0.5)
            sp.set_color("#888888")
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=th.fs_title, pad=2.5)
    return ax, mappable

def overlay_grid(
    ax: Axes,
    values: ArrayLike,
    *,
    window: tuple[int, int, int],
    cmap: str = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    alpha: float = 0.6,
    mask_below: float | None = None,
    outline: bool = True,
    outline_color: str = "white",
    outline_linewidth: float = 0.6,
) -> AxesImage:
    """Overlay a coarse ``(h, w)`` grid of values on a square window of an image.

    The grid is stretched over image pixels ``[row, row + size)`` x ``[col, col + size)``
    of the image already on ``ax`` (pixel-centre coordinates, as :func:`image` draws it),
    so grid cell ``(i, j)`` covers ``size / h`` x ``size / w`` image pixels. The axes
    limits are left as they were.

    Args:
        ax: Axes holding the image.
        values: Grid of shape ``(h, w)``; NaN cells are transparent.
        window: ``(row, col, size)`` of the window, in image pixels.
        cmap: Colormap name of the grid.
        vmin: Lower colour limit of the grid.
        vmax: Upper colour limit of the grid.
        alpha: Opacity of the grid.
        mask_below: Cells with values at or below this are transparent.
        outline: Draw the window's frame.
        outline_color: Frame colour.
        outline_linewidth: Frame line width in points.

    Returns:
        The grid's ``AxesImage``.
    """
    import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

    row, col, size = window
    grid = np.ma.masked_invalid(np.asarray(values, dtype=float))
    if mask_below is not None:
        grid = np.ma.masked_where(grid <= mask_below, grid)
    xlim, ylim = ax.get_xlim(), ax.get_ylim()
    extent = (col - 0.5, col + size - 0.5, row + size - 0.5, row - 0.5)
    im = ax.imshow(
        grid,
        cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap),
        vmin=vmin,
        vmax=vmax,
        alpha=alpha,
        extent=extent,
        interpolation="nearest",
        zorder=3,
    )
    if outline:
        ax.add_patch(
            mpatches.Rectangle(
                (col - 0.5, row - 0.5),
                size,
                size,
                fill=False,
                edgecolor=outline_color,
                linewidth=outline_linewidth,
                zorder=4,
            )
        )
    ax.set_xlim(xlim)
    ax.set_ylim(ylim)
    return im

def pca_rgb(
    field: ArrayLike,
    *,
    basis: PCABasis | tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None = None,
    percentile: tuple[float, float] = (2, 98),
    return_basis: bool = False,
) -> np.ndarray | tuple[np.ndarray, PCABasis]:
    """Map a multi-channel field to RGB through its first three principal components.

    Each component is scaled to ``[0, 1]`` between its ``percentile`` limits and
    mapped to R, G, B.

    Args:
        field: Array of shape ``(..., D)`` with ``D >= 3``, e.g. ``(H, W, D)``.
        basis: Reuse a projection. A ``(mean, components, limits)`` basis from
            ``return_basis=True`` colours several fields identically; a
            ``(mean, components)`` pair reuses the projection but rescales each
            field to its own percentiles. ``None`` fits the PCA on ``field``.
        percentile: Lower/upper percentiles mapped to 0 and 1.
        return_basis: Also return the ``(mean, components, limits)`` basis.

    Returns:
        RGB array of shape ``field.shape[:-1] + (3,)``, or ``(rgb, basis)`` when
        ``return_basis``.
    """
    arr = np.asarray(field, dtype=float)
    lead = arr.shape[:-1]
    flat = arr.reshape(-1, arr.shape[-1])
    limits = None
    if basis is None:
        mean = flat.mean(0)
        comps = np.linalg.svd(flat - mean, full_matrices=False)[2][:3]
    elif len(basis) == 2:
        mean, comps = basis
    else:
        mean, comps, limits = basis[0], basis[1], np.asarray(basis[2], dtype=float)
    proj = (flat - mean) @ comps.T  # (N, 3)
    if limits is None:
        limits = np.stack([np.nanpercentile(proj[:, c], percentile) for c in range(3)])
    out = np.clip((proj - limits[:, 0]) / np.maximum(limits[:, 1] - limits[:, 0], 1e-9), 0, 1)
    rgb = out.reshape(*lead, 3)
    return (rgb, (mean, comps, limits)) if return_basis else rgb

def heatmap(
    matrix: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    row_labels: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    col_labels: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    cmap: str = "Spectral_r",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    annotate: bool = False,
    annot_fmt: str = "{:.2f}",
    annot_size: float | None = None,
    grid: bool = True,
    title: str = "",
) -> tuple[Axes, AxesImage]:
    """Draw a labelled heatmap of a 2-D matrix, optionally annotating each cell.

    Args:
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        matrix: Values of shape ``(rows, cols)``; NaN cells are left blank.
        row_labels: Tick labels for the rows.
        col_labels: Tick labels for the columns, rotated 45°.
        cmap: Colormap name.
        vmin: Lower colour limit.
        vmax: Upper colour limit.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        annotate: Write each value in its cell, in black or white by cell luminance.
        annot_fmt: :meth:`str.format` pattern for annotations.
        annot_size: Annotation size in points; defaults to the theme's annotation size.
        grid: Separate cells with thin white lines.
        title: Axes title.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, image)``: the axes and the drawn :class:`~matplotlib.image.AxesImage`.
    """
    if ax is None:
        _, ax = subplots()
    th = get_theme()
    matrix = np.asarray(matrix, dtype=float)
    kw = dict(cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), aspect="auto")
    if norm is not None:
        kw["norm"] = norm
    else:
        kw["vmin"], kw["vmax"] = vmin, vmax
    im = ax.imshow(matrix, **kw)
    nr, nc = matrix.shape
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(nc))
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(nr))
    if col_labels is not None:
        ax.set_xticklabels(col_labels, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=th.fs_tick)
    if row_labels is not None:
        ax.set_yticklabels(row_labels, fontsize=th.fs_tick)
    ax.tick_params(length=0)
    for sp in ax.spines.values():
        sp.set_visible(False)
    if grid:
        ax.set_xticks(np.arange(-0.5, nc, 1), minor=True)
        ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-0.5, nr, 1), minor=True)
        ax.grid(which="minor", color="white", linewidth=0.6)
        ax.tick_params(which="minor", length=0)
    if annotate:
        fs = annot_size or th.fs_annot
        for i in range(nr):
            for j in range(nc):
                v = matrix[i, j]
                if not np.isfinite(v):
                    continue
                r, g, b, _ = im.cmap(im.norm(v))
                lum = 0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b
                ax.text(
                    j,
                    i,
                    annot_fmt.format(v),
                    ha="center",
                    va="center",
                    fontsize=fs,
                    color="white" if lum < 0.55 else "#222222",
                )
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=th.fs_title, pad=3)
    return ax, im

def image_grid(
    images: Sequence[ArrayLike],
    *,
    nrows: int | None = None,
    ncols: int | None = None,
    cmap: str = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    robust: bool = True,
    rgb: bool = False,
    stretch: bool = False,
    shared_scale: bool = True,
    colorbar_mode: Literal["single", "row", "each", "none"] = "single",
    colorbar_label: str = "",
    titles: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    row_labels: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    col_labels: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    width: str | float = "full",
    panel_aspect: float = 1.0,
    wspace: float = 0.06,
    hspace: float = 0.1,
    fig: Figure | None = None,
) -> tuple[Figure, np.ndarray]:
    """Lay out images in a grid, with one, per-row, per-image or no colorbars.

    Args:
        images: 2-D intensity or 3-D RGB arrays, filled row by row.
        nrows: Number of rows; inferred (near-square grid) if omitted.
        ncols: Number of columns; inferred if omitted.
        cmap: Colormap name for intensity images.
        vmin: Lower colour limit; overrides the shared scale.
        vmax: Upper colour limit; overrides the shared scale.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        robust: Base the shared scale on the 2nd/98th percentiles, not min/max.
        rgb: Treat every image as a colour image.
        stretch: Contrast-stretch RGB images, as in :func:`image`.
        shared_scale: Use one colour range across all intensity images.
        colorbar_mode: ``"single"`` (one bar for the grid), ``"row"`` (one per
            row), ``"each"`` (one per image) or ``"none"``.
        colorbar_label: Label of every colorbar.
        titles: Per-image titles.
        row_labels: Labels left of the first column.
        col_labels: Labels above the first row.
        width: Figure width, a named width or inches (see :func:`nicefigs.figure_size`).
        panel_aspect: Height / width of each panel.
        wspace: Horizontal gap between panels, as a fraction of panel width.
        hspace: Vertical gap between panels, as a fraction of panel height.
        fig: Existing figure to draw into; a new one is created if ``None``.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, axes)`` with ``axes`` a ``(nrows, ncols)`` object array; cells
        beyond ``len(images)`` are switched off.
    """
    from .figure import figure_size
    from .style import style

    th = get_theme()
    n = len(images)
    if nrows is None and ncols is None:
        ncols = int(np.ceil(np.sqrt(n)))
        nrows = int(np.ceil(n / ncols))
    elif ncols is None:
        ncols = int(np.ceil(n / nrows))
    elif nrows is None:
        nrows = int(np.ceil(n / ncols))

    if shared_scale and not rgb and norm is None and vmin is None and vmax is None:
        allv = np.concatenate([np.asarray(im, float).ravel() for im in images])
        vmin, vmax = robust_limits(allv) if robust else (float(np.nanmin(allv)), float(np.nanmax(allv)))

    size = figure_size(width, panel_aspect=panel_aspect, nrows=nrows, ncols=ncols)
    with style(th):
        if fig is None:
            fig = plt.figure(figsize=size, dpi=th.dpi)
        axes = np.empty((nrows, ncols), dtype=object)
        mappables = np.empty((nrows, ncols), dtype=object)
        gs = fig.add_gridspec(nrows, ncols, wspace=wspace, hspace=hspace)
        for k in range(nrows * ncols):
            i, j = divmod(k, ncols)
            ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, j])
            axes[i, j] = ax
            if k < n:
                _, m = image(
                    images[k],
                    cmap=cmap,
                    vmin=vmin,
                    vmax=vmax,
                    norm=norm,
                    rgb=rgb,
                    stretch=stretch,
                    title=(titles[k] if titles is not None and k < len(titles) else ""),
                    ax=ax,
                )
                mappables[i, j] = m
                if colorbar_mode == "each" and m is not None:
                    colorbar(m, ax, label=colorbar_label, thickness=0.02)
            else:
                ax.axis("off")
            if row_labels is not None and j == 0 and i < len(row_labels):
                ax.set_ylabel(row_labels[i], fontsize=th.fs_axis_label)
            if col_labels is not None and i == 0 and j < len(col_labels):
                ax.set_title(col_labels[j], fontsize=th.fs_axis_label, pad=3)

        valid = [m for m in mappables.ravel() if m is not None]
        if colorbar_mode == "single" and valid:
            colorbar(valid[0], list(axes.ravel()), label=colorbar_label, location="right")
        elif colorbar_mode == "row":
            for i in range(nrows):
                row_m = [m for m in mappables[i] if m is not None]
                if row_m:
                    colorbar(row_m[0], list(axes[i]), label=colorbar_label, location="right")
    return fig, axes

def component_panel(
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike,
    values: ArrayLike,
    *,
    chips: ArrayLike | None = None,
    overlays: ArrayLike | None = None,
    window: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
    hist_edges: ArrayLike | None = None,
    hist_counts: ArrayLike | None = None,
    text: Sequence[str] = (),
    label: str = "",
    title: str = "",
    map_label: str = "",
    cmap: str | Colormap = "inferno",
    overlay_cmap: str | Colormap = "inferno",
    overlay_alpha: float = 0.6,
    overlay_mask_below: float | None = None,
    extra_rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]] = (),
    width: float | str = "full",
    fig: Figure | None = None,
) -> tuple[Figure, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Draw the atlas panel of one component.

    Top row: a Robinson map of ``values`` at ``lon``/``lat``, the histogram given by
    ``hist_edges``/``hist_counts``, and a text box (``text`` lines, then the label
    slot, left blank as ``label: ____`` when ``label`` is empty). Bottom row: one
    axes per chip, its RGB stretched per chip, with ``overlays[i]`` drawn over
    ``window`` by :func:`nicefigs.overlay_grid` on one shared colour scale.

    Args:
        lon: ``(n,)`` longitudes in degrees east.
        lat: ``(n,)`` latitudes in degrees north.
        values: ``(n,)`` values of the component at those locations.
        chips: ``(m, H, W, 3)`` RGB chips; ``None`` draws no bottom row.
        overlays: ``(m, h, w)`` coarse grids, one per chip.
        window: ``(row, col, size)`` of the overlaid window in chip pixels; required
            with ``overlays``.
        hist_edges: Histogram bin edges, as returned by :func:`numpy.histogram`.
        hist_counts: Histogram counts, as returned by :func:`numpy.histogram`.
        text: Lines for the text box; wrapped to fit, shrinking the font if needed.
        label: The component's short label.
        title: Panel title, above the map.
        map_label: Colorbar label of the map.
        cmap: Colormap of the map.
        overlay_cmap: Colormap of the overlays.
        overlay_alpha: Opacity of the overlays.
        overlay_mask_below: Overlay cells at or below this value are transparent.
        extra_rows: Further chip rows below the first, each a dict with ``chips``,
            optional ``overlays`` (one per chip, needs ``window``) and optional ``title``
            (shown above the row's first chip).
        width: Figure width (inches or a :data:`nicefigs.figure.WIDTHS` name).
        fig: Draw into this figure instead of a new one.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, axes)``, ``axes`` a dict with ``map``, ``hist``, ``text``, the list ``chips``
        and ``extra_rows`` (one list of axes per extra row).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``overlays`` come without a ``window`` or not one per chip.
    """
    n_chips = 0 if chips is None else len(chips)
    for c, o in [(chips, overlays)] + [(r["chips"], r.get("overlays")) for r in extra_rows]:
        if o is not None:
            if window is None:
                raise ValueError("overlays need the chip window they cover")
            if len(o) != (0 if c is None else len(c)):
                raise ValueError(f"{len(o)} overlays for {0 if c is None else len(c)} chips")
    th = get_theme()
    with style(th):
        if fig is None:
            aspect = (0.62 if n_chips else 0.42) + 0.2 * len(extra_rows)
            fig = plt.figure(figsize=figure_size(width, aspect=aspect), dpi=th.dpi)
        heights = [1.0] + ([0.62] if n_chips else []) + [0.62] * len(extra_rows)
        gs = fig.add_gridspec(len(heights), 12, height_ratios=heights, hspace=0.12, wspace=0.25)
        _, ax_map, _ = world_map(
            lon,
            lat,
            values,
            ax=None,
            fig=fig,
            subplot_spec=gs[0, 0:7],
            kind="scatter",
            cmap=cmap,
            inset_hist=False,
            cbar=True,
            colorbar_label=map_label,
            size=3.0,
        )
        if title:
            clean_title(ax_map, title)
        side = gs[0, 9:12].subgridspec(2, 1, height_ratios=[1.0, 1.0], hspace=0.35)
        ax_hist = fig.add_subplot(side[0])
        if hist_edges is not None and len(hist_edges):
            ax_hist.stairs(hist_counts, hist_edges, fill=True, color=COLORS["primary"], alpha=0.85)
        ax_hist.set_xlabel("value", fontsize=th.fs_axis_label)
        ax_hist.set_ylabel("count", fontsize=th.fs_axis_label)
        ax_hist.tick_params(labelsize=th.fs_tick)
        ax_hist.yaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(3))
        ax_hist.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
            EngFormatter(sep="")
        )  # 20k, not 20000: keeps clear of the map's colorbar
        ax_text = fig.add_subplot(side[1])
        ax_text.axis("off")
        lines = [*text, f"label: {label}" if label else "label: ____________"]
        _fit_text(fig, ax_text, ax_hist, lines, fontsize=th.fs_annot, color=COLORS["neutral"])
        rows = ([{"chips": chips, "overlays": overlays, "title": ""}] if n_chips else []) + list(extra_rows)
        all_overlays = [np.asarray(r["overlays"], float) for r in rows if r.get("overlays") is not None]
        vmax = (
            float(np.nanpercentile(np.concatenate([o.ravel() for o in all_overlays]), 98))
            if all_overlays
            else None
        )
        vmin = 0.0 if all_overlays and min(np.nanmin(o) for o in all_overlays) >= 0 else None
        drawn = []
        for j, row in enumerate(rows):
            span = 12 // max(len(row["chips"]), 1)
            axes_row = []
            for i, chip in enumerate(row["chips"]):
                ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1 + j, i * span : (i + 1) * span])
                image(chip, rgb=True, stretch=True, ax=ax)
                if row.get("overlays") is not None:
                    overlay_grid(
                        ax,
                        row["overlays"][i],
                        window=window,
                        cmap=overlay_cmap,
                        vmin=vmin,
                        vmax=vmax,
                        alpha=overlay_alpha,
                        mask_below=overlay_mask_below,
                    )
                if i == 0 and row.get("title"):
                    ax.set_title(row["title"], fontsize=th.fs_annot, loc="left", pad=2)
                axes_row.append(ax)
            drawn.append(axes_row)
        chip_axes = drawn[0] if n_chips else []
        extra_axes = drawn[1:] if n_chips else drawn
    return fig, {
        "map": ax_map,
        "hist": ax_hist,
        "text": ax_text,
        "chips": chip_axes,
        "extra_rows": extra_axes,
    }

def scatter(
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    color: Any = None,
    hue: ArrayLike | None = None,
    hue_cmap: str = "viridis",
    hue_label: str = "",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    size: ArrayLike | None = None,
    size_range: tuple[float, float] = (8, 120),
    size_label: str = "",
    group: ArrayLike | None = None,
    group_markers: Mapping[Any, str] | None = None,
    group_colors: Mapping[Any, Any] | None = None,
    marker: str = "o",
    alpha: float = 0.85,
    edgecolor: Any = "none",
    linewidth: float = 0.0,
    xerr: ArrayLike | None = None,
    yerr: ArrayLike | None = None,
    point_labels: Sequence[Any] | None = None,
    label_top: int = 0,
    legend: bool = True,
    colorbar: bool = False,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> tuple[Axes, PathCollection | dict[Any, PathCollection]]:
    """Scatter ``y`` against ``x`` with optional shape, size and colour encodings.

    Args:
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        x: Point x coordinates, shape ``(n,)``.
        y: Point y coordinates, shape ``(n,)``.
        color: Single colour for all points; ignored when ``hue`` or ``group`` is set.
        hue: Continuous values, shape ``(n,)``, mapped to colour on ``hue_cmap``.
        hue_cmap: Colormap name for ``hue``.
        hue_label: Colorbar label for ``hue``.
        vmin: Lower ``hue`` colour limit.
        vmax: Upper ``hue`` colour limit.
        size: Continuous values, shape ``(n,)``, mapped to marker area.
        size_range: Marker area range (pt²) that ``size`` is scaled into.
        size_label: Title of the size legend.
        group: Categorical labels, shape ``(n,)``, mapped to marker shape and,
            unless ``hue`` is set, colour.
        group_markers: ``{group: marker}`` overrides; defaults rotate :data:`MARKERS`.
        group_colors: ``{group: colour}`` overrides; defaults to the theme palette.
        marker: Marker shape when ``group`` is not set.
        alpha: Marker opacity.
        edgecolor: Marker edge colour.
        linewidth: Marker edge width (pt).
        xerr: Per-point x error bars, drawn faint behind the markers.
        yerr: Per-point y error bars, drawn faint behind the markers.
        point_labels: Per-point text labels, shape ``(n,)``.
        label_top: Annotate only the ``label_top`` points furthest from the
            centroid with ``point_labels``; ``0`` annotates none.
        legend: Add group and size legends where they apply.
        colorbar: Add a colorbar for ``hue``.
        **kwargs: Forwarded to :meth:`matplotlib.axes.Axes.scatter`.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, artists)``: the axes and the scatter collection, or ``{group: collection}`` when ``group`` is given.
    """
    if ax is None:
        _, ax = subplots()
    th = get_theme()
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    s = _scale_size(size, size_range) if size is not None else None
    s_default = kwargs.pop("s", 36)

    if xerr is not None or yerr is not None:
        ax.errorbar(
            x,
            y,
            xerr=xerr,
            yerr=yerr,
            fmt="none",
            ecolor="#999999",
            elinewidth=0.6,
            capsize=1.2,
            zorder=1,
            alpha=0.7,
        )

    handles = []
    mappable = None

    if group is not None:
        group = np.asarray(group)
        cats = list(dict.fromkeys(group.tolist()))
        gm = group_markers or {c: MARKERS[i % len(MARKERS)] for i, c in enumerate(cats)}
        gc = group_colors or (dict(zip(cats, qualitative(len(cats)))) if hue is None else None)
        colls = {}
        for c in cats:
            m = group == c
            kwc = dict(marker=gm[c], alpha=alpha, edgecolors=edgecolor, linewidths=linewidth)
            kwc["s"] = s[m] if s is not None else s_default
            if hue is not None:
                kwc.update(c=np.asarray(hue)[m], cmap=resolve_cmap(hue_cmap), vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
            else:
                kwc["color"] = gc[c]
            colls[c] = ax.scatter(x[m], y[m], **kwc, **kwargs)
            mappable = colls[c]
            handles.append(
                mlines.Line2D(
                    [],
                    [],
                    color=(gc[c] if gc else th.text_color),
                    marker=gm[c],
                    linestyle="None",
                    markersize=np.sqrt(40),
                    label=str(c),
                )
            )
        result = colls
    else:
        kwc = dict(marker=marker, alpha=alpha, linewidths=linewidth)
        if MarkerStyle(marker).is_filled():  # an unfilled marker ("x", "+") is drawn by its edge colour
            kwc["edgecolors"] = edgecolor
        kwc["s"] = s if s is not None else s_default
        if hue is not None:
            kwc.update(c=np.asarray(hue, dtype=float), cmap=resolve_cmap(hue_cmap), vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)
        else:
            kwc["color"] = color or th.palette[0]
        mappable = ax.scatter(x, y, **kwc, **kwargs)
        result = mappable

    if legend and group is not None:
        leg = ax.legend(
            handles=handles, loc="best", fontsize=th.fs_legend, title=None, handletextpad=0.4, borderpad=0.4
        )
        ax.add_artist(leg)

    if legend and size is not None:
        _add_size_legend(ax, size, size_range, size_label, th)

    if colorbar and hue is not None and mappable is not None:
        from .colorbars import colorbar as _cb

        _cb(mappable, ax, label=hue_label)

    if point_labels is not None and label_top > 0:
        d = np.hypot(x - np.nanmean(x), y - np.nanmean(y))
        for i in np.argsort(d)[::-1][:label_top]:
            ax.annotate(
                str(point_labels[i]),
                (x[i], y[i]),
                fontsize=th.fs_annot,
                xytext=(3, 2),
                textcoords="offset points",
            )

    return ax, result

def agreement(
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    cmap: str = "nice_teal",
    density: str = "kde",
    gridsize: int = 60,
    outlier_z: float = 3.0,
    show_outliers: bool = True,
    one_to_one: bool = True,
    regression: bool = True,
    metrics: bool = True,
    xlabel: str = "Observed",
    ylabel: str = "Predicted",
    units: str | None = None,
    equal: bool = True,
    width: float | str = "half",
    color_line: Any = None,
) -> tuple[Axes, dict[str, float]]:
    """Density agreement plot of predicted ``y`` against observed ``x``.

    Layers a density of the bulk of the cloud, a dashed 1:1 line, outliers as
    faint points, a least-squares fit line and a metrics box (n, R², RMSE, bias).
    Non-finite pairs are dropped.

    Args:
        x: Observed values, shape ``(n,)``.
        y: Predicted values, shape ``(n,)``.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new square figure is created if ``None``.
        cmap: Colormap for the density shading.
        density: ``"kde"`` (gaussian-KDE contours, needs scipy; falls back to
            ``"hexbin"`` for degenerate clouds), ``"hexbin"`` or ``"hist"``.
        gridsize: Grid resolution of the density.
        outlier_z: Points whose residual from the 1:1 line exceeds this many
            robust standard deviations are drawn as points instead of density.
        show_outliers: Draw the outlier points.
        one_to_one: Draw the 1:1 reference line.
        regression: Draw the least-squares fit line.
        metrics: Draw the metrics box.
        xlabel: x-axis label.
        ylabel: y-axis label.
        units: Unit appended to both axis labels.
        equal: Share limits on both axes and force a square aspect.
        width: Figure width (preset name or inches) when ``ax`` is ``None``.
        color_line: Colour of the fit line; defaults to the theme orange.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, stats)`` with ``stats`` keys ``slope``, ``intercept``, ``r2``,
        ``rmse`` and ``bias`` (``y - x``, in data units), and ``n``.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    m = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    x, y = x[m], y[m]

    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=1.0)

    a, b, r2, rmse, bias = _linfit(x, y)

    resid = y - x
    rstd = np.median(np.abs(resid - np.median(resid))) * 1.4826 or resid.std() or 1.0
    is_out = np.abs(resid - np.median(resid)) > outlier_z * rstd
    inl = ~is_out

    cm = resolve_cmap(cmap)
    if density == "kde":
        density = _kde_density(ax, x[inl], y[inl], x, y, cm, gridsize)
    if density == "hexbin":
        ax.hexbin(x[inl], y[inl], gridsize=gridsize, cmap=cm, mincnt=1, linewidths=0, zorder=1)
    elif density == "hist":
        ax.hist2d(x[inl], y[inl], bins=gridsize, cmap=cm, cmin=1, zorder=1)

    if show_outliers and is_out.any():
        ax.scatter(
            x[is_out], y[is_out], s=5, c=COLORS["neutral"], alpha=0.5, linewidths=0, zorder=2, rasterized=True
        )

    lo = min(x.min(), y.min())
    hi = max(x.max(), y.max())
    pad = 0.03 * (hi - lo)
    lim = (lo - pad, hi + pad)
    if one_to_one:
        ax.plot(lim, lim, ls="--", lw=0.8, color=COLORS["neutral"], zorder=3, label="1:1")
    if regression:
        xs = np.array(lim)
        from .artists import NICE_COLORS

        ax.plot(
            xs, a * xs + b, ls="-", lw=1.2, color=color_line or NICE_COLORS["orange"], zorder=4, label="fit"
        )

    if equal:
        ax.set_xlim(*lim)
        ax.set_ylim(*lim)
        ax.set_aspect("equal")

    from .units import axis_label

    ax.set_xlabel(axis_label(xlabel, units))
    ax.set_ylabel(axis_label(ylabel, units))

    stats = dict(
        slope=float(a), intercept=float(b), r2=float(r2), rmse=float(rmse), bias=float(bias), n=int(x.size)
    )
    if metrics:
        txt = f"n = {stats['n']}\nR² = {fmt_val(r2)}\nRMSE = {fmt_val(rmse)}\nbias = {fmt_val(bias)}"
        ax.text(
            0.04,
            0.96,
            txt,
            transform=ax.transAxes,
            va="top",
            ha="left",
            fontsize=th.fs_annot,
            linespacing=1.35,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.35", fc="white", ec="#cccccc", lw=0.4, alpha=0.85),
        )
    return ax, stats

def timeseries(
    dates: Sequence[Any] | ArrayLike,
    series: Mapping[str, ArrayLike] | ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    bands: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    colors: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    styles: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    linewidth: float | None = None,
    obs: tuple[Any, ArrayLike] | Mapping[str, tuple[Any, ArrayLike]] | None = None,
    obs_label: str = "obs",
    obs_color: Any = "#222222",
    obs_size: float = 9,
    obs_marker: str = "x",
    obs_hue: ArrayLike | Mapping[str, ArrayLike] | None = None,
    obs_cmap: str = "viridis",
    obs_vmin: float | None = None,
    obs_vmax: float | None = None,
    obs_hue_label: str = "",
    obs_colorbar: bool = False,
    annotation: str = "",
    ylabel: str = "",
    yunits: str | None = None,
    xlabel: str = "",
    title: str = "",
    legend: bool = True,
    highlight: str | None = None,
    marker: str | None = None,
    width: float | str = "full",
    aspect: float = 0.4,
    band_alpha: float = 0.18,
) -> Axes:
    """Plot named series against ``dates`` on a date axis sized to the span.

    Args:
        dates: Shared ``datetime``/``date``/``datetime64`` x values.
        series: ``{name: values}``, or a single array for one unnamed series.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        bands: ``{name: (lower, upper)}`` for one uncertainty band, or
            ``{name: [(lo1, hi1), (lo2, hi2), ...]}`` for nested bands. Nested
            bands are drawn widest first with opacity rising toward the centre,
            in any input order.
        colors: ``{name: colour}``; defaults to the theme palette.
        styles: ``{name: linestyle}``.
        linewidth: Line width (pt); defaults to the theme's.
        obs: Sparse observations drawn as markers, ``(dates, values)`` or
            ``{label: (dates, values)}``.
        obs_label: Legend label when ``obs`` is a single tuple.
        obs_color: Marker colour of ``obs`` without ``obs_hue``.
        obs_size: Marker area of ``obs`` (pt²).
        obs_marker: Marker shape of ``obs``.
        obs_hue: Continuous values colouring the ``obs`` markers on ``obs_cmap``;
            an array for a single ``obs`` tuple, or ``{label: values}`` matching
            an ``obs`` mapping.
        obs_cmap: Colormap for ``obs_hue``.
        obs_vmin: Lower ``obs_hue`` colour limit.
        obs_vmax: Upper ``obs_hue`` colour limit.
        obs_hue_label: Colorbar label for ``obs_hue``.
        obs_colorbar: Add a colorbar for ``obs_hue``.
        annotation: Text box in the upper-left corner.
        ylabel: y-axis label.
        yunits: Units appended to ``ylabel``.
        xlabel: x-axis label.
        title: Left-aligned panel title.
        legend: Add a legend when there is more than one labelled entry.
        highlight: Name of a series to draw thicker and on top.
        marker: Marker shape on the series lines.
        width: Figure width (preset name or inches) when ``ax`` is ``None``.
        aspect: Figure height / width when ``ax`` is ``None``.
        band_alpha: Opacity of a single band; the innermost of nested bands.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    if not isinstance(series, Mapping):
        series = {"series": np.asarray(series)}
    names = list(series)
    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=aspect)
    cols = colors or dict(zip(names, qualitative(len(names))))
    styles = styles or {}
    lw = linewidth if linewidth is not None else th.lw_line

    for name in names:
        vals = np.asarray(series[name], dtype=float)
        is_hi = name == highlight
        ax.plot(
            dates,
            vals,
            color=cols[name],
            lw=lw * (1.4 if is_hi else 1.0),
            linestyle=styles.get(name, "-"),
            zorder=(5 if is_hi else 3),
            label=name,
            marker=marker,
            markersize=3 if marker else 0,
        )
        if bands and name in bands:
            raw = bands[name]
            band_list = raw if isinstance(raw, list) else [raw]
            band_list = sorted(
                band_list,
                key=lambda b: float(np.nanmax(np.asarray(b[1], dtype=float) - np.asarray(b[0], dtype=float))),
                reverse=True,
            )
            n_bands = len(band_list)
            for bi, (lo, hi) in enumerate(band_list):
                a = band_alpha * (bi + 1) / n_bands if n_bands > 1 else band_alpha
                ax.fill_between(dates, lo, hi, color=cols[name], alpha=a, linewidth=0, zorder=1)

    proxy_handles = []
    if obs is not None:
        obs_map = obs if isinstance(obs, Mapping) else {obs_label: obs}
        hue_map = (
            {}
            if obs_hue is None
            else (obs_hue if isinstance(obs_hue, Mapping) else {next(iter(obs_map)): obs_hue})
        )
        # 'x' markers read cleanly against the model lines; thin stroke, no fill.
        lw = 0.7 if obs_marker in ("x", "+", ".", "1", "2") else 0
        hue_mappable = None
        for label, (odates, ovals) in obs_map.items():
            hue_vals = hue_map.get(label)
            if hue_vals is not None:
                # Per-point colour would give the legend a meaningless swatch, so draw
                # unlabelled and add one neutral proxy handle. scatter() casts x to
                # float, which datetimes reject, hence date2num.
                _, hue_mappable = _scatter(
                    mdates.date2num(odates),
                    np.asarray(ovals, dtype=float),
                    hue=hue_vals,
                    hue_cmap=obs_cmap,
                    hue_label=obs_hue_label,
                    vmin=obs_vmin,
                    vmax=obs_vmax,
                    s=obs_size,
                    marker=obs_marker,
                    alpha=0.8,
                    edgecolor="none",
                    linewidth=lw,
                    zorder=6,
                    legend=False,
                    ax=ax,
                )
                proxy_handles.append(
                    mlines.Line2D(
                        [],
                        [],
                        color=th.text_color,
                        marker=obs_marker,
                        linestyle="None",
                        markersize=np.sqrt(obs_size),
                        label=label,
                    )
                )
            else:
                ax.scatter(
                    odates,
                    np.asarray(ovals, dtype=float),
                    s=obs_size,
                    marker=obs_marker,
                    color=obs_color,
                    alpha=0.8,
                    linewidths=lw,
                    zorder=6,
                    label=label,
                )
        if obs_colorbar and hue_mappable is not None:
            from .colorbars import colorbar as _cb

            _cb(hue_mappable, ax, label=obs_hue_label)

    _format_date_axis(ax, dates)
    if xlabel:
        ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_ylabel(axis_label(ylabel, yunits) if ylabel else "")
    if title:
        from .panels import clean_title

        clean_title(ax, title)
    if annotation:
        ax.text(
            0.02,
            0.97,
            annotation,
            transform=ax.transAxes,
            va="top",
            ha="left",
            fontsize=th.fs_annot,
            linespacing=1.3,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec="#cccccc", lw=0.4, alpha=0.85),
        )
    n_lab = len(names) + (0 if obs is None else (len(obs) if isinstance(obs, Mapping) else 1))
    if legend and n_lab > 1:
        if proxy_handles:
            handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
            handles = handles + proxy_handles
            labels = labels + [h.get_label() for h in proxy_handles]
            ax.legend(
                handles=handles,
                labels=labels,
                loc="best",
                fontsize=th.fs_legend,
                ncol=min(n_lab, 3),
                handlelength=1.2,
                columnspacing=1.0,
            )
        else:
            ax.legend(
                loc="best", fontsize=th.fs_legend, ncol=min(n_lab, 3), handlelength=1.2, columnspacing=1.0
            )
    ax.margins(x=0.01)
    return ax

def lines(
    x: ArrayLike | Mapping[str, ArrayLike],
    series: Mapping[str, ArrayLike],
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    colors: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    styles: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    bands: Mapping[str, tuple[ArrayLike, ArrayLike]] | None = None,
    markers: str | Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    logx: bool = False,
    logy: bool = False,
    logx_base: float = 10,
    baselines: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    baseline_colors: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    xlabel: str = "",
    ylabel: str = "",
    xunits: str | None = None,
    yunits: str | None = None,
    xdirection: str | None = None,
    ydirection: str | None = None,
    title: str = "",
    legend: bool = True,
    band_alpha: float = 0.16,
    width: float | str = "half",
    aspect: float = 0.72,
) -> Axes:
    """Plot named series against a numeric ``x``.

    Use :func:`nicefigs.timeseries` when ``x`` holds dates.

    Args:
        x: Shared x values, or ``{name: x}`` for per-series x.
        series: ``{name: y}``, one line per entry.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        colors: ``{name: colour}``; defaults to the theme palette.
        styles: ``{name: linestyle}``, a second encoding beside colour.
        bands: ``{name: (lower, upper)}`` uncertainty shading.
        markers: One marker for all series, or ``{name: marker}``.
        logx: Log-scale the x-axis.
        logy: Log-scale the y-axis.
        logx_base: Base of the log x-axis (e.g. ``2``).
        baselines: ``{label: y}`` labelled horizontal reference lines.
        baseline_colors: ``{label: colour}`` for ``baselines``; defaults to greys.
        xlabel: x-axis label.
        ylabel: y-axis label.
        xunits: Unit appended to ``xlabel``.
        yunits: Unit appended to ``ylabel``.
        xdirection: ``"lower_better"`` or ``"higher_better"``; adds an arrow to ``xlabel``.
        ydirection: ``"lower_better"`` or ``"higher_better"``; adds an arrow to ``ylabel``.
        title: Left-aligned panel title.
        legend: Add a legend when there is more than one series.
        band_alpha: Opacity of ``bands``.
        width: Figure width (preset name or inches) when ``ax`` is ``None``.
        aspect: Figure height / width when ``ax`` is ``None``.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    names = list(series)
    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=aspect)
    cols = colors or dict(zip(names, qualitative(len(names))))
    styles = styles or {}
    xmap = x if isinstance(x, Mapping) else None

    for name in names:
        xs = np.asarray(xmap[name] if xmap else x, dtype=float)
        ys = np.asarray(series[name], dtype=float)
        mk = markers.get(name) if isinstance(markers, dict) else markers
        ax.plot(
            xs,
            ys,
            color=cols[name],
            linestyle=styles.get(name, "-"),
            lw=th.lw_line,
            marker=mk,
            markersize=3.5 if mk else 0,
            label=name,
            zorder=3,
        )
        if bands and name in bands:
            lo, hi = bands[name]
            ax.fill_between(xs, lo, hi, color=cols[name], alpha=band_alpha, linewidth=0, zorder=1)

    if logx:
        ax.set_xscale("log", base=logx_base)
    if logy:
        ax.set_yscale("log")

    if baselines:
        from .panels import reference_line

        bc = baseline_colors or {}
        for i, (label, val) in enumerate(baselines.items()):
            reference_line(
                ax,
                val,
                axis="y",
                label=label,
                fmt="{label} ({value:.3g})",
                color=bc.get(label, ["#888888", "#aaaaaa", "#666666"][i % 3]),
                linestyle=":",
            )

    if xlabel:
        ax.set_xlabel(axis_label(xlabel, xunits, direction=xdirection))
    if ylabel:
        ax.set_ylabel(axis_label(ylabel, yunits, direction=ydirection))
    if title:
        from .panels import clean_title

        clean_title(ax, title)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.15, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    if legend and len(names) > 1:
        ax.legend(loc="best", fontsize=th.fs_legend)
    return ax

    eigenvalues: ArrayLike | Sequence[ArrayLike] | Mapping[str, ArrayLike],
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    labels: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    colors: Mapping[str, Any] | Sequence[Any] | None = None,

    normalize: bool = True,
    rtol: float = 1e-10,
    cumulative: bool = False,
    thresholds: Sequence[float] = (0.5, 0.9, 0.99),
    reference_alpha: float | None = None,

    ``normalize``. With ``cumulative=True`` it draws the cumulative
    explained-variance fraction on a log rank axis instead, with one labelled
    horizontal guide per threshold and, for each series, a marker where it
    first reaches that threshold. Each spectrum is sorted descending, and its
    non-finite, non-positive and round-off-sized (``λ ≤ rtol · λ_max``)

            :func:`~nicefigs.qualitative`.
        styles: ``{name: linestyle}``.
        normalize: Plot ``λ_k / Σλ`` instead of ``λ_k``; ignored when ``cumulative``.
        rtol: Relative floor below which eigenvalues count as numerical zeros;
            ``0`` keeps every positive eigenvalue.
        cumulative: Plot ``Σ_{j≤k} λ_j / Σλ`` instead of the spectrum.
        thresholds: Explained-variance fractions marked when ``cumulative``.
        reference_alpha: Draw a ``k^-α`` power law through the plotted leading
            value of the first series; spectrum mode only.
        xlabel: x-axis label.
        ylabel: y-axis label; defaults to the plotted quantity.
        title: Panel title.
        legend: Add a legend when more than one line is labelled.
        width: Figure width (preset name or inches) when ``ax`` is ``None``.
        aspect: Figure ``height / width`` when ``ax`` is ``None``.

    Returns:
        The axes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``reference_alpha`` is given with ``cumulative``, a spectrum
            is not 1-D or has no positive eigenvalue, or ``labels`` has the
            wrong length.
    """
    if cumulative and reference_alpha is not None:
        raise ValueError("reference_alpha applies to the spectrum, not cumulative=True")
    spectra = _as_named_spectra(eigenvalues, labels, rtol)
    names = list(spectra)
    if colors is None:
        colors = dict(zip(names, qualitative(len(names))))
    elif not isinstance(colors, Mapping):
        colors = dict(zip(names, colors))

    if cumulative:
        series = {n: np.cumsum(ev) / ev.sum() for n, ev in spectra.items()}
        default_ylabel = "cumulative explained variance"
    elif normalize:
        series = {n: ev / ev.sum() for n, ev in spectra.items()}
        default_ylabel = r"$\lambda_k / \sum \lambda$"
    else:
        series = spectra
        default_ylabel = r"$\lambda_k$"
    ranks = {n: np.arange(1, len(y) + 1) for n, y in series.items()}

    ax = lines(
        ranks,
        series,
        ax=ax,
        colors=colors,
        styles=styles,
        logx=True,
        logy=not cumulative,
        xlabel=xlabel,
        ylabel=default_ylabel if ylabel is None else ylabel,
        title=title,
        legend=False,
        width=width,
        aspect=aspect,
    )

    if cumulative:
        _mark_thresholds(ax, ranks, series, colors, thresholds)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02)
    elif reference_alpha is not None:
        k = np.geomspace(1, max(len(r) for r in ranks.values()), 50)
        lead = series[names[0]][0]  # the plotted value at k = 1, normalised or not
        ax.plot(
            k,
            lead * k ** -float(reference_alpha),
            label=f"$k^{{-{reference_alpha:g}}}$",
            **role_style("reference", kind="line"),
        )

    if legend and len([lbl for lbl in ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1] if lbl]) > 1:
        ax.legend(loc="best")
    return ax

def model_comparison(
    scores: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    models: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    metrics: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    groups: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    group_label: str = "",
    kind: str = "violin",
    ncols: int | None = None,
    metric_units: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    metric_lims: Mapping[str, tuple[float, float]] | None = None,
    model_colors: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    reference: float | Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    reference_label: str = "",
    median_labels: bool = False,
    divider_after: int | None = None,
    width: float | str = "full",
    panel_aspect: float = 0.85,
    group_gap: float = 0.82,
    legend: bool = True,
    sharey: bool = False,
) -> tuple[Figure, np.ndarray]:
    """Grid of metric panels comparing the score distributions of several models.

    Args:
        scores: ``{metric: {model: values}}``, or ``{metric: {model: {group: values}}}``
            to dodge a second factor (e.g. dataset) within each model. Also accepts
            the dict returned by :func:`nicefigs.data.model_scores`.
        models: Model order on the x-axis; inferred if ``None``.
        metrics: Metric (panel) order; inferred if ``None``.
        groups: Group order within each model; inferred if ``None``.
        group_label: Title of the shared group legend.
        kind: ``"violin"``, ``"box"`` or ``"strip"``.
        ncols: Panel columns; defaults to one row for up to three metrics.
        metric_units: ``{metric: unit}`` shown as the y-axis label.
        metric_lims: ``{metric: (lo, hi)}`` y-limits.
        model_colors: ``{model: colour}``; colours by model instead of by group.
        reference: Reference line value, one for all panels or ``{metric: value}``.
        reference_label: Label of the reference line; defaults to its value.
        median_labels: Annotate each distribution with its median.
        divider_after: Draw a vertical divider after this many models.
        width: Figure width (preset name or inches).
        panel_aspect: Height / width of each panel.
        group_gap: Fraction of the slot per model shared by its groups.
        legend: Add the shared group legend.
        sharey: Share the y-axis across panels.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, axes)`` with ``axes`` a flat array, one per metric; unused grid
        cells are hidden.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``kind`` is not ``"violin"``, ``"box"`` or ``"strip"``.
    """
    if kind not in ("violin", "box", "strip"):
        raise ValueError(f"kind must be 'violin', 'box' or 'strip', got {kind!r}")
    th = get_theme()
    if isinstance(scores, dict) and "scores" in scores and isinstance(scores["scores"], dict):
        meta = scores
        scores = meta["scores"]
        models = models or meta.get("models")
        metrics = metrics or meta.get("metrics")
        groups = groups or meta.get("timescales")

    metrics = metrics or list(scores)
    first_metric = scores[metrics[0]]
    models = models or list(first_metric)

    _, inferred_groups = _as_grouped(first_metric)
    groups = groups if groups is not None else inferred_groups

    n = len(metrics)
    ncols = ncols or (n if n <= 3 else int(np.ceil(np.sqrt(n))))
    nrows = int(np.ceil(n / ncols))

    from .figure import figure_size
    from .style import style

    size = figure_size(width, nrows=nrows, ncols=ncols, panel_aspect=panel_aspect)
    with style(th):
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=size, dpi=th.dpi, squeeze=False, sharey=sharey)
    axes_flat = axes.ravel()

    gcolors = dict(zip(groups, qualitative(len(groups)))) if groups else None
    ng = len(groups) if groups else 1

    for mi, metric in enumerate(metrics):
        ax = axes_flat[mi]
        norm, _ = _as_grouped(scores[metric])
        base = np.arange(len(models))
        for gi, g in enumerate(groups or [""]):
            offset = (gi - (ng - 1) / 2) * (group_gap / ng)
            wdt = (group_gap / ng) * 0.9
            for mj, model in enumerate(models):
                color = (
                    (model_colors or {}).get(model)
                    if model_colors
                    else (gcolors[g] if gcolors else th.palette[0])
                )
                d = norm.get(model, {}).get(g, [])
                _violin(ax, d, base[mj] + offset, color, wdt, kind)
                if median_labels and np.size(d):
                    med = float(np.nanmedian(np.asarray(d, dtype=float)))
                    ax.annotate(
                        f"{med:.2g}",
                        (base[mj] + offset, med),
                        fontsize=th.fs_annot - 0.5,
                        ha="center",
                        va="bottom",
                        xytext=(0, 2),
                        textcoords="offset points",
                    )
        ref = reference.get(metric) if isinstance(reference, dict) else reference
        if ref is not None:
            from .panels import reference_line

            reference_line(
                ax, ref, axis="y", label=reference_label, fmt="{label}" if reference_label else "{value:.2g}"
            )
        if divider_after is not None and 0 < divider_after < len(models):
            ax.axvline(divider_after - 0.5, color="#bbbbbb", linewidth=0.7, linestyle="-", zorder=0)
        ax.set_xticks(base)
        ax.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=30, ha="right", fontsize=th.fs_tick)
        from .units import prettify_unit

        unit = (metric_units or {}).get(metric)
        ax.set_ylabel(prettify_unit(unit) if unit else "", fontsize=th.fs_axis_label)
        ax.set_title(metric, fontsize=th.fs_title, loc="left", pad=3)
        if metric_lims and metric in metric_lims:
            ax.set_ylim(*metric_lims[metric])
        ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.15, linewidth=0.5)
        ax.set_axisbelow(True)

    for k in range(n, len(axes_flat)):
        axes_flat[k].axis("off")

    top = 1.0
    if legend and groups:
        import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

        handles = [
            mpatches.Patch(facecolor=gcolors[g], edgecolor="none", alpha=0.7, label=str(g)) for g in groups
        ]
        leg = fig.legend(
            handles=handles,
            title=group_label or None,
            loc="upper center",
            bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0),
            ncol=len(groups),
            fontsize=th.fs_legend,
            title_fontsize=th.fs_legend,
            frameon=False,
        )
        # Reserve exactly the legend's height so it never overlaps the panel titles.
        bbox = leg.get_window_extent(fig.canvas.get_renderer()).transformed(fig.transFigure.inverted())
        top = bbox.y0 - 0.01
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, top))
    return fig, axes_flat

Ternary encodings: three-part compositions drawn as barycentric blends of corner colours.

def resolve_corners(corners: Corners) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    """Resolve a palette name or three explicit colours to a 3-tuple of colours.

    Raises:
        KeyError: ``corners`` is a name not in :data:`TERNARY_PALETTES`.
        ValueError: ``corners`` is a sequence that is not of length 3.
    """
    if isinstance(corners, str):
        try:
            return TERNARY_PALETTES[corners]
        except KeyError as exc:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown ternary palette {corners!r}. Known: {sorted(TERNARY_PALETTES)}") from exc
    corners = tuple(corners)
    if len(corners) != 3:
        raise ValueError(f"ternary corners must be a name or 3 colours, got {corners!r}")
    return corners

def normalize_composition(comp: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray:
    """Rescale compositions of shape ``(..., 3)`` so each sums to 1; all-zero rows become NaN."""
    c = np.asarray(comp, dtype=float)
    s = c.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        out = np.where(s > 0, c / s, np.nan)
    return out

def color(
    comp: ArrayLike, *, corners: Corners = DEFAULT_CORNERS, gamma: float = 0.8, brighten: float = 1.0
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Colour each composition by barycentric blending of three corner colours.

    Args:
        comp: Compositions of shape ``(..., 3)``, e.g. ``(N, 3)`` or ``(H, W, 3)``;
            normalised to sum to 1.
        corners: Palette name or three colours for components 0, 1, 2.
        gamma: Exponent applied to the blended RGB; values below 1 brighten mixtures.
        brighten: Multiplicative factor applied before ``gamma``, then clipped to 1.

    Returns:
        RGB array of shape ``comp.shape`` (trailing axis of 3) in ``[0, 1]``.
    """
    w = normalize_composition(comp)
    cols = np.array([to_rgb(c) for c in resolve_corners(corners)])  # (3,3)
    rgb = np.tensordot(w, cols, axes=([-1], [0]))  # (..., 3)
    rgb = np.clip(rgb * brighten, 0, 1) ** gamma
    return rgb

def barycentric_to_xy(comp: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray:
    """Map compositions of shape ``(..., 3)`` to ``(x, y)`` positions in the unit-edge triangle.

    Component 0 sits at ``(0, 0)``, 1 at ``(1, 0)`` and 2 at the apex ``(0.5, sqrt(3)/2)``.
    """
    w = normalize_composition(comp)
    return w @ _V

def ternary_axes(
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    *,
    labels: Sequence[str] = ("A", "B", "C"),
    gridlines: int = 5,
    corner_colors: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    fontsize: float | None = None,
) -> Axes:
    """Draw a ternary triangle frame (outline, gridlines, corner labels) on ``ax``.

    Args:
        ax: Axes to draw into; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        labels: Corner labels for components 0, 1, 2.
        gridlines: Number of intervals per edge; ``gridlines - 1`` interior lines
            are drawn parallel to each edge.
        corner_colors: Label colours per corner; dark grey if ``None``.
        fontsize: Label size in points; defaults to the theme's axis-label size.

    Returns:
        The axes, with limits, equal aspect and hidden ticks/spines set.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width="half", aspect=np.sqrt(3) / 2 + 0.12)
    fs = fontsize or th.fs_axis_label
    tri = np.vstack([_V, _V[0]])
    ax.plot(tri[:, 0], tri[:, 1], color="#333333", lw=0.8, zorder=2)
    for k in range(1, gridlines):
        f = k / gridlines
        # lines parallel to each edge
        for i, j, m in ((0, 1, 2), (1, 2, 0), (2, 0, 1)):
            p1 = _V[i] * (1 - f) + _V[m] * f
            p2 = _V[j] * (1 - f) + _V[m] * f
            ax.plot([p1[0], p2[0]], [p1[1], p2[1]], color="#cccccc", lw=0.35, zorder=1)
    ccols = corner_colors or ["#333333"] * 3
    offs = [(-0.02, -0.04, "right", "top"), (0.02, -0.04, "left", "top"), (0.0, 0.03, "center", "bottom")]
    for v, lab, cc, (dx, dy, ha, va) in zip(_V, labels, ccols, offs):
        ax.text(v[0] + dx, v[1] + dy, lab, ha=ha, va=va, fontsize=fs, color=cc, fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_xlim(-0.08, 1.08)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.1, np.sqrt(3) / 2 + 0.1)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    # Hide the frame but keep the background patch (so insets can be given a
    # white backing) — ``axis("off")`` would suppress the patch too.
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    for sp in ax.spines.values():
        sp.set_visible(False)
    return ax

def ternary_scatter(
    comp: ArrayLike,
    values: ArrayLike | None = None,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    corners: Corners = DEFAULT_CORNERS,
    labels: Sequence[str] = ("A", "B", "C"),
    size: float = 10,
    cmap: str = "inferno",
    color_by: Literal["composition", "value"] = "composition",
    **kw: Any,
) -> tuple[Axes, PathCollection | None]:
    """Scatter compositions inside a ternary triangle.

    Args:
        comp: Compositions of shape ``(N, 3)``.
        values: Per-point values of shape ``(N,)``, used when ``color_by="value"``.
        ax: Axes to draw into; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        corners: Palette name or three corner colours.
        labels: Corner labels for components 0, 1, 2.
        size: Marker area in points².
        cmap: Colormap name for ``color_by="value"``.
        color_by: ``"composition"`` colours points by their ternary colour;
            ``"value"`` colours them by ``values`` through ``cmap``.
        **kw: Forwarded to :meth:`matplotlib.axes.Axes.scatter`.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, mappable)``; ``mappable`` is the scatter collection when colouring by
        value (for a colorbar) and ``None`` otherwise.
    """
    ax = ternary_axes(ax, labels=labels, corner_colors=list(resolve_corners(corners)))
    xy = barycentric_to_xy(comp)
    if color_by == "value" and values is not None:
        from .palettes import cmap as resolve_cmap

        sc = ax.scatter(
            xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=np.asarray(values), cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), s=size, linewidths=0, **kw
        )
        return ax, sc
    cols = color(comp, corners=corners)
    ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=cols, s=size, linewidths=0, **kw)
    return ax, None

        ax: Axes to draw into, typically ``parent.inset_axes([...])``; a new
            figure is created if ``None``.
        corners: Palette name or three corner colours.
        labels: Corner labels for components 0, 1, 2.
        n: Raster resolution of the triangle per side.
        gamma: As in :func:`color`.
        points: Optional compositions ``(N, 3)`` overlaid as dots to show where the
            data lie.
        point_kw: Overrides for the overlay's :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.scatter` keywords.
        fontsize: Corner-label size in points.

    Returns:
        The legend axes.
    """
    ax = ternary_axes(ax, labels=labels, corner_colors=list(resolve_corners(corners)), fontsize=fontsize)
    xs = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
    ys = np.linspace(0, np.sqrt(3) / 2, n)
    gx, gy = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    # invert xy -> barycentric
    T = np.array([[_V[0, 0] - _V[2, 0], _V[1, 0] - _V[2, 0]], [_V[0, 1] - _V[2, 1], _V[1, 1] - _V[2, 1]]])
    Tinv = np.linalg.inv(T)
    d = np.stack([gx - _V[2, 0], gy - _V[2, 1]], -1)
    ab = d @ Tinv.T
    a, b = ab[..., 0], ab[..., 1]
    c = 1 - a - b
    inside = (a >= 0) & (b >= 0) & (c >= 0)
    comp = np.stack([a, b, c], -1)
    rgb = color(comp, corners=corners, gamma=gamma)
    img = np.dstack([rgb, inside.astype(float)])
    ax.imshow(img, extent=(0, 1, 0, np.sqrt(3) / 2), origin="lower", interpolation="bilinear", zorder=0)
    if points is not None:
        xy = barycentric_to_xy(points)
        pk = dict(s=3, color="#222222", alpha=0.5, linewidths=0)
        pk.update(point_kw or {})
        ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], zorder=3, **pk)
    return ax

def ternary_image(
    comp_img: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    corners: Corners = DEFAULT_CORNERS,
    labels: Sequence[str] = ("A", "B", "C"),
    inset: bool = True,
    title: str = "",
    gamma: float = 0.8,
) -> Axes:
    """Show a composition image of shape ``(H, W, 3)`` in ternary colours.

    Args:
        comp_img: Per-pixel compositions of shape ``(H, W, 3)``.
        ax: Axes to draw into; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        corners: Palette name or three corner colours.
        labels: Corner labels for the legend.
        inset: Add a ternary legend inset in the top-right corner.
        title: Axes title.
        gamma: As in :func:`color`.

    Returns:
        The image axes.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width="half", aspect=1.0)
    rgb = color(comp_img, corners=corners, gamma=gamma)
    ax.imshow(np.clip(rgb, 0, 1), interpolation="nearest")
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=th.fs_title, pad=2.5)
    if inset:
        iax = ax.inset_axes([0.71, 0.71, 0.29, 0.29])
        iax.set_facecolor("white")
        iax.patch.set_alpha(0.85)
        ternary_legend(iax, corners=corners, labels=labels, gamma=gamma, fontsize=th.fs_annot)
    return ax

def ternary_map(
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike,
    comp: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    corners: Corners = DEFAULT_CORNERS,
    labels: Sequence[str] = ("A", "B", "C"),
    projection: str = "robinson",
    antarctica_cutoff: bool = True,
    extent: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    size: float = 6,
    inset: bool = True,
    land: bool = True,
    coastline: bool = True,
    title: str = "",
    gamma: float = 0.8,
    **kw: Any,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
    """Scatter points on a map, each coloured by its composition.

    Args:
        lon: Longitudes in degrees east, shape ``(N,)``.
        lat: Latitudes in degrees north, shape ``(N,)``.
        comp: Compositions of shape ``(N, 3)``.
        ax: Existing (cartopy) axes; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        corners: Palette name or three corner colours.
        labels: Corner labels for the legend.
        projection: Projection name, as in :func:`nicefigs.make_map_axes`.
        antarctica_cutoff: Crop the southern edge when ``extent`` is ``None``.
        extent: ``(lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max)`` in degrees.
        size: Marker area in points².
        inset: Add a ternary legend inset in the lower-left corner.
        land: Draw the land background.
        coastline: Draw coastlines.
        title: Axes title.
        gamma: As in :func:`color`.
        **kw: Forwarded to :meth:`matplotlib.axes.Axes.scatter`.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, ax)``.
    """
    from .maps import _apply_extent, _try_cartopy, draw_background, make_map_axes

    th = get_theme()
    if ax is None:
        from .figure import figure_size

        fig = plt.figure(figsize=figure_size("full", aspect=0.52), dpi=th.dpi)
        ax, ccrs = make_map_axes(fig, 111, projection=projection)
    else:
        fig = ax.figure
        ccrs = _try_cartopy() if hasattr(ax, "projection") else None
    draw_background(ax, ccrs, land=land, coastline=coastline)
    _apply_extent(ax, ccrs, extent, antarctica_cutoff and extent is None)
    cols = color(comp, corners=corners, gamma=gamma)
    skw = dict(s=size, linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    if ccrs is not None:
        skw["transform"] = ccrs.PlateCarree()
    ax.scatter(np.asarray(lon), np.asarray(lat), c=cols, **skw, **kw)
    if title:
        from .panels import clean_title

        clean_title(ax, title)
    if inset:
        # Lower-left corner of a global map is open ocean, so the inset needs no backing.
        iax = ax.inset_axes([0.03, 0.06, 0.19, 0.19])
        iax.patch.set_alpha(0.0)
        ternary_legend(iax, corners=corners, labels=labels, gamma=gamma, fontsize=th.fs_annot - 0.5)
    return fig, ax

def frontier(
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    *,
    xdirection: str = "lower_better",
    ydirection: str = "higher_better",
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Indices of the Pareto-optimal points of ``(x, y)``, ordered by ``x``.

    A point is optimal iff no other point is at least as good on both axes and
    strictly better on at least one.

    Args:
        x: First objective, shape ``(n,)``.
        y: Second objective, shape ``(n,)``.
        xdirection: ``"lower_better"`` or ``"higher_better"`` for ``x``.
        ydirection: ``"lower_better"`` or ``"higher_better"`` for ``y``.

    Returns:
        Integer index array into ``x``/``y``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: A direction is not ``"lower_better"`` or ``"higher_better"``.
    """
    for d in (xdirection, ydirection):
        if d not in ("lower_better", "higher_better"):
            raise ValueError(f"a Pareto direction must be 'lower_better' or 'higher_better', got {d!r}")
    minimize_x = xdirection == "lower_better"
    maximize_y = ydirection == "higher_better"
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    n = x.size
    keep = np.ones(n, dtype=bool)
    for i in range(n):
        xb = (x <= x[i]) if minimize_x else (x >= x[i])
        yb = (y >= y[i]) if maximize_y else (y <= y[i])
        xs = (x < x[i]) if minimize_x else (x > x[i])
        ys = (y > y[i]) if maximize_y else (y < y[i])
        dominated = xb & yb & (xs | ys)
        dominated[i] = False
        if dominated.any():
            keep[i] = False
    idx = np.where(keep)[0]
    return idx[np.argsort(x[idx])]

def pareto(
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    group: ArrayLike | None = None,
    group_colors: Mapping[Any, Any] | None = None,
    group_markers: Mapping[Any, str] | None = None,
    hue: ArrayLike | None = None,
    hue_cmap: str = "viridis",
    hue2d: tuple[ArrayLike, ArrayLike] | None = None,
    cmap2d: str = "flat",
    cmap2d_kwargs: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    size: ArrayLike | None = None,
    size_range: tuple[float, float] = (15, 140),
    xdirection: str = "lower_better",
    ydirection: str = "higher_better",
    frontier: bool = True,
    frontier_per_group: bool = False,
    frontier_kwargs: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    baselines: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    baseline_colors: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    xlabel: str = "",
    ylabel: str = "",
    xunits: str | None = None,
    yunits: str | None = None,
    edgecolor: Any = "white",
    linewidth: float = 0.6,
    legend: bool = True,
    width: float | str = "half",
) -> tuple[Axes, np.ndarray | None]:
    """Scatter a trade-off ``(x, y)`` with its Pareto frontier and optional baselines.

    Args:
        x: First objective, shape ``(n,)``.
        y: Second objective, shape ``(n,)``.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        group: Categorical labels, shape ``(n,)``, mapped to colour and marker.
        group_colors: ``{group: colour}``; defaults to the theme palette.
        group_markers: ``{group: marker}``; defaults rotate :data:`nicefigs.scatter.MARKERS`.
        hue: Continuous values, shape ``(n,)``, coloured on ``hue_cmap`` with a
            colorbar; overrides group colours.
        hue_cmap: Colormap for ``hue``.
        hue2d: Two arrays ``(u, v)``, each shape ``(n,)``, coloured on a 2-D
            colormap; overrides ``hue`` and group colours.
        cmap2d: 2-D colormap for ``hue2d``: ``"flat"``, ``"bivariate"`` or ``"hsv"``.
        cmap2d_kwargs: Forwarded to the 2-D colormap function.
        size: Continuous values, shape ``(n,)``, mapped to marker area.
        size_range: Marker area range (pt²) that ``size`` is scaled into.
        xdirection: ``"lower_better"`` or ``"higher_better"`` for ``x``; sets the
            frontier and the arrow appended to the x-axis label.
        ydirection: As ``xdirection``, for ``y``.
        frontier: Draw the frontier line.
        frontier_per_group: Draw one colour-matched frontier per ``group``
            instead of one for all points.
        frontier_kwargs: Overrides for the frontier :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.plot` style.
        baselines: ``{label: y}`` labelled horizontal reference lines.
        baseline_colors: ``{label: colour}`` for ``baselines``; defaults to greys.
        xlabel: x-axis label.
        ylabel: y-axis label.
        xunits: Unit appended to ``xlabel``.
        yunits: Unit appended to ``ylabel``.
        edgecolor: Marker edge colour.
        linewidth: Marker edge width (pt).
        legend: Add a group legend.
        width: Figure width (preset name or inches) when ``ax`` is ``None``.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, frontier_indices)``; the indices are those of :func:`frontier` for
        all points, or ``None`` when ``frontier`` is off or ``frontier_per_group``.

    Raises:
        KeyError: ``cmap2d`` is not a known 2-D colormap.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=0.85)

    fk = dict(color="#333333", linewidth=1.0, linestyle="--", alpha=0.7, zorder=4)
    fk.update(frontier_kwargs or {})
    sizes = _sizes(size, size_range, x.shape)

    colors2d = None
    if hue2d is not None:
        from .colormaps2d import bivariate_cmap, flat_cmap, hsv_cmap, normalize01

        u, v = hue2d
        u01 = normalize01(u)[0]
        v01 = normalize01(v)[0]
        fn = {"flat": flat_cmap, "bivariate": bivariate_cmap, "hsv": hsv_cmap}[cmap2d]
        colors2d = fn(u01, v01, **(cmap2d_kwargs or {}))

    handles = []
    mappable = None
    if group is not None:
        group = np.asarray(group)
        cats = list(dict.fromkeys(group.tolist()))
        gc = group_colors or dict(zip(cats, qualitative(len(cats))))
        gm = group_markers or {c: MARKERS[i % len(MARKERS)] for i, c in enumerate(cats)}
        for c in cats:
            m = group == c
            ckw = dict(marker=gm[c], edgecolors=edgecolor, linewidths=linewidth, zorder=5)
            if colors2d is not None:
                ax.scatter(x[m], y[m], c=colors2d[m], s=sizes[m], **ckw)
            elif hue is not None:
                mappable = ax.scatter(
                    x[m], y[m], c=np.asarray(hue)[m], cmap=resolve_cmap(hue_cmap), s=sizes[m], **ckw
                )
            else:
                ax.scatter(x[m], y[m], color=gc[c], s=sizes[m], **ckw)
            handles.append(
                mlines.Line2D(
                    [], [], color=gc[c], marker=gm[c], linestyle="None", markersize=np.sqrt(45), label=str(c)
                )
            )
            if frontier and frontier_per_group:
                fi = _compute_frontier(x[m], y[m], xdirection=xdirection, ydirection=ydirection)
                ax.plot(x[m][fi], y[m][fi], **{**fk, "color": gc[c], "alpha": 0.85})
    else:
        ckw = dict(edgecolors=edgecolor, linewidths=linewidth, zorder=5)
        if colors2d is not None:
            ax.scatter(x, y, c=colors2d, s=sizes, **ckw)
        elif hue is not None:
            mappable = ax.scatter(x, y, c=np.asarray(hue), cmap=resolve_cmap(hue_cmap), s=sizes, **ckw)
        else:
            ax.scatter(x, y, color=COLORS["blue"], s=sizes, **ckw)

    front_idx = None
    if frontier and not frontier_per_group:
        front_idx = _compute_frontier(x, y, xdirection=xdirection, ydirection=ydirection)
        ax.plot(x[front_idx], y[front_idx], **fk)

    if baselines:
        bc = baseline_colors or {}
        fallback = ["#888888", "#AAAAAA", "#666666"]
        for i, (label, val) in enumerate(baselines.items()):
            col = bc.get(label, fallback[i % len(fallback)])
            ax.axhline(val, color=col, linestyle=":", linewidth=0.8, zorder=2)
            ax.text(
                0.995,
                val,
                f" {label} ({val:.3g})",
                transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(),
                ha="right",
                va="bottom",
                fontsize=th.fs_annot,
                color=col,
            )

    from .units import axis_label

    xa = axis_label(xlabel, xunits, direction=xdirection)
    ya = axis_label(ylabel, yunits, direction=ydirection)
    if xlabel:
        ax.set_xlabel(xa)
    if ylabel:
        ax.set_ylabel(ya)
    if legend and handles:
        ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="best", fontsize=th.fs_legend)
    if mappable is not None:
        from .colorbars import colorbar

        colorbar(mappable, ax)
    return ax, front_idx
