def caterpillar(
    labels: Sequence[Any],
    values: ArrayLike,
    *,
    err: ArrayLike | None = None,
    lo: ArrayLike | None = None,
    hi: ArrayLike | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    sort_by: str | ArrayLike = "value",
    ascending: bool = True,
    orientation: str = "horizontal",
    groups: ArrayLike | None = None,
    group_colors: Mapping[Any, Any] | None = None,
    color: Any = None,
    baseline: ArrayLike | tuple[ArrayLike, ArrayLike] | None = None,
    baseline_label: str = "baseline",
    baseline_color: Any = COLORS["neutral"],
    offset: float = 0.18,
    ref_line: float | None = 0.0,
    ref_label: str = "",
    summary: tuple[str, float] | None = None,
    value_label: str = "",
    value_units: str | None = None,
    annotate_threshold: float | None = None,
    markersize: float = 4,
    capsize: float = 1.5,
    width: float | str = "half",
    aspect: float | None = None,
    legend: bool = True,
) -> Axes:
    """Ranked per-item value ± error plot.

    Args:
        labels: Item names, one per value.
        values: Central values, shape ``(n,)``.
        err: Symmetric error, shape ``(n,)``; ignored when ``lo`` and ``hi`` are given.
        lo: Explicit lower bounds, shape ``(n,)``.
        hi: Explicit upper bounds, shape ``(n,)``.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        sort_by: ``"value"`` (rank by value), ``"none"`` (input order), or an
            array of sort keys, shape ``(n,)``.
        ascending: Sort order.
        orientation: ``"horizontal"`` (items down y, the forest layout) or
            ``"vertical"`` (items along x).
        groups: Per-item categorical labels, shape ``(n,)``, mapped to colour
            with a legend.
        group_colors: ``{group: colour}``; defaults to the theme palette.
        color: Point colour without ``groups``.
        baseline: A second series, ``values`` or ``(values, err)``, drawn offset
            beside each item.
        baseline_label: Legend label of ``baseline``.
        baseline_color: Colour of ``baseline``.
        offset: Offset between the series and ``baseline``, in item slots.
        ref_line: Reference line value; ``None`` omits it.
        ref_label: Text placed in the corner to name ``ref_line``.
        summary: ``(name, value)`` shown as a headline annotation.
        value_label: Value-axis label.
        value_units: Unit appended to ``value_label``.
        annotate_threshold: Label items whose ``|value|`` is at least this.
        markersize: Point size (pt).
        capsize: Error-bar cap length (pt).
        width: Figure width (preset name or inches) when ``ax`` is ``None``.
        aspect: Figure height / width when ``ax`` is ``None``; scales with the
            item count by default.
        legend: Add a legend when ``groups`` or ``baseline`` is set.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    labels = list(labels)
    values, low, high = _resolve_bounds(values, err, lo, hi)
    n = len(labels)

    if isinstance(sort_by, str):
        if sort_by == "value":
            order = np.argsort(values)
            if not ascending:
                order = order[::-1]
        else:
            order = np.arange(n)
    else:
        order = np.argsort(np.asarray(sort_by))
        if not ascending:
            order = order[::-1]

    labels = [labels[i] for i in order]
    values, low, high = values[order], low[order], high[order]
    lo_err = np.clip(values - low, 0, None)
    hi_err = np.clip(high - values, 0, None)
    pos = np.arange(n)

    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        asp = aspect if aspect is not None else max(0.35, 0.06 * n)
        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=asp)

    if groups is not None:
        groups = np.asarray(groups)[order]
        cats = list(dict.fromkeys(groups.tolist()))
        gc = group_colors or dict(zip(cats, qualitative(len(cats))))
        colors = [gc[g] for g in groups]
    else:
        colors = color or COLORS["blue"]

    horiz = orientation == "horizontal"

    def _errbar(p, v, le, he, c, **kw):
        if horiz:
            ax.errorbar(
                v,
                p,
                xerr=[le, he],
                fmt="o",
                color=c,
                ecolor=c,
                markersize=markersize,
                capsize=capsize,
                elinewidth=0.8,
                markeredgecolor="white",
                markeredgewidth=0.4,
                **kw,
            )
        else:
            ax.errorbar(
                p,
                v,
                yerr=[le, he],
                fmt="o",
                color=c,
                ecolor=c,
                markersize=markersize,
                capsize=capsize,
                elinewidth=0.8,
                markeredgecolor="white",
                markeredgewidth=0.4,
                **kw,
            )

    off = offset if baseline is not None else 0.0
    if groups is not None:
        for c in cats:
            m = np.array([g == c for g in groups])
            _errbar(pos[m] + off, values[m], lo_err[m], hi_err[m], gc[c], zorder=5, label=str(c))
    else:
        _errbar(pos + off, values, lo_err, hi_err, colors, zorder=5)

    if baseline is not None:
        bvals, berr, blo, bhi = _baseline_arrays(baseline, order)
        ble = np.clip(bvals - blo, 0, None)
        bhe = np.clip(bhi - bvals, 0, None)
        _errbar(pos - off, bvals, ble, bhe, baseline_color, zorder=4, alpha=0.8, label=baseline_label)

    if ref_line is not None:
        (ax.axvline if horiz else ax.axhline)(
            ref_line, color=COLORS["neutral"], linestyle="--", linewidth=0.7, zorder=1
        )
        if ref_label:
            ax.text(
                0.99,
                0.99,
                ref_label,
                transform=ax.transAxes,
                ha="right",
                va="top",
                fontsize=th.fs_annot,
                color=COLORS["neutral"],
            )

    from .units import axis_label

    vlabel = axis_label(value_label, value_units) if value_label else ""
    if horiz:
        ax.set_yticks(pos)
        ax.set_yticklabels(labels, fontsize=th.fs_tick)
        ax.set_ylim(-0.6, n - 0.4)
        if vlabel:
            ax.set_xlabel(vlabel)
        ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.15, linewidth=0.5)
    else:
        ax.set_xticks(pos)
        ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=th.fs_tick)
        ax.set_xlim(-0.6, n - 0.4)
        if vlabel:
            ax.set_ylabel(vlabel)
        ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.15, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)

    if annotate_threshold is not None:
        for p, v, lab in zip(pos, values, labels):
            if abs(v) >= annotate_threshold:
                xy, xytext, ha, va = (
                    ((v, p), (3, 0), "left", "center") if horiz else ((p, v), (0, 3), "center", "bottom")
                )
                ax.annotate(
                    lab, xy, fontsize=th.fs_annot, xytext=xytext, textcoords="offset points", ha=ha, va=va
                )

    if summary is not None:
        name, val = summary
        ax.text(
            0.02,
            0.98,
            f"{name} = {val:.3g}",
            transform=ax.transAxes,
            va="top",
            ha="left",
            fontsize=th.fs_annot,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec="#cccccc", lw=0.4, alpha=0.85),
        )

    if legend and (groups is not None or baseline is not None):
        ax.legend(loc="best", fontsize=th.fs_legend)
    return ax

def grouped(
    categories: Sequence[Any],
    series: Mapping[str, ArrayLike | Mapping[Any, float]],
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    colors: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    hatches: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    width_frac: float = 0.8,
    value_label: str = "",
    value_units: str | None = None,
    baseline: float | None = None,
    legend: bool = True,
    rotation: float = 0,
    edgecolor: Any = "white",
) -> Axes:
    """Grouped (dodged) bars, one per ``(category, series)`` pair.

    Args:
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        categories: x-axis category labels.
        series: ``{name: values}`` with values aligned to ``categories``, or
            ``{name: {category: value}}`` where missing categories count as 0.
        colors: ``{name: colour}``; defaults to the theme palette.
        hatches: ``{name: hatch}`` as a texture encoding.
        width_frac: Fraction of each category slot covered by its bars.
        value_label: y-axis label.
        value_units: Unit appended to ``value_label``.
        baseline: y value of a dashed reference line.
        legend: Add a legend when there is more than one series.
        rotation: Category tick-label rotation (degrees).
        edgecolor: Bar edge colour.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    if ax is None:
        _, ax = subplots()
    th = get_theme()
    categories = list(categories)
    data = _as_series(series, categories)
    names = list(data)
    cols = colors or dict(zip(names, qualitative(len(names))))
    nser = len(names)
    x = np.arange(len(categories))
    bw = width_frac / max(nser, 1)

    for i, name in enumerate(names):
        offset = (i - (nser - 1) / 2) * bw
        ax.bar(
            x + offset,
            data[name],
            width=bw * 0.92,
            color=cols[name],
            edgecolor=edgecolor,
            linewidth=0.4,
            label=name,
            hatch=(hatches or {}).get(name),
        )

    if baseline is not None:
        ax.axhline(baseline, color=th.spine_color, linestyle="--", linewidth=0.7, alpha=0.6)

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(
        categories, rotation=rotation, ha="right" if rotation else "center", fontsize=th.fs_tick
    )
    from .units import axis_label

    if value_label:
        ax.set_ylabel(axis_label(value_label, value_units))
    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.15, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    if legend and nser > 1:
        ax.legend(loc="best", fontsize=th.fs_legend, ncol=min(nser, 3))
    return ax

def stacked(
    categories: Sequence[Any],
    segments: Mapping[str, ArrayLike | Mapping[Any, float]],
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    colors: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    width_frac: float = 0.7,
    value_label: str = "",
    value_units: str | None = None,
    legend: bool = True,
    rotation: float = 0,
    normalize: bool = False,
    edgecolor: Any = "white",
) -> Axes:
    """Stacked bars, ``segments`` stacked within each category.

    Args:
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        categories: x-axis category labels.
        segments: ``{name: values}`` with values aligned to ``categories``, or
            ``{name: {category: value}}`` where missing categories count as 0.
            Stacked bottom-up in mapping order.
        colors: ``{name: colour}``; defaults to the theme palette.
        width_frac: Bar width as a fraction of the category slot.
        value_label: y-axis label; defaults to ``"fraction"`` when ``normalize``.
        value_units: Unit appended to ``value_label``.
        legend: Add a legend to the right of the axes.
        rotation: Category tick-label rotation (degrees).
        normalize: Scale each category's stack to sum to 1; all-zero stacks stay 0.
        edgecolor: Bar edge colour.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    if ax is None:
        _, ax = subplots()
    th = get_theme()
    categories = list(categories)
    data = _as_series(segments, categories)
    names = list(data)
    cols = colors or dict(zip(names, qualitative(len(names))))
    x = np.arange(len(categories))
    mat = np.vstack([data[n] for n in names])  # (nseg, ncat)
    if normalize:
        totals = mat.sum(axis=0)
        mat = np.divide(mat, totals, out=np.zeros_like(mat), where=totals > 0)

    bottom = np.zeros(len(categories))
    for i, name in enumerate(names):
        ax.bar(
            x,
            mat[i],
            bottom=bottom,
            width=width_frac,
            color=cols[name],
            edgecolor=edgecolor,
            linewidth=0.4,
            label=name,
        )
        bottom += mat[i]

    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(
        categories, rotation=rotation, ha="right" if rotation else "center", fontsize=th.fs_tick
    )
    from .units import axis_label

    if value_label:
        ax.set_ylabel(axis_label(value_label, value_units))
    elif normalize:
        ax.set_ylabel("fraction")
    if legend:
        ax.legend(loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5), fontsize=th.fs_legend, frameon=False)
    return ax

def skill_gap(
    values: ArrayLike,
    reference: ArrayLike,
    *,
    uncertainty: ArrayLike | None = None,
    direction: str | Sequence[str] = "higher_better",
    target: ArrayLike = 0.0,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Signed distance of ``values`` from a reference, optionally in units of its uncertainty.

    Positive is always better, whichever way a metric is read, so one diverging
    colour scale can carry metrics in different units (see :func:`scorecard`).
    A ``"target"`` metric is scored by closeness to ``target``:
    ``|reference - target| - |values - target|``. Dividing by ``uncertainty``
    turns each gap into a signal-to-noise ratio: ``-3`` is three error bars
    worse than the reference, ``0`` indistinguishable from it.

    Args:
        values: ``(n_rows, n_cols)`` metric table; a 1-D input is one row.
        reference: Values to measure against, broadcast against ``values``.
        uncertainty: Scale the gap is divided by, in the metric's units (e.g. a
            standard error), broadcast against ``values``. Non-positive or
            non-finite entries give ``nan``. ``None`` keeps the metric's units.
        direction: ``"higher_better"``, ``"lower_better"`` or ``"target"``,
            for the whole table or one per column.
        target: Value a ``"target"`` metric is best at, broadcast against ``values``.

    Returns:
        ``(n_rows, n_cols)`` signed gaps, positive where ``values`` beat
        ``reference``; ``nan`` wherever an input is missing.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``values`` and ``reference`` do not broadcast, a per-column
            ``direction`` does not label every column, or a direction is not in
            :data:`DIRECTIONS`.
    """
    values = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(values, dtype=float))
    try:
        reference = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(reference, dtype=float), values.shape)
        target = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(target, dtype=float), values.shape)
    except ValueError:
        raise ValueError(f"values {values.shape} and reference must broadcast to the same shape") from None

    directions = [direction] * values.shape[1] if isinstance(direction, str) else list(direction)
    if len(directions) != values.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(f"give one direction per column: {values.shape[1]} columns, {len(directions)} given")
    unknown = sorted({d for d in directions if d not in DIRECTIONS})
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown direction(s) {unknown}; known: {list(DIRECTIONS)}")

    gap = np.full(values.shape, np.nan)
    for j, how in enumerate(directions):
        if how == "higher_better":
            gap[:, j] = values[:, j] - reference[:, j]
        elif how == "lower_better":
            gap[:, j] = reference[:, j] - values[:, j]
        else:  # closeness to the target, so positive is still better
            gap[:, j] = np.abs(reference[:, j] - target[:, j]) - np.abs(values[:, j] - target[:, j])

    if uncertainty is not None:
        scale = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(uncertainty, dtype=float), values.shape)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            gap = np.where(np.isfinite(scale) & (scale > 0), gap / scale, np.nan)
    return gap

    width: float | str = "half",
    title: str = "",
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    square: bool = False,
    col_groups: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    group_gap: float = 0.6,
    colorbar: bool = False,
    colorbar_label: str = "",
    colorbar_extend: str | None = None,
) -> Axes:
    """Render a ``(n_rows, n_cols)`` metric table as a coloured-cell figure.

    By default each cell is coloured by its per-column goodness rank (green is
    best) and the best cell per column is outlined. ``reference`` colours cells
    by :func:`skill_gap` instead, and ``norm`` by their raw value.

    Args:
        values: Table of shape ``(len(row_labels), len(col_labels))``; ``nan``
            cells are drawn blank in ``na_color``.
        row_labels: Row (model) names.
        col_labels: Column (metric) names.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        direction: ``{col_label: direction}`` with values from
            :data:`~nicefigs.units.DIRECTIONS`; unlisted columns are
            ``"higher_better"``. ``"target"`` ranks by closeness to ``target``.
        per_column_norm: Rank each column on its own min→max (else one global
            range). Ignored for colour when ``norm`` or ``reference`` is given.
        highlight_best: Outline the best cell in each column by the goodness rank.
        reference: Values to measure against, broadcast against ``values``.
            Cell colour becomes the signed :func:`skill_gap` on one diverging
            scale; cell text stays the raw value.
        uncertainty: With ``reference``, the scale each gap is divided by.
        target: The value a ``"target"`` metric is best at, broadcast against
            ``values``.
        gap_limit: Gap at which the ``reference`` colour scale saturates.
        cell_format: Format string for the cell text.
        col_units: ``{col_label: unit}`` shown below the column name.
        cmap: Colormap name or object.
        na_color: Colour of missing cells.
        width: Figure width (preset name or inches) when ``ax`` is ``None``.
        title: Left-aligned title.
        norm: Normalisation mapping raw ``values`` straight to ``cmap`` (e.g. from
            :func:`nicefigs.scorecard_diverging_cmap`).
        square: Size the figure from the cell count and force square cells;
            only sizes the figure when ``ax`` is ``None``.
        col_groups: One group name per column; consecutive equal names form a
            group with a gap before it and a bold title above it.
        group_gap: Gap before each group, in cell widths.
        colorbar: Add a horizontal colorbar below the table.
        colorbar_label: Colorbar label.
        colorbar_extend: ``"neither"``, ``"min"``, ``"max"`` or ``"both"``;
            inferred from ``cmap``'s under/over colours if ``None``.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    nr, nc = values.shape
    directions = [check_direction((direction or {}).get(c, "higher_better")) for c in col_labels]
    targets = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(target, dtype=float), values.shape)
    cm = resolve_cmap(cmap)

    lefts = np.zeros(nc)
    cur = 0.0
    for j in range(nc):
        if col_groups is not None and j > 0 and col_groups[j] != col_groups[j - 1]:
            cur += group_gap
        lefts[j] = cur
        cur += 1.0
    total_w = cur

    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        if square:
            fig_w = max(total_w * _SQUARE_CELL_INCH, 1.0)
            fig_h = max(nr * _SQUARE_CELL_INCH, 1.0)
            _, ax = subplots(width=fig_w, height=fig_h)
        else:
            _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=max(0.3, 0.12 * nr + 0.12))
    if square:
        ax.set_aspect("equal")

    # Goodness in [0, 1] (1 = best); drives `highlight_best` whatever colours the cells.
    good = np.full_like(values, 0.5)
    if per_column_norm:
        for j in range(nc):
            col = values[:, j]
            dirn = directions[j]
            metric = np.abs(col - targets[:, j]) if dirn == "target" else col
            finite = metric[np.isfinite(metric)]
            if finite.size == 0:
                continue
            lo, hi = finite.min(), finite.max()
            g = np.zeros_like(metric) if hi <= lo else (metric - lo) / (hi - lo)
            if dirn in ("lower_better", "target"):
                g = 1 - g
            good[:, j] = g
    else:
        finite = values[np.isfinite(values)]
        lo, hi = (finite.min(), finite.max()) if finite.size else (0, 1)
        good = np.zeros_like(values) if hi <= lo else (values - lo) / (hi - lo)

    gap = None
    if reference is not None:
        gap = skill_gap(
            values,
            reference,
            uncertainty=uncertainty,
            direction=directions,
            target=target,
        )
        norm = (
            norm if norm is not None else mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0.0, vmin=-gap_limit, vmax=gap_limit)
        )

    ax.set_xlim(0, total_w)
    ax.set_ylim(0, nr)
    ax.invert_yaxis()

    for i in range(nr):
        for j in range(nc):
            v = values[i, j]
            if not np.isfinite(v):
                face = na_color
            elif gap is not None:
                face = na_color if not np.isfinite(gap[i, j]) else cm(norm(gap[i, j]))
            elif norm is not None:
                face = cm(norm(v))
            else:
                face = cm(float(np.clip(good[i, j], 0, 1)))
            ax.add_patch(
                mpatches.Rectangle((lefts[j], i), 1, 1, facecolor=face, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1.0)
            )
            if np.isfinite(v):
                r, g, b = face[:3] if isinstance(face, tuple) else (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
                txtcol = "white" if (0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b) < 0.5 else "#222222"
                ax.text(
                    lefts[j] + 0.5,
                    i + 0.5,
                    cell_format.format(v),
                    ha="center",
                    va="center",
                    fontsize=th.fs_annot,
                    color=txtcol,
                )

    if highlight_best:
        for j in range(nc):
            col_good = good[:, j].copy()
            col_good[~np.isfinite(values[:, j])] = -np.inf
            if np.isfinite(col_good).any():
                bi = int(np.argmax(col_good))
                ax.add_patch(
                    mpatches.Rectangle(
                        (lefts[j], bi), 1, 1, fill=False, edgecolor=th.spine_color, linewidth=1.6, zorder=5
                    )
                )

    ax.set_xticks(lefts + 0.5)
    heads = []
    for c in col_labels:
        u = (col_units or {}).get(c)
        heads.append(f"{c}\n[{prettify_unit(u)}]" if u else c)
    ax.set_xticklabels(heads, fontsize=th.fs_tick)
    ax.xaxis.set_ticks_position("top")
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(nr) + 0.5)
    ax.set_yticklabels(row_labels, fontsize=th.fs_tick)
    ax.tick_params(length=0)
    for sp in ax.spines.values():
        sp.set_visible(False)

    if col_groups is not None:
        import matplotlib.transforms as mtransforms

        blend = mtransforms.blended_transform_factory(ax.transData, ax.transAxes)
        j = 0
        while j < nc:
            k = j
            while k + 1 < nc and col_groups[k + 1] == col_groups[j]:
                k += 1
            cx = 0.5 * (lefts[j] + lefts[k] + 1)
            ax.text(
                cx,
                1.22,
                col_groups[j],
                transform=blend,
                ha="center",
                va="bottom",
                fontsize=th.fs_tick,
                fontweight="bold",
            )
            j = k + 1

    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=th.fs_title, pad=28 if col_groups is not None else 14, loc="left")

    if colorbar:
        from matplotlib.cm import ScalarMappable

        from .colorbars import colorbar as _draw_colorbar

        cb_norm = norm if norm is not None else mcolors.Normalize(vmin=0.0, vmax=1.0)
        extend = colorbar_extend if colorbar_extend is not None else _cmap_extend(cm)
        sm = ScalarMappable(norm=cb_norm, cmap=cm)
        sm.set_array([])
        _draw_colorbar(sm, ax, location="bottom", extend=extend, label=colorbar_label)

    return ax

def profile(
    profiles: Mapping[str, ArrayLike] | ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike | None = None,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    invert_y: bool = True,
    log_y: bool = False,
    colors: Mapping[str, str] | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    styles: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    markers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    marker: str = "o",
    baselines: Mapping[str, ArrayLike] | None = None,
    baseline_colors: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    xlabel: str = "",
    xunits: str | None = None,
    ylabel: str = "level",
    yunits: str | None = None,
    title: str = "",
    legend: bool = True,
    width: float | str = "half",
    aspect: float = 0.95,
) -> Axes:
    """Draw one or more vertical profiles: value on x, level on y.

    The 1-D companion to :func:`cross_section`. The vertical axis is inverted by
    default so that descending pressure levels put the surface at the bottom.

    Args:
        profiles: ``{name: values}`` along ``y``, or a single array.
        y: Vertical coordinate shared by all profiles (e.g. pressure); defaults
            to the level index.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created when ``None``.
        invert_y: Invert the vertical axis.
        log_y: Log-scale the vertical axis.
        colors: ``{name: colour}`` or a list cycled over the profiles; defaults to
            the theme's qualitative palette.
        styles: ``{name: linestyle}``; default solid.
        markers: ``{name: marker}`` overriding ``marker``.
        marker: Marker used for profiles not in ``markers``.
        baselines: ``{name: values}`` reference profiles drawn dashed.
        baseline_colors: ``{name: colour}`` for ``baselines``; default grey.
        xlabel: Value-axis label.
        xunits: Value-axis units, appended to the label.
        ylabel: Vertical-axis label.
        yunits: Vertical-axis units, appended to the label.
        title: Axes title.
        legend: Draw a legend when there is more than one line.
        width: Figure width in inches or a :data:`nicefigs.figure.WIDTHS` name,
            used only when a new figure is created.
        aspect: Figure ``height / width``, used only when a new figure is created.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    if not isinstance(profiles, dict):
        profiles = {"profile": profiles}
    names = list(profiles)
    palette = colors or {nm: c for nm, c in zip(names, qualitative(len(names)))}
    if not isinstance(palette, dict):
        palette = {nm: palette[i % len(palette)] for i, nm in enumerate(names)}
    marks = markers or {}

    if ax is None:
        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=aspect)

    for nm in names:
        v = np.asarray(profiles[nm], dtype=float)
        yy = np.arange(v.size) if y is None else np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
        ax.plot(
            v,
            yy,
            linestyle=(styles or {}).get(nm, "-"),
            color=palette.get(nm),
            marker=marks.get(nm, marker),
            markersize=4,
            linewidth=th.lw_line,
            label=nm,
        )
    if baselines:
        bpal = baseline_colors or {}
        for nm, v in baselines.items():
            v = np.asarray(v, dtype=float)
            yy = np.arange(v.size) if y is None else np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
            ax.plot(
                v, yy, linestyle="--", color=bpal.get(nm, "#888888"), linewidth=th.lw_line * 0.8, label=nm
            )

    if log_y:
        ax.set_yscale("log")
    if invert_y and not ax.yaxis_inverted():
        ax.invert_yaxis()

    from .units import axis_label

    ax.set_xlabel(axis_label(xlabel, xunits))
    ax.set_ylabel(axis_label(ylabel, yunits))
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=th.fs_title, loc="left", pad=3)
    if legend and (len(names) > 1 or baselines):
        ax.legend(fontsize=th.fs_legend, framealpha=0.9)
    return ax

def cross_section(
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    z: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    cmap: str | Colormap = "Spectral_r",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    diff: bool = False,
    robust: bool = True,
    invert_y: bool = True,
    xlabel: str = "latitude",
    ylabel: str = "pressure",
    xunits: str | None = "°N",
    yunits: str | None = "hPa",
    title: str = "",
    log_y: bool = False,
) -> tuple[Axes, QuadMesh]:
    """Draw a field over a horizontal and a vertical coordinate as a curtain.

    Args:
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created if ``None``.
        x: Horizontal coordinate of length ``nx`` (e.g. latitude).
        y: Vertical coordinate of length ``ny`` (e.g. pressure).
        z: Field of shape ``(nx, ny)``.
        cmap: Colormap name or object.
        vmin: Lower colour limit; derived from ``z`` if ``None``.
        vmax: Upper colour limit; derived from ``z`` if ``None``.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        diff: Treat ``z`` as a difference: symmetric limits, and ``RdBu_r`` when
            ``cmap`` is left at its default.
        robust: Derive limits from the 2nd/98th percentiles instead of min/max.
        invert_y: Invert the vertical axis (surface at the bottom for pressure).
        xlabel: x-axis label.
        ylabel: y-axis label.
        xunits: Units appended to the x-axis label.
        yunits: Units appended to the y-axis label.
        title: Axes title.
        log_y: Log-scale the vertical axis.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, mesh)``: the axes and the drawn :class:`~matplotlib.collections.QuadMesh`.
    """
    if ax is None:
        _, ax = subplots()
    th = get_theme()
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    if diff and cmap == "Spectral_r":
        cmap = "RdBu_r"
    if norm is None and (vmin is None or vmax is None):
        if diff:
            lo, hi = symmetric_limits(z)
        elif robust:
            lo, hi = robust_limits(z)
        else:
            lo, hi = float(np.nanmin(z)), float(np.nanmax(z))
        vmin = lo if vmin is None else vmin
        vmax = hi if vmax is None else vmax

    kw = dict(cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), shading="auto")
    if norm is not None:
        kw["norm"] = norm
    else:
        kw["vmin"], kw["vmax"] = vmin, vmax
    mesh = ax.pcolormesh(x, y, z.T, **kw)

    if log_y:
        ax.set_yscale("log")
    if invert_y and not ax.yaxis_inverted():
        ax.invert_yaxis()

    from .units import axis_label

    ax.set_xlabel(axis_label(xlabel, xunits))
    ax.set_ylabel(axis_label(ylabel, yunits))
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=th.fs_title, loc="left", pad=3)
    return ax, mesh

def cross_section_panels(
    fields: Mapping[str, ArrayLike],
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    *,
    diff_fields: Collection[str] = (),
    value_cmap: str | Colormap = "Spectral_r",
    diff_cmap: str | Colormap = "RdBu_r",
    value_label: str = "",
    diff_label: str = "",
    invert_y: bool = True,
    log_y: bool = False,
    width: float | str = "full",
    panel_aspect: float = 0.8,
    ylabel: str = "pressure",
    yunits: str | None = "hPa",
    xlabel: str = "latitude",
    xunits: str | None = "°N",
    title: str = "",
    titles: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> tuple[Figure, np.ndarray]:
    """Lay out curtains in a row with shared value and difference colorbars.

    Value fields share robust colour limits and one colorbar; difference fields
    share symmetric limits and a second, diverging colorbar.

    Args:
        fields: ``{name: (nx, ny) array}`` in display order.
        x: Shared horizontal coordinate of length ``nx``.
        y: Shared vertical coordinate of length ``ny``.
        diff_fields: Names in ``fields`` drawn on the difference scale.
        value_cmap: Colormap of the value panels.
        diff_cmap: Colormap of the difference panel.
        value_label: Label of the value colorbar.
        diff_label: Label of the difference colorbar.
        invert_y: Invert the vertical axis.
        log_y: Log-scale the vertical axis.
        width: Figure width in inches or a :data:`nicefigs.figure.WIDTHS` name.
        panel_aspect: Height / width of each panel.
        ylabel: Vertical-axis label (first panel only).
        yunits: Vertical-axis units, appended to the label (first panel only).
        xlabel: Horizontal-axis label.
        xunits: Horizontal-axis units, appended to the label.
        title: Figure title above the row.
        titles: Per-panel titles aligned with ``fields``; defaults to the field
            names.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, axes)`` with ``axes`` a flat array, one per field.
    """
    from .colorbars import colorbar
    from .figure import subplots

    names = list(fields)
    diff_set = set(diff_fields)
    n = len(names)
    fig, axes = subplots(1, n, width=width, panel_aspect=panel_aspect, wspace=0.14, squeeze=False)
    axes = axes.ravel()

    val_names = [nm for nm in names if nm not in diff_set]
    dif_names = [nm for nm in names if nm in diff_set]
    val_lim = (
        robust_limits(np.concatenate([np.asarray(fields[nm]).ravel() for nm in val_names]))
        if val_names
        else None
    )
    dif_lim = (
        symmetric_limits(np.concatenate([np.asarray(fields[nm]).ravel() for nm in dif_names]))
        if dif_names
        else None
    )

    val_m = dif_m = None
    for i, (ax, nm) in enumerate(zip(axes, names)):
        is_diff = nm in diff_set
        lim = dif_lim if is_diff else val_lim
        panel_title = titles[i] if titles is not None and i < len(titles) else nm
        _, m = cross_section(
            x,
            y,
            fields[nm],
            cmap=(diff_cmap if is_diff else value_cmap),
            vmin=lim[0],
            vmax=lim[1],
            diff=is_diff,
            invert_y=invert_y,
            log_y=log_y,
            xlabel=xlabel,
            xunits=xunits,
            ylabel=(ylabel if ax is axes[0] else ""),
            yunits=yunits,
            title=panel_title,
            ax=ax,
        )
        if ax is not axes[0]:
            ax.set_yticklabels([])
        if is_diff:
            dif_m = m
        else:
            val_m = m
    # Extra pad so the horizontal bars sit clear below the x-axis labels.
    if val_m is not None:
        colorbar(
            val_m,
            [ax for ax, nm in zip(axes, names) if nm not in diff_set],
            label=value_label,
            location="bottom",
            thickness=0.03,
            shrink=0.85,
            pad=0.14,
        )
    if dif_m is not None:
        colorbar(
            dif_m,
            [ax for ax, nm in zip(axes, names) if nm in diff_set],
            label=diff_label,
            location="bottom",
            thickness=0.03,
            shrink=0.85,
            pad=0.14,
        )
    if title:
        # Sit clear above the per-panel titles (the row is short, so 1.02 collides).
        fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=get_theme().fs_panel_label, y=1.16)
    return fig, axes

def taylor(
    stats: Mapping[str, Any] | Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    ref_std: float = 1.0,
    normalize: bool = True,
    ref_label: str = "Reference",
    std_label: str | None = None,
    colors: Sequence[Any] | None = None,
    markers: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    marker_size: float = 9.0,
    rms_contours: bool = True,
    n_rms: int = 4,
    corr_ticks: Sequence[float] = (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 1.0),
    negative: bool = False,
    title: str = "",
    legend: bool = True,
    width: float | str = "half",
) -> Axes:
    """Draw a Taylor diagram of one or more models against a reference.

    Each model sits at angle ``arccos(r)`` (its correlation ``r`` with the
    reference) and radius equal to its standard deviation; its distance to the
    reference point is the centred RMS difference.

    Args:
        stats: A list of dicts, one per model, or ``{name: dict}``, or
            ``{name: (std, corr)}``. Each dict holds ``name`` (optional with the
            mapping forms), a correlation ``corr`` (or ``correlation``), and
            either an absolute ``std`` or a normalised ``std_ratio``
            (σ_model / σ_ref). Other keys are ignored.
        ax: Existing polar axes to draw on; a new one is created if ``None``.
        ref_std: Reference standard deviation, in the units of ``std``.
        normalize: Divide absolute ``std`` values by ``ref_std`` so the
            reference sits at radius 1; otherwise it sits at ``ref_std`` and
            ``std_ratio`` values are multiplied by ``ref_std``.
        ref_label: Legend label of the reference point.
        std_label: Radial-axis label; defaults to "(Normalized) standard deviation".
        colors: Per-model colours; defaults to the theme palette.
        markers: Per-model markers; defaults to :data:`MARKERS`.
        marker_size: Model marker size (pt).
        rms_contours: Draw dotted centred-RMS-difference arcs around the reference.
        n_rms: Number of RMS arcs.
        corr_ticks: Correlations marked on the angular axis.
        negative: Extend the diagram to negative correlations (half circle).
        title: Left-aligned title.
        legend: Add a legend of the model markers outside the axes.
        width: Figure width (preset name or inches) when ``ax`` is ``None``.

    Returns:
        The polar axes.

    Raises:
        KeyError: An entry has no correlation or no standard deviation.
    """
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    rows = _coerce(stats)
    th = get_theme()
    ref = 1.0 if normalize else float(ref_std)

    def _std(row):
        if row["is_ratio"]:
            return row["std"] if normalize else row["std"] * ref_std
        return row["std"] / ref_std if normalize else row["std"]

    stds = [_std(r) for r in rows]

    if ax is None:
        from .figure import figure_size
        from .style import style

        with style(th):
            fig = plt.figure(figsize=figure_size(width, aspect=1.0), dpi=th.dpi)
            ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="polar")

    theta_max = np.pi if negative else np.pi / 2.0
    ax.set_thetamin(0)
    ax.set_thetamax(np.degrees(theta_max))
    ax.set_theta_zero_location("E")
    ax.set_theta_direction(1)

    smax = max([ref, *stds]) * 1.3 if stds else ref * 1.3
    ax.set_ylim(0, smax)

    # Angular (correlation) grid.
    ticks = list(corr_ticks)
    if negative:
        ticks = sorted({*ticks, *[-t for t in corr_ticks]})
    ang = np.degrees(np.arccos(np.clip(ticks, -1, 1)))
    ax.set_thetagrids(ang, labels=[f"{t:g}" for t in ticks])
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=th.fs_tick)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=th.fs_tick)

    # Centred-RMS-difference arcs, centred on the reference point (ref, 0).
    if rms_contours:
        rmax = np.hypot(smax, ref)
        for R in np.linspace(rmax / (n_rms + 1), rmax, n_rms):
            phi = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 361)
            x = ref + R * np.cos(phi)
            y = R * np.sin(phi)
            r = np.hypot(x, y)
            t = np.arctan2(y, x)
            keep = (t >= -1e-9) & (t <= theta_max + 1e-9) & (r <= smax)
            if keep.sum() > 1:
                ax.plot(t[keep], r[keep], ls=":", color="#9aa0a6", lw=0.6, zorder=1)

    # Reference point + its std arc.
    ax.plot(
        np.linspace(0, theta_max, 100),
        np.full(100, ref),
        ls="--",
        color=th.spine_color,
        lw=0.6,
        alpha=0.6,
        zorder=1,
    )
    ax.plot(
        0,
        ref,
        marker="*",
        markersize=marker_size + 5,
        color=th.spine_color,
        zorder=6,
        label=ref_label,
        linestyle="none",
    )

    palette = colors or qualitative(len(rows))
    marks = markers or MARKERS
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        ax.plot(
            np.arccos(np.clip(row["corr"], -1, 1)),
            _std(row),
            marker=marks[i % len(marks)],
            color=palette[i % len(palette)],
            markersize=marker_size,
            linestyle="none",
            zorder=5,
            label=row["name"] or None,
        )

    ax.set_rlabel_position(90 if negative else 135)
    lbl = std_label or ("Normalized standard deviation" if normalize else "Standard deviation")
    ax.set_ylabel(lbl, fontsize=th.fs_axis_label, labelpad=22)
    ax.text(
        np.radians(45 if not negative else 90),
        smax * 1.12,
        "Correlation",
        ha="center",
        va="center",
        fontsize=th.fs_axis_label,
        rotation=(-45 if not negative else 0),
    )
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=th.fs_title, loc="left", pad=10)
    if legend and any(r["name"] for r in rows):
        ax.legend(
            loc="upper right",
            bbox_to_anchor=(1.32, 1.08),
            fontsize=th.fs_legend,
            framealpha=0.9,
            markerscale=0.6,
        )
    return ax

def hovmoller(
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    z: ArrayLike,
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    cmap: str | Colormap = "Spectral_r",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    norm: Normalize | None = None,
    diff: bool = False,
    robust: bool = True,
    colorbar: bool | None = None,
    colorbar_label: str = "",
    xlabel: str = "time",
    ylabel: str = "latitude",
    xunits: str | None = None,
    yunits: str | None = "°N",
    title: str = "",
    width: float | str = "full",
    aspect: float = 0.5,
) -> tuple[Axes, QuadMesh]:
    """Draw a field over time (x axis) and one spatial coordinate (y axis).

    Args:
        x: Time coordinate of length ``nt``: numbers or ``datetime`` objects
            (dates get a compact date axis).
        y: Spatial coordinate of length ``ny``, e.g. latitude.
        z: Field of shape ``(nt, ny)``.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created when ``None``.
        cmap: Colormap name or object.
        vmin: Lower colour limit; derived from ``z`` if ``None``.
        vmax: Upper colour limit; derived from ``z`` if ``None``.
        norm: Colour normalisation; overrides ``vmin``/``vmax``.
        diff: Treat ``z`` as a difference: symmetric limits, and ``RdBu_r`` when
            ``cmap`` is left at its default.
        robust: Derive limits from the 2nd/98th percentiles instead of min/max.
        colorbar: Draw a colorbar. Defaults to ``True`` when this call creates the
            figure and ``False`` when drawing onto a supplied ``ax``.
        colorbar_label: Colorbar label.
        xlabel: x-axis label; ``""`` leaves the axis unlabelled.
        ylabel: y-axis label; ``""`` leaves the axis unlabelled.
        xunits: Units appended to the x-axis label.
        yunits: Units appended to the y-axis label.
        title: Axes title.
        width: Figure width in inches or a :data:`nicefigs.figure.WIDTHS` name,
            used only when a new figure is created.
        aspect: Figure ``height / width``, used only when a new figure is created.

    Returns:
        ``(ax, mesh)``: the axes and the ``QuadMesh``, for composing colorbars.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    if diff and cmap == "Spectral_r":
        cmap = "RdBu_r"
    if norm is None and (vmin is None or vmax is None):
        if diff:
            lo, hi = symmetric_limits(z)
        elif robust:
            lo, hi = robust_limits(z)
        else:
            lo, hi = float(np.nanmin(z)), float(np.nanmax(z))
        vmin = lo if vmin is None else vmin
        vmax = hi if vmax is None else vmax

    owns_fig = ax is None
    if colorbar is None:
        colorbar = owns_fig
    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=aspect)

    xv = np.asarray(x)
    is_dates = _is_dates(x)
    if is_dates:
        import matplotlib.dates as mdates

        xv = mdates.date2num(list(x))

    kw = dict(cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), shading="auto")
    if norm is not None:
        kw["norm"] = norm
    else:
        kw["vmin"], kw["vmax"] = vmin, vmax
    mesh = ax.pcolormesh(xv, y, z.T, **kw)

    if is_dates:
        from .timeseries import _format_date_axis

        _format_date_axis(ax, list(x))
    if xlabel:
        ax.set_xlabel(axis_label(xlabel, xunits))
    if ylabel:
        ax.set_ylabel(axis_label(ylabel, yunits))
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=th.fs_title, loc="left", pad=3)
    if colorbar:
        from .colorbars import colorbar as _cbar

        _cbar(mesh, ax, label=colorbar_label)
    return ax, mesh

def hovmoller_panels(
    fields: Mapping[str, ArrayLike],
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    *,
    diff_fields: Collection[str] = (),
    value_cmap: str | Colormap = "Spectral_r",
    diff_cmap: str | Colormap = "RdBu_r",
    value_label: str = "",
    diff_label: str = "",
    xlabel: str = "time",
    xunits: str | None = None,
    ylabel: str = "latitude",
    yunits: str | None = "°N",
    width: float | str = "full",
    panel_aspect: float = 0.62,
    title: str = "",
    titles: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> tuple[Figure, np.ndarray]:
    """Lay out Hovmöller panels in a row with shared value and difference colorbars.

    Value fields share robust colour limits and one colorbar; difference fields
    share symmetric limits and a second, diverging colorbar.

    Args:
        x: Shared time coordinate of length ``nt``.
        fields: ``{name: (nt, ny) array}`` in display order.
        y: Shared spatial coordinate of length ``ny``.
        diff_fields: Names in ``fields`` drawn on the difference scale.
        value_cmap: Colormap of the value panels.
        diff_cmap: Colormap of the difference panel.
        value_label: Label of the value colorbar.
        diff_label: Label of the difference colorbar.
        xlabel: Time-axis label.
        xunits: Time-axis units, appended to the label.
        ylabel: Spatial-axis label (first panel only).
        yunits: Spatial-axis units, appended to the label (first panel only).
        width: Figure width in inches or a :data:`nicefigs.figure.WIDTHS` name.
        panel_aspect: Height / width of each panel.
        title: Figure title above the row.
        titles: Per-panel titles aligned with ``fields``; defaults to the field
            names.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, axes)`` with ``axes`` a flat array, one per field.
    """
    from .colorbars import colorbar
    from .figure import subplots

    names = list(fields)
    diff_set = set(diff_fields)
    n = len(names)
    fig, axes = subplots(1, n, width=width, panel_aspect=panel_aspect, wspace=0.12, squeeze=False)
    axes = axes.ravel()

    val_names = [nm for nm in names if nm not in diff_set]
    dif_names = [nm for nm in names if nm in diff_set]
    val_lim = (
        robust_limits(np.concatenate([np.asarray(fields[nm]).ravel() for nm in val_names]))
        if val_names
        else None
    )
    dif_lim = (
        symmetric_limits(np.concatenate([np.asarray(fields[nm]).ravel() for nm in dif_names]))
        if dif_names
        else None
    )

    val_m = dif_m = None
    for i, (ax, nm) in enumerate(zip(axes, names)):
        is_diff = nm in diff_set
        lim = dif_lim if is_diff else val_lim
        panel_title = titles[i] if titles is not None and i < len(titles) else nm
        _, m = hovmoller(
            x,
            y,
            fields[nm],
            ax=ax,
            cmap=(diff_cmap if is_diff else value_cmap),
            vmin=lim[0],
            vmax=lim[1],
            diff=is_diff,
            colorbar=False,
            xlabel=xlabel,
            xunits=xunits,
            ylabel=(ylabel if ax is axes[0] else ""),
            yunits=yunits,
            title=panel_title,
        )
        if ax is not axes[0]:
            ax.set_yticklabels([])
        if is_diff:
            dif_m = m
        else:
            val_m = m
    if val_m is not None:
        colorbar(
            val_m,
            [ax for ax, nm in zip(axes, names) if nm not in diff_set],
            label=value_label,
            location="bottom",
            thickness=0.03,
            shrink=0.85,
            pad=0.26,
        )
    if dif_m is not None:
        colorbar(
            dif_m,
            [ax for ax, nm in zip(axes, names) if nm in diff_set],
            label=diff_label,
            location="bottom",
            thickness=0.03,
            shrink=0.85,
            pad=0.26,
        )
    if title:
        # Sit clear above the per-panel titles (the row is short, so 1.02 collides).
        fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=get_theme().fs_panel_label, y=1.16)
    return fig, axes

def reliability(
    nominal: ArrayLike | Mapping[str, ArrayLike],
    observed: ArrayLike | Mapping[str, ArrayLike],
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    colors: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    markers: str | Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    highlight: float | None = 0.90,
    highlight_color: str | None = None,
    diagonal_label: str = "Perfect calibration",
    xlabel: str = "Nominal coverage",
    ylabel: str = "Observed coverage",
    title: str = "",
    legend: bool = True,
    marker_size: float = 4.0,
    width: float | str = "half",
) -> Axes:
    """Draw a reliability diagram: observed against nominal coverage, with the 1:1 line.

    For a PIT calibration plot, pass probability levels as ``nominal`` and the
    empirical CDF of the PIT values at those levels as ``observed``.

    Args:
        nominal: Nominal levels in ``[0, 1]`` shared by all curves, or
            ``{name: levels}`` for curves evaluated at different levels.
        observed: ``{name: observed_frequency}`` aligned with ``nominal``, or one
            array for a single unnamed curve.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new square figure is created when ``None``.
        colors: ``{name: colour}``; defaults to the theme's qualitative palette.
        markers: ``{name: marker}``, or one marker for all curves; default ``"o"``.
        highlight: Nominal level marked on the diagonal (e.g. ``0.90``); ``None``
            omits the mark.
        highlight_color: Colour of the highlight mark; default neutral grey.
        diagonal_label: Legend label of the 1:1 line; ``""`` keeps the line but
            leaves it out of the legend.
        xlabel: x-axis label.
        ylabel: y-axis label.
        title: Axes title.
        legend: Draw a legend.
        marker_size: Marker size in points.
        width: Figure width in inches or a :data:`nicefigs.figure.WIDTHS` name,
            used only when a new figure is created.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    if not isinstance(observed, dict):
        observed = {"": np.asarray(observed, dtype=float)}
    names = list(observed)
    nom_map = nominal if isinstance(nominal, dict) else None

    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=1.0)

    ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], ls="--", lw=0.8, color=COLORS["neutral"], zorder=1, label=diagonal_label or None)

    if highlight is not None:
        ax.plot(
            highlight,
            highlight,
            marker="+",
            markersize=8,
            mew=1.2,
            color=highlight_color or COLORS["neutral"],
            zorder=2,
        )
        ax.axvline(highlight, color=COLORS["neutral"], lw=0.5, ls=":", alpha=0.5, zorder=0)

    cols = colors or dict(zip(names, qualitative(len(names))))
    for name in names:
        x = np.asarray(nom_map[name] if nom_map else nominal, dtype=float)
        y = np.asarray(observed[name], dtype=float)
        mk = markers.get(name) if isinstance(markers, dict) else markers
        ax.plot(
            x,
            y,
            color=cols[name],
            lw=th.lw_line,
            marker=mk or "o",
            markersize=marker_size,
            zorder=4,
            label=name or None,
        )

    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    if title:
        from .panels import clean_title

        clean_title(ax, title)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.15, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    if legend and (len(names) > 1 or (names and names[0]) or diagonal_label):
        ax.legend(loc="best", fontsize=th.fs_legend)
    return ax

def rank_histogram(
    ranks: ArrayLike,
    *,
    n_ranks: int | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    color: str | None = None,
    ideal: bool = True,
    normalize: bool = True,
    summary: tuple[str, float] | None = None,
    xlabel: str = "Rank",
    ylabel: str = "Frequency",
    title: str = "",
    width: float | str = "half",
    aspect: float = 0.72,
) -> Axes:
    """Draw a rank (Talagrand) histogram of verification ranks.

    Args:
        ranks: Integer rank per event: the 0-indexed position of the truth among
            the sorted ensemble members, in ``[0, n_members]``.
        n_ranks: Number of rank bins (``n_members + 1``); defaults to
            ``max(ranks) + 1``.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new figure is created when ``None``.
        color: Bar colour; default the theme's blue.
        ideal: Draw the flat reference a perfectly calibrated ensemble attains.
        normalize: Show frequencies summing to 1 instead of counts.
        summary: ``(name, value)`` written in the top-left corner, e.g. a
            calibration statistic.
        xlabel: x-axis label.
        ylabel: y-axis label.
        title: Axes title.
        width: Figure width in inches or a :data:`nicefigs.figure.WIDTHS` name,
            used only when a new figure is created.
        aspect: Figure ``height / width``, used only when a new figure is created.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    ranks = np.asarray(ranks, dtype=int)
    n_ranks = n_ranks if n_ranks is not None else int(ranks.max()) + 1 if ranks.size else 1
    counts = np.bincount(ranks, minlength=n_ranks)[:n_ranks].astype(float)
    total = counts.sum()
    if normalize and total > 0:
        counts = counts / total

    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=aspect)

    x = np.arange(n_ranks)
    ax.bar(x, counts, width=0.85, color=color or COLORS["blue"], edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.4, zorder=3)

    if ideal:
        from .panels import reference_line

        flat = (1.0 / n_ranks) if normalize else total / n_ranks
        reference_line(ax, flat, axis="y", label="ideal", linestyle="--", zorder=2)

    ax.set_xlim(-0.6, n_ranks - 0.4)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    if title:
        from .panels import clean_title

        clean_title(ax, title)
    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.15, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)

    if summary is not None:
        name, val = summary
        ax.text(
            0.02,
            0.98,
            f"{name} = {val:.3g}",
            transform=ax.transAxes,
            va="top",
            ha="left",
            fontsize=th.fs_annot,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec="#cccccc", lw=0.4, alpha=0.85),
        )
    return ax

def rank_histogram_panels(
    ranks_by_name: Mapping[str, ArrayLike],
    *,
    n_ranks: int | None = None,
    ncols: int = 3,
    colors: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    ideal: bool = True,
    normalize: bool = True,
    summaries: Mapping[str, tuple[str, float]] | None = None,
    width: float | str = "full",
    panel_aspect: float = 0.8,
    titles: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> tuple[Figure, np.ndarray]:
    """Draw one :func:`rank_histogram` panel per model as small multiples.

    Args:
        ranks_by_name: ``{name: ranks}``; see :func:`rank_histogram`.
        n_ranks: Number of rank bins shared by all panels; defaults to the
            maximum over all models, so the panels stay comparable.
        ncols: Panels per row.
        colors: ``{name: colour}``; defaults to the theme's qualitative palette.
        ideal: Draw the flat reference in each panel.
        normalize: Show frequencies instead of counts.
        summaries: ``{name: (label, value)}`` annotation per panel.
        width: Figure width in inches or a :data:`nicefigs.figure.WIDTHS` name.
        panel_aspect: Height / width of each panel.
        titles: Per-panel titles aligned with ``ranks_by_name``; defaults to the
            model names.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, axes)`` with ``axes`` a flat array, one per model.
    """
    from .panels import facet

    names = list(ranks_by_name)
    if n_ranks is None:
        n_ranks = max(int(np.max(np.asarray(v))) for v in ranks_by_name.values() if np.size(v)) + 1
    cols = colors or dict(zip(names, qualitative(len(names))))
    summaries = summaries or {}

    def draw(ax: Axes, name: str, _i: int) -> None:
        panel_title = "" if titles is not None else name
        rank_histogram(
            ranks_by_name[name],
            n_ranks=n_ranks,
            ax=ax,
            color=cols[name],
            ideal=ideal,
            normalize=normalize,
            summary=summaries.get(name),
            title=panel_title,
        )

    return facet(names, draw, ncols=ncols, width=width, panel_aspect=panel_aspect, titles=titles)

def precision_recall(
    curves: Mapping[str, tuple[ArrayLike, ArrayLike]],
    *,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    colors: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    markers: str | Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    iso_f1: Sequence[float] | None = (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8),
    diagonal: float | None = None,
    xlabel: str = "Recall",
    ylabel: str = "Precision",
    title: str = "",
    legend: bool = True,
    marker_size: float = 5.0,
    width: float | str = "half",
) -> Axes:
    """Draw a precision-recall diagram for one or more models.

    Args:
        curves: ``{name: (recall, precision)}``. Arrays draw a curve swept over a
            threshold (sorted by recall); scalars draw a single operating point.
        ax: Axes to draw on; a new square figure is created when ``None``.
        colors: ``{name: colour}``; defaults to the theme's qualitative palette.
        markers: ``{name: marker}``, or one marker for all entries. Points default
            to ``"o"``; curves have no markers unless given.
        iso_f1: F1 values drawn as dotted iso-F1 reference curves; ``None`` or
            ``()`` omits them.
        diagonal: Precision of a dashed "no skill" line (e.g. the class
            prevalence); ``None`` omits it.
        xlabel: x-axis label.
        ylabel: y-axis label.
        title: Axes title.
        legend: Draw a legend.
        marker_size: Operating-point marker size in points.
        width: Figure width in inches or a :data:`nicefigs.figure.WIDTHS` name,
            used only when a new figure is created.

    Returns:
        The axes.
    """
    th = get_theme()
    names = list(curves)
    cols = colors or dict(zip(names, qualitative(len(names))))

    if ax is None:
        from .figure import subplots

        _, ax = subplots(width=width, aspect=1.0)

    if iso_f1:
        rr = np.linspace(1e-3, 1.0, 200)
        for f in iso_f1:
            with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
                pp = f * rr / (2 * rr - f)
            valid = np.isfinite(pp) & (pp > 0) & (pp <= 1.0)
            if valid.sum() > 1:
                ax.plot(rr[valid], pp[valid], color="#cccccc", lw=0.6, ls=":", zorder=0)
                xi, yi = rr[valid][-1], pp[valid][-1]
                ax.annotate(
                    f"F1={f:g}",
                    (xi, yi),
                    fontsize=max(th.fs_annot - 0.5, 4.0),
                    color="#999999",
                    xytext=(-2, 2),
                    textcoords="offset points",
                    ha="right",
                    va="bottom",
                )

    if diagonal is not None:
        ax.axhline(float(diagonal), color=COLORS["neutral"], ls="--", lw=0.7, zorder=1, label="no skill")

    for name in names:
        r, p = curves[name]
        r = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(r, dtype=float))
        p = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(p, dtype=float))
        mk = markers.get(name) if isinstance(markers, dict) else markers
        if r.size == 1:
            ax.plot(
                r,
                p,
                marker=mk or "o",
                color=cols[name],
                markersize=marker_size,
                linestyle="none",
                zorder=5,
                label=name,
            )
        else:
            order = np.argsort(r)
            ax.plot(
                r[order],
                p[order],
                color=cols[name],
                lw=th.lw_line,
                marker=mk,
                markersize=3.5 if mk else 0,
                zorder=4,
                label=name,
            )

    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    if title:
        from .panels import clean_title

        clean_title(ax, title)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.15, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    if legend:
        ax.legend(loc="best", fontsize=th.fs_legend)
    return ax

def normalize01(
    values: ArrayLike, *, method: Literal["quantile", "linear"] = "quantile", clip: bool = True
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, tuple[float, float]]:
    """Scale values into ``[0, 1]`` for use with a 2D colormap.

    Args:
        values: Values of any shape; NaNs are ignored when choosing the range.
        method: ``"quantile"`` maps the 5th/95th percentiles to 0/1, ``"linear"``
            the minimum/maximum.
        clip: Clip the scaled values to ``[0, 1]``.

    Returns:
        ``(scaled, (lo, hi))``: the scaled array (same shape as ``values``) and the
        data range mapped to 0 and 1, for legend tick labels.
    """
    arr = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    finite = arr[np.isfinite(arr)]
    if finite.size == 0:
        return np.zeros_like(arr), (0.0, 1.0)
    if method == "quantile":
        lo, hi = float(np.nanpercentile(arr, 5)), float(np.nanpercentile(arr, 95))
    else:
        lo, hi = float(np.nanmin(arr)), float(np.nanmax(arr))
    if hi <= lo:
        hi = lo + 1.0
    scaled = (arr - lo) / (hi - lo)
    return (np.clip(scaled, 0, 1) if clip else scaled), (lo, hi)

def bivariate_cmap(
    x: ArrayLike, y: ArrayLike, *, corners: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, clip: bool = True
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Colour ``(x, y)`` pairs by bilinear blending of four corner colours.

    Args:
        x: First variable, scaled to ``[0, 1]``.
        y: Second variable, scaled to ``[0, 1]``; same shape as ``x``.
        corners: Colours keyed ``"ll"``, ``"hl"``, ``"lh"``, ``"hh"`` (x-low/high,
            y-low/high). Defaults to :data:`BIVARIATE_CORNERS`.
        clip: Clip ``x`` and ``y`` to ``[0, 1]`` first.

    Returns:
        RGB array of shape ``x.shape + (3,)`` in ``[0, 1]``.
    """
    xs = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    ys = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    if clip:
        xs, ys = np.clip(xs, 0, 1), np.clip(ys, 0, 1)
    c = {k: np.asarray(mcolors.to_rgb(v)) for k, v in (corners or BIVARIATE_CORNERS).items()}
    w_ll = (1 - xs) * (1 - ys)
    w_hl = xs * (1 - ys)
    w_lh = (1 - xs) * ys
    w_hh = xs * ys
    rgb = (
        w_ll[..., None] * c["ll"]
        + w_hl[..., None] * c["hl"]
        + w_lh[..., None] * c["lh"]
        + w_hh[..., None] * c["hh"]
    )
    return np.clip(rgb, 0, 1)

def hsv_cmap(
    hue: ArrayLike,
    sat: ArrayLike,
    *,
    value: float = 0.88,
    sat_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.5, 1.0),
    hue_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.55, 1.0),
    clip: bool = True,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Colour pairs by hue along one variable and saturation along the other.

    Args:
        hue: Variable mapped to hue, scaled to ``[0, 1]``.
        sat: Variable mapped to saturation, scaled to ``[0, 1]``; same shape as ``hue``.
        value: Fixed HSV value (brightness) in ``[0, 1]``.
        sat_range: Saturation at ``sat`` = 0 and 1.
        hue_range: Hue (fraction of the colour wheel) at ``hue`` = 0 and 1.
        clip: Clip ``hue`` and ``sat`` to ``[0, 1]`` first.

    Returns:
        RGB array of shape ``hue.shape + (3,)`` in ``[0, 1]``.
    """
    hs = np.asarray(hue, dtype=float)
    ss = np.asarray(sat, dtype=float)
    if clip:
        hs, ss = np.clip(hs, 0, 1), np.clip(ss, 0, 1)
    h = hue_range[0] + hs * (hue_range[1] - hue_range[0])
    s = sat_range[0] + ss * (sat_range[1] - sat_range[0])
    v = np.full_like(h, value, dtype=float)
    return mcolors.hsv_to_rgb(np.stack([h, s, v], axis=-1))

def flat_cmap(
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    *,
    L: float = 95.0,
    chroma: float = 33.0,
    rotation_deg: float = 0.0,
    transpose: bool = False,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Colour pairs on a constant-lightness CIE-Lab plane.

    ``x`` maps to a* (green to red) and ``y`` to b* (blue to yellow), so every
    colour has the same perceived lightness.

    Args:
        x: First variable, scaled to ``[0, 1]`` (clipped).
        y: Second variable, scaled to ``[0, 1]`` (clipped); same shape as ``x``.
        L: CIE-Lab lightness (0-100).
        chroma: Maximum a*/b* magnitude; larger is more saturated.
        rotation_deg: Rotation of the a*/b* plane in degrees.
        transpose: Swap the roles of ``x`` and ``y``.

    Returns:
        ``float32`` RGB array of shape ``x.shape + (3,)`` in ``[0, 1]``.
    """
    x = np.clip(np.asarray(x, dtype=float), 0, 1)
    y = np.clip(np.asarray(y, dtype=float), 0, 1)
    if transpose:
        x, y = y, x
    a = chroma * (2 * x - 1)
    b = chroma * (2 * y - 1)
    if rotation_deg:
        th = np.deg2rad(rotation_deg)
        ca, sa = np.cos(th), np.sin(th)
        a, b = a * ca - b * sa, a * sa + b * ca
    lab = np.stack([np.full_like(a, L), a, b], axis=-1)
    return _lab_to_srgb(lab).astype(np.float32)

def light_cmap(color: ColorType, name: str = "light") -> mcolors.LinearSegmentedColormap:
    """Single-hue sequential colormap from white through ``color`` to a darker ``color``.

    Suited to density backgrounds (KDEs, hexbins).

    Args:
        color: Any matplotlib colour.
        name: Name of the colormap.
    """
    r, g, b = mcolors.to_rgb(color)
    h, li, s = colorsys.rgb_to_hls(r, g, b)
    dark = colorsys.hls_to_rgb(h, max(li * 0.55, 0.0), s)
    return mcolors.LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(name, ["#ffffff", color, dark])

def artist_palette(name: str, n: int | None = None, *, reverse: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    """Colours of the artist palette ``name``.

    Args:
        name: A key of :data:`ARTIST_PALETTES`, case-insensitive.
        n: Number of colours; the palette repeats if ``n`` exceeds its length.
            ``None`` returns the whole palette.
        reverse: Reverse the order before selecting.

    Returns:
        Hex colour strings.

    Raises:
        KeyError: Unknown palette.
    """
    try:
        cols = list(ARTIST_PALETTES[name.lower()])
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise KeyError(f"Unknown artist palette {name!r}. Available: {sorted(ARTIST_PALETTES)}") from exc
    if reverse:
        cols = cols[::-1]
    if n is None:
        return cols
    if n <= len(cols):
        return cols[:n]
    return [cols[i % len(cols)] for i in range(n)]

def artist_cmap(name: str, *, reverse: bool = False) -> mcolors.LinearSegmentedColormap:
    """Smooth colormap interpolating an artist palette's colours.

    ``"hockney_canyon"`` uses :data:`HOCKNEY_CANYON_SEQ`; other palettes
    interpolate their colours in order.

    Args:
        name: A key of :data:`ARTIST_PALETTES`, case-insensitive.
        reverse: Reverse the colour order.

    Raises:
        KeyError: Unknown palette.
    """
    key = name.lower()
    stops = _CONTINUOUS.get(key) or ARTIST_PALETTES.get(key)
    if stops is None:
        raise KeyError(f"Unknown artist palette {name!r}. Available: {sorted(ARTIST_PALETTES)}")
    if reverse:
        stops = list(stops)[::-1]
    return mcolors.LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(key, list(stops))

Animations of map and image sequences, saved as MP4 (ffmpeg) or GIF (pillow).

:func:animate_maps builds an in-process :class:~matplotlib.animation.FuncAnimation over a (T, H, W) stack with one fixed colour scale; save it with :func:save_animation. :func:render_animation instead draws each frame with a draw(i) -> Figure callback, optionally across processes, and stitches the frames with :func:stitch_frames; use it for expensive or multi-panel frames.

def animate_maps(
    lon: ArrayLike,
    lat: ArrayLike,
    frames: ArrayLike,
    *,
    cmap: str = "inferno",
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    robust: bool = True,
    diverging: bool = False,
    projection: str = "robinson",
    antarctica_cutoff: bool = True,
    extent: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    land: bool = True,
    coastline: bool = True,
    titles: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    suptitle: str = "",
    colorbar_label: str = "",
    fps: float = 8,
    width: str | float = "half",
    aspect: float = 0.62,
    as_map: bool = True,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes, FuncAnimation]:
    """Animate a ``(T, H, W)`` stack of gridded fields with one fixed colour scale.

    Args:
        lon: Longitudes in degrees east, 1-D ``(W,)`` or 2-D ``(H, W)``.
        lat: Latitudes in degrees north, 1-D ``(H,)`` or 2-D ``(H, W)``.
        frames: Field stack of shape ``(T, H, W)``.
        cmap: Colormap name; ``"inferno"`` becomes ``"RdBu_r"`` when ``diverging``.
        vmin: Lower colour limit; computed over all frames if ``None``.
        vmax: Upper colour limit; computed over all frames if ``None``.
        robust: Use the 2nd/98th percentiles rather than min/max for missing limits.
        diverging: Use limits symmetric about zero and a diverging colormap.
        projection: Map projection name, as in :func:`nicefigs.make_map_axes`.
        antarctica_cutoff: Crop the southern edge when ``extent`` is ``None``.
        extent: ``(lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max)`` in degrees.
        land: Draw the land background.
        coastline: Draw coastlines.
        titles: Per-frame titles (e.g. dates), one per frame.
        suptitle: Figure title, constant across frames.
        colorbar_label: Colorbar label.
        fps: Playback rate in frames per second.
        width: Figure width, a named width or inches (see :func:`nicefigs.figure_size`).
        aspect: Figure height / width.
        as_map: Draw on projected map axes; ``False`` draws a plain image.

    Returns:
        ``(fig, ax, anim)``; keep a reference to ``anim`` until it is saved.
    """
    from matplotlib.animation import FuncAnimation

    th = get_theme()
    frames = np.asarray(frames, dtype=float)
    if cmap == "inferno" and diverging:
        cmap = "RdBu_r"
    if vmin is None or vmax is None:
        if diverging:
            from .palettes import symmetric_limits

            lo, hi = symmetric_limits(frames)
        elif robust:
            lo, hi = robust_limits(frames)
        else:
            lo, hi = float(np.nanmin(frames)), float(np.nanmax(frames))
        vmin = lo if vmin is None else vmin
        vmax = hi if vmax is None else vmax

    from .figure import figure_size

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=figure_size(width, aspect=aspect), dpi=th.dpi)

    lon = np.asarray(lon)
    lat = np.asarray(lat)

    if as_map:
        from .maps import _apply_extent, draw_background, make_map_axes

        ax, ccrs = make_map_axes(fig, 111, projection=projection)
        draw_background(ax, ccrs, land=land, coastline=coastline)
        _apply_extent(ax, ccrs, extent, antarctica_cutoff and extent is None)
        tkw = {"transform": ccrs.PlateCarree()} if ccrs is not None else {}
        mesh = ax.pcolormesh(
            lon, lat, frames[0], cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, shading="nearest", **tkw
        )
        is_mesh = True
    else:
        ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
        ax.set_xticks([])
        ax.set_yticks([])
        mesh = ax.imshow(frames[0], cmap=resolve_cmap(cmap), vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, animated=True)
        is_mesh = False

    from .colorbars import colorbar

    colorbar(mesh, ax, label=colorbar_label)
    ttl = ax.set_title(titles[0] if titles else "", fontsize=th.fs_title, loc="left", pad=3)
    if suptitle:
        fig.suptitle(suptitle, fontsize=th.fs_title)

    def update(i: int) -> tuple:
        if is_mesh:
            mesh.set_array(frames[i].ravel())
        else:
            mesh.set_data(frames[i])
        if titles:
            ttl.set_text(titles[i])
        return (mesh, ttl)

    anim = FuncAnimation(fig, update, frames=len(frames), interval=1000 / fps, blit=False)
    return fig, ax, anim

    Args:
        anim: Animation to save, e.g. from :func:`animate_maps`.
        path: Output path; parent directories are created.
        fps: Frames per second.
        dpi: Resolution in dots per inch.

    Returns:
        The path written; a ``.gif`` next to ``path`` if ffmpeg is unavailable or fails.
    """
    p = Path(path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if p.suffix.lower() == ".gif":
        from matplotlib.animation import PillowWriter

        anim.save(str(p), writer=PillowWriter(fps=fps), dpi=dpi)
    else:
        try:
            from matplotlib.animation import FFMpegWriter

            anim.save(str(p), writer=FFMpegWriter(fps=fps, bitrate=2400), dpi=dpi)
        except (OSError, RuntimeError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            gif = p.with_suffix(".gif")
            from matplotlib.animation import PillowWriter

            anim.save(str(gif), writer=PillowWriter(fps=fps), dpi=dpi)
            return gif
    return p

def stitch_frames(
    frame_dir: str | os.PathLike,
    path: str | os.PathLike,
    *,
    fps: float = 8,
    pattern: str = "frame_%06d.png",
    crf: int = 18,
    preset: str = "medium",
) -> Path:
    """Stitch a directory of PNG frames into an MP4 (ffmpeg) or GIF (pillow).

    An ``.mp4`` target is encoded with ffmpeg (libx264, yuv420p, padded to even
    dimensions); any other suffix, or a missing or failing ffmpeg, produces a GIF.

    Args:
        frame_dir: Directory holding frames named per ``pattern``.
        path: Output path; parent directories are created.
        fps: Frames per second.
        pattern: ``printf``-style frame filename with one integer field.
        crf: ffmpeg constant rate factor; lower is higher quality.
        preset: ffmpeg x264 speed preset.

    Returns:
        The path written; its suffix is ``.gif`` on the GIF fallback.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: No frames match ``pattern`` (GIF path).
    """
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if path.suffix.lower() == ".mp4":
        try:
            subprocess.run(
                [
                    "ffmpeg",
                    "-y",
                    "-framerate",
                    str(fps),
                    "-i",
                    os.path.join(str(frame_dir), pattern),
                    "-vf",
                    "pad=ceil(iw/2)*2:ceil(ih/2)*2",
                    "-c:v",
                    "libx264",
                    "-pix_fmt",
                    "yuv420p",
                    "-preset",
                    preset,
                    "-crf",
                    str(crf),
                    str(path),
                ],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                check=True,
            )
            return path
        except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            path = path.with_suffix(".gif")
    return _stitch_gif(frame_dir, path, fps=fps, pattern=pattern)

def render_animation(
    draw: Callable[[int], Figure],
    n_frames: int,
    path: str | os.PathLike,
    *,
    fps: float = 8,
    dpi: float = 120,
    max_workers: int | None = None,
    method: Literal["parallel", "sequential"] = "parallel",
    pattern: str = "frame_%06d.png",
    crf: int = 18,
    preset: str = "medium",
) -> Path:
    """Render frames with a ``draw(i) -> Figure`` callback and stitch them into a video.

    Each returned figure is saved and closed, then all frames are stitched with
    :func:`stitch_frames`. Unlike :func:`animate_maps`, a frame may contain anything.

    Args:
        draw: Callable returning the figure for frame ``i``. With
            ``method="parallel"`` it must be picklable: a module-level function or
            a :func:`functools.partial` of one, not a lambda or closure.
        n_frames: Number of frames.
        path: Output path (``.mp4`` preferred, GIF fallback).
        fps: Frames per second.
        dpi: Frame resolution in dots per inch.
        max_workers: Process cap for ``"parallel"``; default ``min(n_frames, cpus, 8)``.
        method: ``"parallel"`` renders in a process pool, ``"sequential"`` in-process.
        pattern: ``printf``-style frame filename, as in :func:`stitch_frames`.
        crf: ffmpeg constant rate factor, as in :func:`stitch_frames`.
        preset: ffmpeg x264 preset, as in :func:`stitch_frames`.

    Returns:
        The path written, as returned by :func:`stitch_frames`.
    """
    import tempfile

    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="nicefigs_anim_") as td:
        if method == "parallel" and n_frames > 1:
            from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

            mw = max_workers or min(n_frames, (os.cpu_count() or 4), 8)
            with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=mw) as ex:
                futures = [
                    ex.submit(_render_one, draw, i, os.path.join(td, pattern % i), dpi, True)
                    for i in range(n_frames)
                ]
                for f in futures:
                    f.result()
        else:
            for i in range(n_frames):
                _render_one(draw, i, os.path.join(td, pattern % i), dpi, False)
        return stitch_frames(td, path, fps=fps, pattern=pattern, crf=crf, preset=preset)
